4VMmxO5eLl.one_liner: Version-space analysis of Scattered Forest Search showing it behaves like iterating repair instructions (IRRI) rather than sequential refinement (Line).
4VMmxO5eLl.problem: SFS combines MCTS, seeded initial programs, and text-based optimization, and the effect of each component on multi-turn program correction is not understood.
4VMmxO5eLl.method: Introduces Line (sequential self-refinement of one program, in depth) and IRRI (Iterative Refinement of Repair Instructions with fixed initial programs, in width), analyzes both with version spaces, and positions SFS as an intermediate method between them.
4VMmxO5eLl.key_idea: Model refinement as shrinking a version space, contrasting depth-wise program refinement (Line) with width-wise repair-instruction refinement (IRRI) to place SFS between them.
4VMmxO5eLl.evidence: Theoretical analysis in learning-theory terms plus experiments on program-correction datasets (including MBPP per reviews) examining at what depth the first correct program appears.
4VMmxO5eLl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is useful to ask which components of inference-scaling methods drive gains, and that combining version-space theory with a depth-of-first-success analysis gives concrete evidence for a simpler approach.
4VMmxO5eLl.main_concern: The theory rests on debatable assumptions (for example, self-generated tests never rejecting a correct solution) and probability arguments that factor over adaptive events without justification.

FnLrtORsmo.one_liner: Autoregressive time series pretraining that samples a dynamic prediction horizon per token, predicting long futures in one decoding step
FnLrtORsmo.problem: Next-token prediction gives only local supervision and error accumulation, while fixed-horizon next-N-token prediction introduces a horizon bias that may hinder generalization across forecasting horizons.
FnLrtORsmo.method: NxTP reformulates autoregressive pretraining so the prediction horizon is dynamically sampled for each token based on the available context, letting models predict long future sequences in a single decoding step with fewer autoregressive rollouts; reviewers state it uses a log-uniform horizon distribution.
FnLrtORsmo.key_idea: Sample the prediction horizon per token from a log-uniform distribution during pretraining instead of using a fixed horizon.
FnLrtORsmo.evidence: Experiments on two benchmarks (long-term forecasting and GIFT-Eval per reviewers) across six decoder-only backbones, plus a theoretical analysis (Theorem 2) of horizon-distribution matching.
FnLrtORsmo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the horizon-sampling idea simple and broadly applicable, reducing horizon-specific bias and rollout cost, with consistent gains across six backbones.
FnLrtORsmo.main_concern: The theory relies on strong assumptions and is not tied to the log-uniform horizon distribution, and generalization to arbitrary horizons is tested only on a fixed set (96, 192, 336, 720).

EAhhvhCKgs.one_liner: Aligns safety across recurrent depths of looped LMs with depth-specific control, state bridging and joint multi-depth safety supervision.
EAhhvhCKgs.problem: Safety in looped language models varies across recurrent depths: attack success can rise at deeper depths, jailbreaks transfer across depths, and SFT and preference alignment do not close these gaps.
EAhhvhCKgs.method: SafeBridge combines lightweight depth-specific control of shared recurrent layers, selective state bridging, and joint safety supervision across recurrent depths.
EAhhvhCKgs.key_idea: Jointly train depth-indexed safety policies over shared recurrent layers, using depth-specific modulation and bridging of states between depths to curb cross-depth jailbreak transfer.
EAhhvhCKgs.evidence: Jailbreak evaluation of Ouro looped models (two scales per reviews) with several attack methods under matched-depth and cross-depth settings, against SFT, DPO and LoopDPO baselines.
EAhhvhCKgs.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a review cites overall attack success falling from 21.06% (DPO) to 4.56% on Ouro-1.4B and from 44.93% to 9.85% on Ouro-2.6B.
EAhhvhCKgs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-depth safety evaluation (attack source depth versus inference depth) is a timely, useful framing and that SafeBridge gives large reductions in attack success.
EAhhvhCKgs.main_concern: Attack sets are fixed and reused across checkpoints, so defended models face transfer attacks rather than adaptive ones, which undermines the robustness claims.

ua10RlW7vr.one_liner: Autoregressive B-rep generator with a face-by-face frontier grammar that guarantees every finished sequence is a closed shell.
ua10RlW7vr.problem: B-rep generators can only check solid closure after generation, so many outputs are unusable downstream.
ua10RlW7vr.method: GrowBrep serializes a solid as a shell growing one face at a time along a frontier of open edges, each edge introduced once and closed once by a second half-edge, and the sequence cannot end while any edge is open. Geometry enters through per-primitive autoencoders with finite scalar quantization, and a decoder-only transformer (optionally conditioned on a point cloud) generates the sequence with illegal tokens masked at every step.
ua10RlW7vr.key_idea: Make closure a property of the sequence grammar by tracking a frontier of open edges and masking tokens that would leave an edge unclosed or reintroduce one.
ua10RlW7vr.evidence: ABC-1M, with one strict validity checker applied to every attempt of every method without rejection sampling; unconditional and point-cloud-conditioned generation (the rest of the abstract is cut off).
ua10RlW7vr.claimed_gains: 81.7% of generation attempts yield valid watertight solids on ABC-1M, versus 49.0% for the strongest baseline.
ua10RlW7vr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the grammar gives a closure guarantee by construction rather than by post-processing, and results show clearly higher validity under a strict common checker.
ua10RlW7vr.main_concern: Comparisons omit several recent B-Rep generators and program-based CAD methods, and one reviewer finds no controlled ablation isolating the grammar's contribution.

Qju89AVNrj.one_liner: Trains a tiny residual policy with safety-aware GRPO on a frozen VLA, adjusting actions before control-barrier-function safety filtering.
Qju89AVNrj.problem: Execution-time safety filters block unsafe actions but do not teach a VLA policy to avoid repeated interventions, while end-to-end RL on billions of parameters is costly.
Qju89AVNrj.method: VLSA-RL freezes the VLA backbone and learns a 1.3M-parameter residual policy (0.037% of pi_0.5) that adjusts actions before CBF safety filtering. A safety-aware GRPO objective uses feedback from the CBF quadratic program, risk-dependent clipping, and task and safety rewards.
Qju89AVNrj.key_idea: Optimize a small residual policy with GRPO whose objective uses the CBF quadratic program's correction as a feedback signal, so the policy learns to need fewer filter interventions.
Qju89AVNrj.evidence: SafeLIBERO at two safety levels against the CBF-filtered AEGIS baseline, plus an analysis of how residual actions compensate for dynamics mismatch and modulate CBF convergence.
Qju89AVNrj.claimed_gains: 68.0% average safe-success rate across two safety levels on SafeLIBERO, 21.4 and 22.9 percentage points above CBF-filtered AEGIS on Levels I and II, with shorter average episodes.
Qju89AVNrj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the lightweight residual-on-frozen-VLA design well motivated and the safe-success gains over AEGIS large and consistent across suites and levels.
Qju89AVNrj.main_concern: Missing ablations (plain residual RL, evaluation without the CBF-QP, intervention rates) and possible train/eval episode overlap leave the adaptation claim untested, and novelty is seen as incremental.

kTIIWIAE5m.one_liner: Goal-conditioned RL policy for high-precision inverse kinematics that accumulates joint-reference offsets and uses two-scale pose errors and dwell rewards.
kTIIWIAE5m.problem: Precise IK is laborious because of redundancy, singularities, hand-tuned controllers and costly physical-robot training data.
kTIIWIAE5m.method: PolicyIK updates joint-position references from pose feedback and observes its accumulated reference relative to measured joints, uses two-scale pose errors with an error-dependent action gain, and adds progress and dwell rewards so it both reaches and stays within tolerance.
kTIIWIAE5m.key_idea: Observe the accumulated joint reference relative to measured joints so the policy retains the offset the position controller needs at rest, with dwell rewards for holding the pose.
kTIIWIAE5m.evidence: Simulated held-out tasks with PPO, training directly on a physical arm with an off-policy learner against four classic IK controllers, and simulated pick-and-place with a VLA.
kTIIWIAE5m.claimed_gains: A single PPO attempt keeps mean errors over the final second within 1mm and 0.2 degrees on 93.5% of held-out tasks, and a deployment protocol raises success to 98.9%.
kTIIWIAE5m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach reaches millimeter-level accuracy in simulation and on hardware, with thorough ablations (command-state feedback, dwell) and strong reproducibility material.
kTIIWIAE5m.main_concern: Hardware pose errors are not verified against ground truth, the reward has about ten terms with unclear sensitivity, and key details sit in the appendix, making the paper hard to follow.

ln32dm0b7b.one_liner: Benchmark of streaming evolving environments testing whether LLM agents learn hidden, changing policies from serving experience and outcome feedback.
ln32dm0b7b.problem: Agents need knowledge that is implicit, undisclosed and changing, while existing benchmarks give the target knowledge, assume static environments, or are limited in scale and diversity for continual adaptation.
ln32dm0b7b.method: They formalize an evolving-environment streaming dataset and build ServeLearnBench across retail support, banking and sales-pitch generation with 53 environment windows and 7,718 tasks, evaluating five learning harnesses on six models.
ln32dm0b7b.key_idea: Stream tasks whose hidden policies change, give only outcome feedback, and bracket each harness with Blind and Oracle references on held-out evaluation.
ln32dm0b7b.evidence: Five harnesses (RAG, Mem0, SkillOpt, Continual Harness, Prime) across six models, giving 28 model-harness pairs and 252 learning runs.
ln32dm0b7b.claimed_gains: No numeric gains; the abstract reports a substantial gap between task capability and learning from serving experience.
ln32dm0b7b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is well motivated and fills a gap, with a clear streaming protocol, Blind and Oracle references, and broad harness-by-model coverage.
ln32dm0b7b.main_concern: Each cell is a single run with no confidence intervals, and harnesses differ in runtime and information access, so rankings reflect whole systems rather than learning mechanisms.

loy5Am2TPj.one_liner: Jointly trains autoencoder and latent diffusion so diffusion gradients shape the latent space for peptide, antibody and small-molecule binder design.
loy5Am2TPj.problem: A frozen autoencoder is fit only to reconstruct complexes, so its latent space can reconstruct cleanly yet be hard for the diffusion model to occupy.
loy5Am2TPj.method: They formulate autoencoding and latent diffusion as one optimization problem, letting diffusion gradients flow into the autoencoder so the latent manifold is shaped by the generative objective while keeping the structural information needed for reconstruction; reviews say the framework builds on UniMoMo.
loy5Am2TPj.key_idea: Backpropagate the latent-diffusion loss into the autoencoder during joint training, replacing the frozen-latent boundary of two-stage pipelines.
loy5Am2TPj.evidence: Peptide, antibody and small-molecule benchmarks, including training all three modalities in one model, with ablations and latent-distribution analyses.
loy5Am2TPj.claimed_gains: Reports improved structural accuracy, physical plausibility and binding energy together on peptide, antibody and small-molecule benchmarks; no numbers appear in the abstract.
loy5Am2TPj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reconstruction-versus-generation mismatch is a relevant problem and the joint objective is simple, applicable across modalities and supported by detailed ablations.
loy5Am2TPj.main_concern: Novelty is incremental since joint encoder and latent-diffusion training was explored earlier and the framework builds on UniMoMo, and some gains are marginal (small-molecule score 11.53 to 11.57).

QlvNqskhdY.one_liner: Factorial over model precision and eviction-score source splits the quantization and KV-eviction interaction into selection and fragility terms
QlvNqskhdY.problem: Weight quantization and KV-cache eviction are evaluated separately with their losses assumed to add, which misses that the eviction scores come from the quantized model.
QlvNqskhdY.method: The compression square is a factorial over model precision and selection source, with two counterfactual transplant cells that exactly split the interaction into a selection (oracle) term and a fragility term. It is applied to 646k released per-item records on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-3B at 4k-32k context.
QlvNqskhdY.key_idea: Transplanting retained token sets between precision settings separates the cost of the quantized model's own selection from its greater sensitivity to the same eviction.
QlvNqskhdY.evidence: 646k per-item records on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-3B at 4k-32k context with SnapKV eviction, needle tasks, paired statistics, multiple-testing correction, and a score-only intervention.
QlvNqskhdY.claimed_gains: The deployed cell is significantly worse than additive in 71 of 143 identifiable SnapKV cells and sub-additive in 3, and two noisy RTN builds exceed the three shipped W4-g128 recipes in 32 of 33 matched conditions.
QlvNqskhdY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the transplant design is a useful diagnostic that separates changed token selection from sensitivity to eviction, backed by paired statistics and robustness checks.
QlvNqskhdY.main_concern: Reviewers say the strongest claims generalize beyond the evidence, since most positive results come from noisy RTN builds and the common W4-g128 effect is small and mostly not significant, and novelty over known non-additive compression errors is limited.

OSjVF63CMn.one_liner: Static benchmark with a 29,573-instance tool-ordered corpus and probe suite for continual fine-tuning of tool-calling agents under API changes.
OSjVF63CMn.problem: Deployed agents face evolving tool ecosystems (new tools, schema changes, modified parameters), but benchmarks assume static tools and do not separate retention, transfer, and interference.
OSjVF63CMn.method: CAFTBench pairs CAFT-30k, a tool-ordered corpus of 29,573 instances over more than 260 tools, with CAFT-Eval, a probe suite for single-tool routing, cross-stage composition, API upgrades, no-tool abstention, and structured-output robustness. Five metrics (HRF, CSCR, NTHI, TOI, SCR) separate retention, transfer, interference, over-reliance, and format degradation.
OSjVF63CMn.key_idea: Order tool-calling training data by tool stage and probe each failure mode with a dedicated metric, so retention, interference, and format collapse are measured separately.
OSjVF63CMn.evidence: Experiments with Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct comparing continual learning methods such as EWC-style regularization and semantic replay.
OSjVF63CMn.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract reports backbone-dependent trade-offs (EWC-style regularization helps stability and upgraded-API adaptation on Qwen) without numeric results.
OSjVF63CMn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a real gap with disentangled metrics and a useful failure taxonomy, and its static protocol and released code make it cheap to run.
OSjVF63CMn.main_concern: Results are single temperature-0 runs of two 8B backbones with no seeds or significance tests, and the paper does not show fine-tuning is needed compared with updating the schema in the prompt.

2ZGjeTYi0P.one_liner: Replaces the coarse-motion component of the flow-matching source noise with a command, so the flow learns only residual fine motion.
2ZGjeTYi0P.problem: Generative robot policies trained on few demonstrations only reproduce demonstrated routes and do not learn how the embodiment moves, so they are competent only along those routes.
2ZGjeTYi0P.method: An orthonormal basis for the coarse part of an action chunk gives a command; the initial Gaussian noise's component along that basis is replaced with the command, which stays constant along the training path and is absent from the regression target. A learned head predicts the command by default, a planner or operator can override it, and a scalar input modulates adherence at inference.
2ZGjeTYi0P.key_idea: Encode coarse intent in the source distribution by swapping the noise's coarse-basis component for the command, leaving the flow to regress only the residual.
2ZGjeTYi0P.evidence: A quadrotor platform on gate navigation and out-of-distribution maneuvers in simulation and on a physical quadrotor, compared with a pi0 baseline and a velocity-projection baseline per reviews.
2ZGjeTYi0P.claimed_gains: On the demonstrated tasks, success in simulation improves from 45% to 73% where the images differ from those seen in training.
2ZGjeTYi0P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation separating where to go from how to move is intuitive and easy to follow, and that success improves over the pi0 baseline under visual shift.
2ZGjeTYi0P.main_concern: Evaluation is limited: few trials (five real-world trials per task, no real-world baselines), one task family, and the advantage under imperfect guidance is shown on a single flawed sketch while velocity projection matches it on feasible routes.

UYTo08D2eN.one_liner: DCEmbed embeds ReLU surrogates via a shared difference-of-convex formulation and solves with penalty convex-concave iterations, avoiding activation binaries.
UYTo08D2eN.problem: Exact mixed-integer encodings of ReLU networks add many binary variables, making optimization with embedded neural surrogates prohibitively costly at scale.
UYTo08D2eN.method: A ReLU network's difference-of-convex representation shares structure so its convex components need only two linear inequalities and one continuous auxiliary variable per hidden neuron. The embedded problem is solved by an iterative penalty convex-concave procedure that approximates only the concave neural terms, keeping the original objective, constraints, and discrete decisions exact.
UYTo08D2eN.key_idea: Share hidden-neuron epigraph variables across the convex parts of the DC decomposition, then linearize only concave neural terms in a penalty convex-concave loop.
UYTo08D2eN.evidence: Experiments against exact mixed-integer formulations and a continuous heuristic baseline, with a two-path ablation and an analysis that sharing variables adds no relaxation to the convex-concave subproblem.
UYTo08D2eN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared-epigraph formulation yields a simple procedure that is substantially more efficient than the compared exact approaches on the reported experiments, and that the paper is clear and well organized.
UYTo08D2eN.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (it combines existing difference-of-convex decompositions of networks with the standard convex-concave procedure), the application of the procedure to the original problem is under-specified, and baselines are narrow with no DC-based related methods compared.

iSO6eRGxSg.one_liner: Nested sparsity transformer where one column routing selects attention parameters and visible context, nesting with MoE expert sparsity.
iSO6eRGxSg.problem: MoE transformers apply conditional computation only in the MLP operator, so attention has no comparable sparsity mechanism that nests with it.
iSO6eRGxSg.method: Nestor adds a conditional-computation mechanism that generalizes the attention operator, where column routing simultaneously determines the attention parameters used by tokens and the context they can see. This sparsity hierarchically nests with MoE expert routing.
iSO6eRGxSg.key_idea: Route each token to a column that selects both its attention parameters and its visible context, with MoE experts nested inside the column's routing hierarchy.
iSO6eRGxSg.evidence: Language-model pretraining at four model scales against a conventional MoE at equal compute and sparsity, continual pretraining for longer contexts and new domains, and ablations on expert granularity, evaluated by validation loss.
iSO6eRGxSg.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims better pretraining loss than MoE at equal compute and sparsity and better long-context and domain adaptation, without numbers).
iSO6eRGxSg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the nested design is well motivated and clearly presented, and that Nestor beats MoE baselines in pretraining and continual pretraining settings.
iSO6eRGxSg.main_concern: The evaluation lacks closely related sparse-attention baselines and downstream benchmarks, and the two forms of attention sparsity are not isolated in ablations.

TvIxv9gDKE.one_liner: Self-Step Rejection trains a LoRA acceptance gate on a frozen model to reject its own low-recoverability reasoning steps.
TvIxv9gDKE.problem: Verifier-guided decoding usually needs an external learned verifier, and step-level recoverability changes are too noisy to resolve with practical Monte Carlo budgets.
TvIxv9gDKE.method: A LoRA gate on the frozen generator is trained with first-passage labels from a recoverability barrier, pointwise and same-prefix pairwise losses, then group-relative policy refinement; at inference it accepts or rejects sampled steps.
TvIxv9gDKE.key_idea: Label steps before the first resolved crossing of a root-relative recoverability barrier as accepted and the crossing step as rejected, then train a same-backbone gate.
TvIxv9gDKE.evidence: Diagnostic Monte Carlo measurements of recoverability, and accuracy and token-cost comparisons across three reasoning models; the abstract is cut off before results.
TvIxv9gDKE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the first-passage labeling is a principled design and that the frozen generator with a lightweight gate is practical and token-efficient.
TvIxv9gDKE.main_concern: The benefit of the labeling is not isolated from prior rollout-based labeling, and decoding closely follows earlier step-level verification work.

SNIGyRYB8i.one_liner: Joint-embedding world-action model that trains on future latent states but plans trajectories in one forward pass using V-JEPA features.
SNIGyRYB8i.problem: It is unclear which visual representations best support joint future-state and action learning, and how to keep the benefits of future supervision in a single-pass planner.
SNIGyRYB8i.method: JEWAM jointly learns future states and actions under a shared interface, compares ViT, MAE, CroCo v2, DINOv3, and V-JEPA features, and adopts V-JEPA. Future-state supervision is used in training only, with direct full-horizon prediction at deployment from front-view cameras.
SNIGyRYB8i.key_idea: Supervise on future latent states during training but predict full-horizon trajectories directly at inference, using V-JEPA features as the encoder.
SNIGyRYB8i.evidence: NAVSIM v2 NavTest and NavHard benchmarks, an encoder comparison under a shared interface, and ablations on future supervision and iterative variants.
SNIGyRYB8i.claimed_gains: JEWAM achieves 90.98 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 NavTest and 39.86 on NavHard using only front-view camera observations.
SNIGyRYB8i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning from future supervision while deploying a cheap single-pass planner is practically useful and that the controlled encoder study is valuable.
SNIGyRYB8i.main_concern: The encoder comparison confounds history features, future targets, and temporal tokenization, and novelty over Drive-JEPA, Latent-WAM, and Metis is unclear, with no closed-loop evaluation.

UcK90RZMcV.one_liner: Diagnoses writer-executor skill transfer failures (SkillDiag) and rewrites skills using executor failure feedback (SkillTutor).
UcK90RZMcV.problem: Language agents reuse skills written by other models, but stronger writers do not necessarily yield better execution, and task success alone does not explain why.
UcK90RZMcV.method: SkillDiag, based on an information-theoretic view of skill transfer, examines three failure sources: insufficient evidence in the original experience, information omitted during skill writing, and difficulty using information already in the skill. SkillTutor uses the executor's failure feedback to clarify and reorganize skill instructions.
UcK90RZMcV.key_idea: Attribute skill-transfer failures to evidence, writing, or usage gaps, then rewrite skills in response to the executor's own failure feedback.
UcK90RZMcV.evidence: Multiple language models across ALFWorld, WebShop and DAPO-Math, including common-source writer-executor matrices.
UcK90RZMcV.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that SkillTutor can improve skill use and task success.
UcK90RZMcV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experimental methodology is careful, with controlled common-source comparisons, repeated runs, and held-out selection, supporting that skill utility is executor-relative.
UcK90RZMcV.main_concern: The diagnostic scores are only indirectly validated and do not reliably select the right repair, and a teaching capsule built for a different executor performs about as well, weakening the executor-specific repair claim.

YtQjp0daE6.one_liner: Couples a DAG-based LLM-training performance estimator with an experience bank that distills estimator outputs into reusable deployment knowledge.
YtQjp0daE6.problem: Real-system observations for LLM parallel-training configurations are costly and sparse, and estimator solutions are hard to reuse as environments evolve.
YtQjp0daE6.method: Est2Exp's estimator uses a hybrid-granularity DAG for computation-communication dependencies and LLM-assisted calibration with limited real measurements to refine latency functions. The experience bank distills estimator outputs to warm-start later exploration and is refined jointly with the estimator as new measurements arrive.
YtQjp0daE6.key_idea: Bidirectional feedback between an LLM-calibrated DAG performance estimator and an experience bank that warm-starts exploration and is refined by new real-system measurements.
YtQjp0daE6.evidence: Per reviews, Ascend systems up to 16K accelerators with 30B-2K, 90B-6K and 505B-16K held out as extrapolation tests; the abstract is cut off before its results.
YtQjp0daE6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a well-motivated, practically valuable problem with an impressive large-scale evaluation and a promising reusable-knowledge idea.
YtQjp0daE6.main_concern: Gains over the initial estimator are unclear (DAG accuracy is already high and calibration sometimes lowers it), and the experience bank is not compared with simple reuse baselines or existing estimators.

xwnxpBcsr1.one_liner: Refines a frozen tabular foundation model's molecular predictions using a second TFM on molecule pairs and their prediction-error differences.
xwnxpBcsr1.problem: Tabular foundation models' in-context molecular property prediction under structural train-test shift is underexplored and lacks explicit molecular comparisons.
xwnxpBcsr1.method: In MolRIFT, one tabular foundation model makes an initial prediction from molecule-level context, and a second TFM uses molecular pairs and their prediction-error differences to refine it.
xwnxpBcsr1.key_idea: Feed pairwise molecule comparisons with prediction-error differences to a second frozen TFM as in-context residual correction of the first TFM's prediction.
xwnxpBcsr1.evidence: 58 MoleculeACE and Polaris tasks across four molecular representations and three TFM backbones; reviews also mention Lo-Hi and DrugOOD.
xwnxpBcsr1.claimed_gains: CheMeleon with TabPFN-3 wins a majority of tasks against each baseline, MolRIFT improves it on 46 of 58 tasks, and gains persist across four representations and three backbones.
xwnxpBcsr1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad (many tasks, representations and backbones) and the gains are consistent across them.
xwnxpBcsr1.main_concern: Native-metric gains are small (e.g., mean MoleculeACE RMSE 0.8932 to 0.8849) and not clearly separated from simpler residual baselines, while inference cost is large and the need for each component is not established.

Gnb9q66kfJ.one_liner: Decomposes learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian error in the reference eigenbasis to explain physics-informed losses and motivate a spectral-plus-density training signal.
Gnb9q66kfJ.problem: Entry-wise Hamiltonian accuracy does not guarantee accurate eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and existing physics-informed losses help only partially.
Gnb9q66kfJ.method: The prediction error is represented in the eigenbasis of the reference Hamiltonian, where it separates into sectors that each property and training signal reads selectively. This analysis motivates a Hamiltonian representation that sees every sector; reviews refer to cumulative LDOS as part of the proposed supervision.
Gnb9q66kfJ.key_idea: Express Hamiltonian prediction error in the reference eigenbasis so each loss can be audited by which error sectors it observes, then supervise all sectors.
Gnb9q66kfJ.evidence: Theoretical sector analysis plus fine-tuning experiments from shared starting checkpoints with matched protocols and element-wise-only continued-training controls, per reviews; models and datasets not visible in the abstract excerpt.
Gnb9q66kfJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the physical motivation is clear and the paper explains well why element-wise, density-only and wavefunction-alignment losses miss parts of the error.
Gnb9q66kfJ.main_concern: The relation to existing eigenvalue and real-/reciprocal-space objectives (NextHAM, Cignoni et al., Suman et al.) is not explained, and one reviewer calls the contribution incremental.

83BJcyLkqE.one_liner: HiLL recursively splits cell clusters using LLM split validation and comparative marker evidence for reference-free cell type annotation.
83BJcyLkqE.problem: Reference-free LLM annotation methods use a fixed clustering partition and conventional marker extraction, which limits adaptive subtype refinement and accurate annotation.
83BJcyLkqE.method: HiLL treats annotation as hierarchical refinement: an LLM validates whether each cluster should be split further, and comparative evidence across clusters supports the labels. Branches can stop at different depths.
83BJcyLkqE.key_idea: Recursively split clusters only when an LLM split validation approves, using sibling comparisons for split decisions and broader pairwise marker comparisons for labeling.
83BJcyLkqE.evidence: Human and mouse scRNA-seq and single-cell spatial transcriptomics datasets, with ablations of recursive refinement and marker extraction and a multi-resolution comparison.
83BJcyLkqE.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms reference-free LLM baselines, with especially strong gains on fine-grained subtypes (abstract text cuts off); no numbers stated.
83BJcyLkqE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated since cell populations need different annotation depths, no external reference is required, and ablations support recursive refinement and marker extraction.
83BJcyLkqE.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish correct fine-subtype recovery, since hierarchical matching credits any subtype of a coarse reference label, and the value of LLM-controlled granularity beyond extra LLM compute is unclear.

nGjdwrBva0.one_liner: Traces Muon's late-stage max attention-logit growth to BF16 FlashAttention numerical error, whose gradient errors become persistent rank-one.
nGjdwrBva0.problem: The origin of excess late-stage attention-logit growth in Muon training is unclear.
nGjdwrBva0.method: Compares attention implementations and numerical precisions, characterizes the resulting rank-one gradient errors, proves a two-stage logit growth for a retrieval task with additive rank-one errors, and mitigates growth by raising the precision of selected FlashAttention intermediate quantities.
nGjdwrBva0.key_idea: BF16 FlashAttention errors become stable, same-sign rank-one gradient errors that accumulate coherently into structured high-logit heads; raising precision of the responsible intermediates mitigates the growth.
nGjdwrBva0.evidence: Controlled comparisons of attention implementations and precisions, gradient-error measurements, a theorem on a retrieval task with additive rank-one errors, and interventions on FlashAttention intermediates.
nGjdwrBva0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical investigation is rigorous, linking precision choices to the logit dynamics through controlled comparisons and interventions, and that the practical mitigation is useful.
nGjdwrBva0.main_concern: The conceptual advance over closely related work on attention numerical error is limited, the explanation lacks null controls (such as AdamW or MATH32 versus MATH16 comparisons), and Theorem 1 rests on strong assumptions.

PlspL3L46i.one_liner: Proves unclipped population RLHF attains near-optimal distortion at every KL budget, without reward clipping.
PlspL3L46i.problem: The known finite-KL-budget linear-in-beta distortion guarantee relies on clipping the fitted reward, and the best known bound for the unclipped reward is quadratic in beta.
PlspL3L46i.method: Analyzes unclipped RLHF with the reward fitted to population comparisons and no distribution mismatch, comparing reward maximization with win-probability maximization inside the same KL ball.
PlspL3L46i.key_idea: Compare reward maximization against win-probability maximization inside the same KL ball, so the proof never bounds reward magnitudes and uses the reward only through the exponential tilt.
PlspL3L46i.evidence: A theorem bounding worst-case distortion, plus population simulations on MovieLens and KuaiRec.
PlspL3L46i.claimed_gains: Worst-case distortion is at most C_0 kappa(beta) at every KL budget, with C_0 < 2.526 and kappa(beta) = beta/[2 tanh(beta/2)], the known algorithm-independent lower bound.
PlspL3L46i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result gives a clean, optimal-order guarantee for the unclipped objective, closing a gap left by prior work, with a reusable technical idea.
PlspL3L46i.main_concern: The guarantee holds only in an idealized setting with exact population comparisons, no distribution mismatch, and no reward-fitting error, so it does not cover rewards estimated from finitely many comparisons.

ijzD68LDjM.one_liner: Chooses per-step payload size for multi-bit LLM watermarking by mutual information, approximated online from token entropy.
ijzD68LDjM.problem: Most multi-bit watermarking embeds a fixed number of message bits at every generation step, although the payload should adapt to maximize detectability.
ijzD68LDjM.method: They formulate per-step payload selection as mutual-information maximization, define MMIP (an oracle that exhaustively evaluates candidate payload sizes), and propose EWP, which derives the payload from entropy for efficient online allocation.
ijzD68LDjM.key_idea: Select the per-step payload that maximizes mutual information between message and sampled tokens, approximated online from token entropy.
ijzD68LDjM.evidence: The abstract is truncated; reviews indicate bit-accuracy and message-recovery evaluation against multi-bit baselines such as XMark, StealthInk and DepthW.
ijzD68LDjM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree fixed payload is a real weakness and that the mutual-information formulation is intuitive and well motivated.
ijzD68LDjM.main_concern: EWP's link to the MMIP optimum rests on an observed entropy correlation without direct evidence, and evaluation emphasizes bit accuracy over full message recovery.

AdnUNAPXDO.one_liner: Induces behavioral rubrics from an agent's own failures, repairs failed turns, and trains on repaired-versus-original preference pairs.
AdnUNAPXDO.problem: Expert-data training misses the states a learner reaches after its own mistakes, while terminal-reward RL visits them but needs full rollouts and cannot say which turn went wrong.
AdnUNAPXDO.method: RePair turns recurring errors into reusable rubrics (error pattern, correcting rule, criterion). When a rubric matches a failed turn, a repair model rewrites it and a validator checks it using only what the agent saw at that turn, and the rewrite and original response form a preference pair on the same input, so no rubric is needed at inference.
AdnUNAPXDO.key_idea: Rubric-guided single-turn repair, validated without rollouts, yields on-policy preference pairs for training.
AdnUNAPXDO.evidence: BrowseComp-Plus with Qwen3-14B and Gemma-4-12B-IT agents, four held-out multi-hop QA benchmarks, and self-repair experiments.
AdnUNAPXDO.claimed_gains: On BrowseComp-Plus, lifts a supervised Qwen3-14B search agent from 42.6% to 53.2% with 2,097 pairs and Gemma-4-12B-IT from 43.6% to 51.2%, gains 5.6 points on average on four held-out multi-hop QA benchmarks, and two rounds of self-repair gain 7.2 points.
AdnUNAPXDO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea clean and well motivated, with clear presentation and a thorough ablation battery.
AdnUNAPXDO.main_concern: Evidence is limited to one environment (BrowseComp-Plus) and one model family with single trials and few baselines, so generality is unproven.

4TpJXm9CNo.one_liner: Recurrent latent judgment state retrieves evidence from image-token memory to refine aesthetic scores without annotated reasoning text.
4TpJXm9CNo.problem: Image-rating pairs give judgment outcomes but not how evidence is integrated or revised, while direct MLLM scoring lacks explicit revision and verbalized reasoning needs reasoning-text targets and token-by-token decoding.
4TpJXm9CNo.method: After one multimodal encoding pass, an evolving judgment state repeatedly retrieves and integrates evidence from persistent image-token memory. Regression on human ratings trains the scorer, internal self-distillation aligns intermediate score readouts with the final prediction, and inference fuses the recurrent score with a parallel language-aligned rating estimate without decoding an explanation.
4TpJXm9CNo.key_idea: A recurrent latent state cross-attends over persistent image tokens, with intermediate score readouts self-distilled toward the final prediction instead of supervised by reasoning text.
4TpJXm9CNo.evidence: Experiments on holistic and aspect-specific aesthetic assessment benchmarks including AVA, AADB, and PARA, compared with methods such as ROC4MLLM per reviewers.
4TpJXm9CNo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree LAD avoids reasoning annotations and token-by-token decoding and shows strong benchmark results with a coherent design of persistent memory, recurrent retrieval, and self-distillation.
4TpJXm9CNo.main_concern: Reviewers say the deliberation framing exceeds the evidence: intermediate steps only match the final score, so the model may just perform iterative feature refinement, and ablations on latent-token count and dataset-level iteration benefits are missing.

rDapC2jWnc.one_liner: Video agent answers all questions about a video in one shared tool-use trajectory, trained with question-horizon policy optimization.
rDapC2jWnc.problem: Existing video agents handle each question in an isolated tool-use trajectory, repeatedly restarting video exploration and memory construction when a video has several questions.
rDapC2jWnc.method: VAMR uses a persistent policy that invokes tools for one or more unresolved questions per round and submits answers once evidence suffices, with question-conditioned visual perception and layered multi-question memory. After SFT, QHPO uses a question-level critic and round alignment to map each question's advantage to the rounds that serve it.
rDapC2jWnc.key_idea: One shared trajectory serves all questions, and RL assigns each question's critic-estimated advantage only to the rounds that directly serve it (round alignment).
rDapC2jWnc.evidence: Long-form video benchmarks (reviews mention LVBench) against independent baselines with matched training data, tools and budgets and against VideoARM, plus question-count and component experiments.
rDapC2jWnc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared multi-question trajectory addresses repeated video exploration and that QHPO's question-level advantage is a meaningful fine-grained credit assignment design, backed by strong controls.
rDapC2jWnc.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate the method: the direct baseline sees 32 frames versus 84.9 on average for VAMR, reproduced baselines are restricted to single-question interfaces, and shared memory is not separated from joint scheduling.

zOc3NBJKNk.one_liner: An LLM builds task-specific small models for root cause analysis, admitted only if measured training performance meets criteria.
zOc3NBJKNk.problem: RCA systems either rely on an LLM alone, which compares numbers unreliably across thousands of feature rows, or add ML pipelines that experts rebuild per system and whose rules are admitted without measuring firing rate or precision.
zOc3NBJKNk.method: HatchRCA has the LLM design task-specific small models for each new system and write and run their training programs. A generated model, rule or experience is admitted only when its performance measured on training cases meets admission criteria, and each admitted model attaches its measured accuracy to the candidates it proposes.
zOc3NBJKNk.key_idea: The LLM writes and trains small numeric models, and a host-side gate admits each model, rule or experience only if its measured training-case performance meets criteria.
zOc3NBJKNk.evidence: OpenRCA benchmark with the same backbone, scoring program and 87 test tasks as the official RCA-agent.
zOc3NBJKNk.claimed_gains: Raises the full-score rate from 29.9% to 55.2% and the partial rate (tasks with at least one correct field) from 49.4% to 79.3%.
zOc3NBJKNk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that having the LLM build numeric models with evidence-based admission and measured accuracy is a concrete idea, with strong OpenRCA gains under a matched-baseline comparison.
zOc3NBJKNk.main_concern: No ablation isolates the claimed mechanisms (disabling admission alone or swapping in conventional models), and the best configuration still relies on manually written prompts and rules.

TMQXORjxix.one_liner: Trains the solver to reject invalid questions and uses a frozen model's novelty judgments to sustain self-evolving reasoning.
TMQXORjxix.problem: Repeated self-training of reasoning models on self-generated questions collapses, because invalid questions grow (and answer-consistency filtering raises their share) and lexical-similarity diversity controls miss mathematically equivalent repeats.
TMQXORjxix.method: R-Quest first trains the solver to recognize and reject invalid questions, then uses its judgments to guide questioner rewards and filter solver training data. A frozen base model compares sampled question pairs to give novelty feedback against repetition.
TMQXORjxix.key_idea: Use a solver trained to detect invalid questions to shape questioner rewards and filter training data, plus frozen-model pairwise novelty feedback against mathematically equivalent repeats.
TMQXORjxix.evidence: 12 benchmarks across mathematical reasoning, general-domain reasoning and code generation with two model families, plus diagnostic experiments such as repairing invalid questions and comparisons with R-Zero and R-Diverse.
TMQXORjxix.claimed_gains: Consistently achieves the highest average performance on 12 benchmarks in mathematical reasoning, general-domain reasoning and code generation across two model families.
TMQXORjxix.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of self-evolution collapse is well motivated, notably that answer-consistency filtering raises the share of invalid questions, and that a repair experiment shows invalid questions hurt training.
TMQXORjxix.main_concern: The method depends on an external proprietary judge (GPT-5.6-Sol) for validity labels replayed every round, so it is unclear how much of the gain comes from that supervision rather than the online validity feedback.

BmVmnQXR1A.one_liner: Per-neuron null-space projector that removes only the old-token directions on which each ReLU neuron is active, to reduce fine-tuning forgetting.
BmVmnQXR1A.problem: Shared null-space projection (Adam-NSCL, GPM) removes the same dominant old-token directions from every neuron's update, yet in OPT-1.3b 96% of (token, neuron) pairs are inactive, so the constraint protects outputs that are already zero.
BmVmnQXR1A.method: For each neuron, the projector removes only the directions of old tokens on which that neuron is active. An exact decomposition splits the squared output change into three terms (tokens that stay active, switch off, switch on), and constraining active tokens removes the first two.
BmVmnQXR1A.key_idea: Constrain each ReLU neuron's update only on the old tokens where that neuron is active, leaving inactive tokens free, using an exact three-term decomposition of output change.
BmVmnQXR1A.evidence: OPT-1.3b compared with Adam-NSCL at six matched budgets of removed directions; reviews add three OPT sizes, WikiText-103 and Python code corpora, and selector controls (random, sign-blind, inactive-input).
BmVmnQXR1A.claimed_gains: Forgets less than Adam-NSCL at every matched budget on OPT-1.3b (TL;DR); no magnitudes are visible because the abstract is cut off.
BmVmnQXR1A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that restricting constraints to each neuron's active tokens is an intuitive, well-motivated relaxation of null-space projection, supported by an exact decomposition and informative selector controls.
BmVmnQXR1A.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow (three OPT sizes, two corpora, 128 training steps) and the theory covers ReLU-style hard gates but not GELU or SwiGLU.

51HIOBWD08.one_liner: PED corrects merged-model weights so confidence scores rank correct predictions above errors, protecting selected fitting predictions from class changes.
51HIOBWD08.problem: Model merging can leave a classifier's answers unchanged while making its errors harder to find by confidence, so high-confidence errors escape human review.
51HIOBWD08.method: A three-class linear example shows that averaging experts with different runner-up classes can make a shared error look more confident than a shared correct decision. PED learns a correction to the merged weights that scores correct predictions above errors while protecting selected correct fitting predictions against class changes, using 128 fitting and 128 selection labels per task.
51HIOBWD08.key_idea: Learn a correction to merged weights that raises confidence of correct over wrong predictions, with fitting-set constraints that keep selected correct fitting predictions from changing class.
51HIOBWD08.evidence: TIES-merged CLIP ViT-B/32 models; agreement-subset diagnosis on five eligible tasks and PED evaluation across eight tasks (reviews mention two CLIP backbones and two merging methods).
51HIOBWD08.claimed_gains: Experts reach 86.4% macro AUROC versus 69.2% for TIES on five eligible tasks; PED raises held-out AUROC from 84.7% to 88.2% and accuracy from 71.7% to 73.4% across eight tasks, bringing about eight additional errors into review per 100 images inspected at 5% review.
51HIOBWD08.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the agreement-subset evaluation and the three-class construction clearly show that confidence ranking can degrade even when predictions are unchanged, separating error detectability from accuracy.
51HIOBWD08.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate PED's components (margin constraints, acceptance procedure, AUROC eligibility gate), so gains are attributable only to the full procedure.

CjfiLD0imi.one_liner: MT-Tab adapts pretrained tabular foundation models to multi-target prediction by unfolding targets along the batch dimension and expanding prompts.
CjfiLD0imi.problem: Single-target tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL have inference cost that scales linearly with the number of targets and leave target dependencies out of the prediction path, while pretraining a joint model is expensive and complex.
CjfiLD0imi.method: Target unfolding places multi-target labels along the meta/batch dimension, passes them through the pretrained target encoder, and integrates them into the transformer input through prompt expansion. Reviewers note that adaptation uses LoRA fine-tuning on each downstream dataset; the abstract is cut off after this point.
CjfiLD0imi.key_idea: Unfold multi-target labels along the batch dimension and inject them into the pretrained transformer through prompt expansion, so one pass can use inter-target dependencies.
CjfiLD0imi.evidence: Comparisons with tabular foundation model and conventional baselines (including GBDTs) on several tabular datasets, with analyses of target correlation, target imbalance, few-shot performance and inference efficiency.
CjfiLD0imi.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off; a reviewer cites an 11.2x speedup over serial single-target inference, which drops to about 1.5x against batched inference at 32 targets).
CjfiLD0imi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, extending existing tabular foundation models to multi-target prediction via LoRA without pretraining from scratch and with inference-efficiency gains.
CjfiLD0imi.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the benefit of target dependencies (the permutation test also breaks the input-target mapping), and performance gains are narrow, leading on only 3 of 9 datasets in one table.

63b2JLGQOn.one_liner: CoRE alternately trains an RL rule-routing agent and a contrastive rule-constrained retriever from retrieval feedback, without query-rule labels.
63b2JLGQOn.problem: Structured knowledge retrieval methods are either unconstrained or depend on predefined query-rule supervision, which is rarely available in practice.
63b2JLGQOn.method: A routing agent assigns each query to a reasoning rule, and the corresponding retriever traverses the structured knowledge base and ranks evidence that satisfies the rule's constraints. Alternate optimization couples reinforcement learning for rule routing with contrastive learning for the retriever.
63b2JLGQOn.key_idea: Because routing and retrieval depend on each other, alternate RL updates of the router with contrastive updates of the rule-constrained retriever so each adapts to the other's retrieval feedback.
63b2JLGQOn.evidence: STaRK-QA datasets (Amazon, MAG and PRIME per reviewers) spanning scientific discovery, biomedical reasoning and e-commerce, with component ablations and a case study.
63b2JLGQOn.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off; a reviewer cites CoRE-BERT-C raising average H@1 over MoR from 48.93 to 54.47 and MRR from 58.77 to 65.97).
63b2JLGQOn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning rule routing without query-rule labels is well motivated and the co-adaptive design is conceptually clean, with strong results across the evaluated domains.
63b2JLGQOn.main_concern: The rule sets are predefined and small (6, 8 and 65 rules), with no study of rule quality or larger rule spaces, and the baseline comparison conflates component training with co-adaptation.

7QtQQi4vnK.one_liner: IMUHand is a bimanual IMU-glove dataset with MANO ground truth, plus a baseline using learned calibration and independent root orientation.
7QtQQi4vnK.problem: Sparse hand-mounted IMUs cannot directly recover full articulated hand pose and suffer orientation drift and placement variation, and large public datasets and standardized protocols for continuous IMU-only bimanual reconstruction are lacking.
7QtQQi4vnK.method: The authors build IMU gloves for synchronized acquisition and a benchmark with long continuous bimanual sequences, per-frame MANO ground truth, synchronized egocentric video and a unified IMU-only protocol. The baseline combines learned secondary calibration with independent root orientation estimation to recover wrist orientation and full hand pose from IMU sequences alone.
7QtQQi4vnK.key_idea: Combine a learned secondary calibration of IMU placement with separate root orientation estimation to reconstruct articulated hand pose from sparse IMUs alone.
7QtQQi4vnK.evidence: The new benchmark under a unified IMU-only evaluation protocol; the abstract is cut off before the results, and a reviewer describes an approximately 80/20 sequence split.
7QtQQi4vnK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset is a valuable multimodal resource (bimanual IMUs, egocentric video, MANO annotations) and the baseline is practical, needing few sensors and running in real time.
7QtQQi4vnK.main_concern: The benchmark's reliability and generalization are not established (the split does not state whether participants or donning sessions overlap), and the baseline omits global translation and relative bimanual positions, weakening the bimanual and hand-object claims.

huu1MTnczQ.one_liner: PhysicsLENS uses matched scenario pairs to test whether robot video generation models follow hidden physical properties.
huu1MTnczQ.problem: Video generation benchmarks exclude physics hidden by visuals (weight, viscosity, friction), so models are judged on the fidelity of physics rather than its underlying accuracy.
huu1MTnczQ.method: The dataset and benchmark use matched scenario pairs that hold the conditioning frame, task and scene description fixed. Scenarios are curated from public robot video sources and annotated across seven physical domains: collision, gravity, momentum, friction, deformation, fluid and causality.
huu1MTnczQ.key_idea: Pair scenarios that differ only in the stated physical property, so physical plausibility and property grounding can be scored separately.
huu1MTnczQ.evidence: Four video generation models with over 400 human-annotated labels.
huu1MTnczQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports a consistent accuracy gap between observable and unobservable conditions, without numbers).
huu1MTnczQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating physical plausibility from property grounding with matched prompts is well motivated and shows that plausible-looking videos often ignore the stated property.
huu1MTnczQ.main_concern: The evidence is thin: only four open-source models, one generation per prompt, a single annotation per clip without agreement measures, and a small hidden-property set, so the central gap is not statistically supported.

ga3Lctwzff.one_liner: DyCAST tokenizes speech at variable frame rate using soft character-level alignment and explicit duration modeling.
ga3Lctwzff.problem: Neural audio codecs typically use fixed frame rates, allocating tokens uniformly in time without adapting to the linguistic structure of speech.
ga3Lctwzff.method: DyCAST learns to associate tokens with character-level linguistic units during training, and supports alignment-free inference with direct control over token durations at decoding time.
ga3Lctwzff.key_idea: Learn soft alignment between speech tokens and characters plus an explicit duration model, so the frame rate follows linguistic content and can be set at decoding time.
ga3Lctwzff.evidence: Reconstruction quality and downstream tasks (resynthesis, voice conversion and TTS per reviewers) against fixed-rate codecs; reviewers note the variable-rate baselines are discussed but not compared experimentally.
ga3Lctwzff.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says competitive reconstruction quality and downstream performance, without numbers).
ga3Lctwzff.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses the practical problem of long speech token sequences, with a coherent framework combining learned boundaries and duration prediction and a broad evaluation.
ga3Lctwzff.main_concern: The core dynamic-rate contribution is not compared empirically against dynamic-rate baselines such as FlexiCodec and CodecSlime, and character alignment is not justified against phoneme or fixed segmentation.

ZhRgDvN6F3.one_liner: dOPT differentiates conic programs by reducing them at a primal-dual solution to an equality-constrained QP needing one symmetric linear solve.
ZhRgDvN6F3.problem: Training systems with embedded optimization layers requires differentiating through the optimization problem, which is challenging for general conic programs.
ZhRgDvN6F3.method: Rather than differentiating the full conic formulation, dOPT reduces it at a computed primal-dual solution to an equality-constrained quadratic program that preserves the reference solution and its first-order sensitivity. The reduction captures local first- and second-order conic geometry, stays well defined at singular configurations, and has explicit forms for convex NLPs, QPs, SOCPs and SDPs.
ZhRgDvN6F3.key_idea: Replace the conic program by a geometrically reduced equality-constrained QP at the solution, so derivatives come from one symmetric linear solve independent of the forward solver.
ZhRgDvN6F3.evidence: Numerical experiments validating computed gradients (including a comparison with CVXPYLayers per reviewers) and measuring backward-pass scalability against existing differentiable conic optimization methods.
ZhRgDvN6F3.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says substantial speedups over existing differentiable conic optimization methods as problem size increases, without numbers).
ZhRgDvN6F3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric reduction links classical sensitivity analysis to differentiable optimization, handles the curvature of nonpolyhedral cones (SOCP, SDP), and scales where baselines fail.
ZhRgDvN6F3.main_concern: It is unclear why the method is faster than other approaches that also solve linear systems, and the regularity assumptions are not stress-tested against near-degenerate cases such as SDP rank thresholds.

WmKScf8BXx.one_liner: SceneBloom samples furniture layouts with diffusion priors per functional zone, then compiles them to valid 3D via relation-guided geometric fitting.
WmKScf8BXx.problem: Language-guided scene generation lacks precise spatial grounding, while visual generative models give plausible layout priors but need geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes.
WmKScf8BXx.method: A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction.
WmKScf8BXx.key_idea: Propose layouts from a visual diffusion prior, then make them valid with a contract-guided compiler that fits geometry to extracted relations and corrects poses locally.
WmKScf8BXx.evidence: Five room types compared with other scene-generation methods on visual quality, physical stability, collisions and layout similarity to real rooms, plus object navigation policies trained on generated scenes and tested on held-out real scans.
WmKScf8BXx.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports highest visual quality and physical stability, no detected mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects, and higher held-out real-scan navigation success than training on an equal number of real scans, without numbers).
WmKScf8BXx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline is complete and well evaluated with ablations, and that training navigation policies on the generated scenes shows value beyond visual quality.
WmKScf8BXx.main_concern: Downstream navigation gains are small, and zero collisions may reflect post-processing repair and retrieved reference layouts rather than better initial layouts.

SpLs5saqpk.one_liner: Test-Time Generation replaces deterministic fast-weight readout with sampling a short conditional denoising trajectory, leaving the memory write operator unchanged.
SpLs5saqpk.problem: Fast-weight and test-time-training memories are read by deterministic regression, which under squared loss maps a query key to the conditional mean of its bindings and averages competing values away.
SpLs5saqpk.method: Test-Time Generation (TTG) is a drop-in readout: online updates supervise noisy versions of the observed bindings, and a query is answered by sampling a short denoising trajectory conditioned on the key. The write operator and fixed-size state are untouched.
SpLs5saqpk.key_idea: Cast fast weights as a conditional associative memory and read them with a key-conditioned denoiser, which adds a value-space posterior term that squared-error regression discards.
SpLs5saqpk.evidence: A controlled two-values-per-key recall probe, long-context language modeling at several scales (124M and 3B per reviewers) and novel view synthesis, with comparison to LaCT.
SpLs5saqpk.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off; it says no deterministic readout recovers both competing values on any key in the two-values-per-key probe, while the generative readout does).
SpLs5saqpk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the readout-bottleneck framing is clear and well motivated, supported by a controlled two-value probe and positive results in long-context language modeling and novel view synthesis.
SpLs5saqpk.main_concern: Gains cannot be cleanly attributed to the generative readout, since TTG also changes the write objective and conditioning modules and adds parameters (172.7M versus the 124M family), and language modeling gains are modest and inconsistent across scales.

vMnbPrABxw.one_liner: Agent alternates proof search and lemma extraction to discover reusable theorems from axioms alone, without human data.
vMnbPrABxw.problem: It is an open question whether an agent can autonomously discover useful theorems without human-provided theorem, proof, or training-problem data.
vMnbPrABxw.method: A self-supervised agent alternates between proof search in Hilbert-style propositional systems and useful-theorem extraction, selecting reusable lemmas for further search by generality and low reprovability under the current policy. The discovered theorems are also supplied as prompt lemmas to external LLMs.
vMnbPrABxw.key_idea: Select theorems that are general (not subsumed by specializations) and have low reprovability under the current policy, and feed them back as reusable lemmas for further proof search.
vMnbPrABxw.evidence: Tens of thousands of theorems discovered across three Hilbert-style propositional axiom systems; the classical-logic instance proves human-written benchmark problems; prompt lemmas are tested on multiple external LLMs, including GPT-6 Astra, on human-written and synthetic benchmarks.
vMnbPrABxw.claimed_gains: Discovers tens of thousands of theorems across three axiom systems and improves proof performance across multiple external LLMs, with larger benefits on harder problems; no accuracy numbers are stated.
vMnbPrABxw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the self-supervised formulation clean and simple, with experiments across three axiom systems showing the discovered theorems improve LLM proof performance.
vMnbPrABxw.main_concern: Scope is limited to Hilbert-style propositional logic, with doubts about mathematical significance beyond proof efficiency, novelty over hindsight relabelling and library learning, and low reprovability as a proxy for usefulness.

Yt75bNzxCB.one_liner: Replaces nested reverse-mode derivatives in weighted score matching for point processes with Taylor-mode evaluation, keeping reverse mode for parameters.
Yt75bNzxCB.problem: Weighted score matching for point processes is bottlenecked by nested reverse-mode automatic differentiation for event-coordinate derivatives.
Yt75bNzxCB.method: Taylor-mode WSM swaps the nested derivative evaluator for a Taylor-mode evaluator while retaining reverse-mode AD for parameter updates. A program-level cost framework derives the training-step speedup ratio and explains why the Taylor-mode evaluator is faster.
Yt75bNzxCB.key_idea: Compute event-coordinate derivatives with Taylor-mode AD so that the outer parameter backpropagation traverses a smaller derivative graph than under nested reverse mode.
Yt75bNzxCB.evidence: Experiments on statistical point processes, deep temporal point processes, and deep spatio-temporal point processes, plus studies varying derivative order and event-coordinate dimension.
Yt75bNzxCB.claimed_gains: Average speedup of 3.85x and up to 5.6x on deep STPPs without sacrificing model performance; outer backpropagation accounts for 90.4%-99.6% of the total time reduction.
Yt75bNzxCB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a drop-in change that preserves the original objective and model, substantial speedups on deep STPPs, and a cost analysis that locates where the savings come from.
Yt75bNzxCB.main_concern: The method is a known substitution (Taylor-mode AD is standard), with limited comparison to alternative higher-order differentiation strategies and evaluation confined to JAX on one GPU platform.

W1GdEjiyzl.one_liner: Counterfactual GRPO variant that suppresses video hallucination via paired opposite-label prompts, blind-failure advantage scaling, and within-group credit allocation.
W1GdEjiyzl.problem: Outcome-reward GRPO cannot distinguish visually grounded correct answers from those produced by the language prior (source-blind credit assignment).
W1GdEjiyzl.method: CF-GRPO adds three mechanisms: counterfactual pair optimization jointly trains opposite-label prompts sharing the same video, blind-failure advantage shaping scales the advantage by the model's failure probability without the video, and a third mechanism allocates credit within each output group.
W1GdEjiyzl.key_idea: Direct and scale GRPO updates by whether correctness depends on the video, using opposite-label prompt pairs and the model's no-video failure probability.
W1GdEjiyzl.evidence: Theoretical analysis of GRPO update dynamics plus experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B against standard GRPO and SFT baselines, including EventHallusion (per reviews).
W1GdEjiyzl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the source-blind credit-assignment failure of outcome-reward GRPO is a meaningful motivation, the three mechanisms are justified, and non-hallucination tasks show no degradation.
W1GdEjiyzl.main_concern: Blind-failure weighting may measure task solvability without the video rather than true visual grounding, and all experiments use a single model, Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

FOQO99yuux.one_liner: Builds semantic directions from text-pair contrasts, calibrates them to image embeddings, and audits VLM robustness with closed-form boundary margins.
FOQO99yuux.problem: Semantic variation is hard to formalize in image space, which makes VLM robustness under such variation difficult to audit.
FOQO99yuux.method: Semantic directions are built from semantic-contrast text pairs, aggregated across textual contexts, and calibrated to the visual embedding space by cross-modal correction. A framework then quantifies prediction stability along these directions with closed-form boundary margins across data, prompt, and model contexts.
FOQO99yuux.key_idea: Represent semantic variation as language-derived directions in embedding space and measure how far an embedding can move along them before the prediction flips (closed-form margin).
FOQO99yuux.evidence: Controlled visual validation on PUG shows language-derived directions align with visual semantic variations; audits are run across data, prompt, and model contexts, with domain-specific applications.
FOQO99yuux.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the research question meaningful and the method clearly structured, with attribute- and class-level auditing giving finer detail than aggregate metrics.
FOQO99yuux.main_concern: Validation shows directional alignment but does not test whether the margins predict actual prediction flips or robustness rankings under real visual transformations.

sl0SFa64mg.one_liner: Belief World Models let LLM agents query a maintained belief about the current state under partial observability.
sl0SFa64mg.problem: Simulation alone does not capture uncertainty about the current state, which LLM agents need for decision-making under partial observability.
sl0SFa64mg.method: Belief World Models maintain a belief that an LLM policy can query for what is known and uncertain about the current state. The paper first tests whether exposing belief directly improves decisions, using hand-built rule-based belief trackers rather than learned ones.
sl0SFa64mg.key_idea: Expose a world model's belief state to the LLM policy through a query interface, in addition to forward simulation of action consequences.
sl0SFa64mg.evidence: Experiments on text-based games (ALFWorld and BabyAI per reviews) across multiple LLMs and agent frameworks, with comparison to WALL-E and memory-only and non-uniform prior ablations.
sl0SFa64mg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree belief access is an intuitive, useful extension of simulation-only world model interfaces and improves performance on text-based games, supported by ablations.
sl0SFa64mg.main_concern: Beliefs rely on hand-made, environment-specific priors and rule-based updates, so it is unclear whether gains hold with inaccurate beliefs, and novelty over existing explicit-belief agents is limited.

AWzNXSkCQX.one_liner: Splits the SAM perturbation interval at key points and reweights the pieces with a convolution to improve generalization.
AWzNXSkCQX.problem: SAM uses only the worst-case perturbation and overlooks geometric information about the loss landscape within the perturbation interval.
AWzNXSkCQX.method: CRIK partitions the perturbation interval using key points and applies convolutional operations to adaptively adjust each interval's contribution. The paper analyzes the effect of interval number and examines convergence, escape time from sharp minima, and implicit gradient-Hessian combination.
AWzNXSkCQX.key_idea: Sample the loss at key points inside the perturbation interval and aggregate them with convolutional (tanh-based, increasing) weights, implicitly combining gradient and Hessian information.
AWzNXSkCQX.evidence: Convergence and escape-time analysis, plus simulations and experiments across a range of datasets and setups, mostly image classification (per reviews).
AWzNXSkCQX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, the method intuitive and plug-and-play through modified gradient updates, and the theoretical analysis extensive.
AWzNXSkCQX.main_concern: Gains over SAM are small, sometimes within run-to-run standard deviation and below the TSAM baseline, and ablations do not separate multi-point sampling, weighting, and gradient reuse.

0XYSiwbjue.one_liner: Builds an empirical transition graph from grouped rollouts and uses finite-budget graph-hit probability for process-level credit assignment.
0XYSiwbjue.problem: Critic-free group-based RL gives only coarse trajectory-level credit for multi-turn agents, and structural distance to success states does not capture policy-dependent success probability within a finite interaction budget.
0XYSiwbjue.method: GHGPO keeps state-transition topology and empirical transition frequencies from grouped rollouts to build a probabilistic state-transition graph, estimates the probability of reaching success within the available budget, and uses it for fine-grained process credit.
0XYSiwbjue.key_idea: Estimate policy-dependent success probability within the interaction budget from an empirical transition graph of rollouts, and use it as process credit alongside structural distance.
0XYSiwbjue.evidence: Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Sokoban across model scales, with ablations on finite-budget estimation and the complementarity of success probability and structural efficiency.
0XYSiwbjue.claimed_gains: Consistently improves aggregate performance over strong RL baselines across model scales with no additional environment interactions; overhead is stated as less than 0.2% (text truncated); specific scores are not stated.
0XYSiwbjue.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and validated, since structural distance to the goal does not reflect policy-dependent success probability, and GHGPO shows consistent improvements over graph-based baselines.
0XYSiwbjue.main_concern: The stationary Markov transition-graph estimate may not match history- and budget-dependent policies, and the evaluated environments are small and structured, so estimates may be unreliable in more complex settings.

OQGvRiW0te.one_liner: Online video memory that writes only the residual between incoming frames and the current memory prediction, trained with redundancy-aware consistency.
OQGvRiW0te.problem: Causal streaming video generation has limited attention windows, and context-based memory methods retain redundant visual information across neighboring frames, wasting memory capacity.
OQGvRiW0te.method: A learnable online memory predicts incoming visual representations from the current memory state with a frame-wise Delta rule and writes only the residual, and retrieved history is injected into attention layers. Redundancy-aware post-training enforces consistency of the recurrent memory state and its readout under constructed redundant history.
OQGvRiW0te.key_idea: Update a recurrent memory with a Delta rule that writes only the prediction residual, so already-represented content is suppressed, and train state and readout consistency under redundant history.
OQGvRiW0te.evidence: Comparisons with baselines on memory-consistency metrics (ORS, CoM), ablations of the update rule and redundancy-aware training, and controlled repetition tests (per reviews).
OQGvRiW0te.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge improved memory consistency over baselines, with ablations supporting the interaction between the Delta update and redundancy-aware training.
OQGvRiW0te.main_concern: The method is seen as complicated, and ablations do not cleanly separate its components or the extra training from the gain (no separate L_state and L_read ablations, no memory-free variant).

B97em83zBy.one_liner: Studies three ways to use deep sequence models in conformal prediction for time series, with asymptotic conditional coverage guarantees.
B97em83zBy.problem: Conformal coverage guarantees rely on exchangeability, which time series violate, and little work systematically studies how deep sequence models can be used in conformal prediction for time series.
B97em83zBy.method: Three approaches are studied: conditional quantile regression, conditional quantile function estimation, and localized conformal prediction (DSCP-QR, DSCP-QFE, DSCP-Local). Each comes with a theoretical analysis of asymptotic conditional coverage under suitable assumptions.
B97em83zBy.key_idea: Use deep sequence-model encoders to estimate conditional residual quantiles or representation-based localization weights, so coverage holds asymptotically via estimation consistency under temporal dependence.
B97em83zBy.evidence: Theory for asymptotic conditional coverage of all three approaches, and experiments on real-world datasets across base predictors, encoder architectures, and coverage levels, with ablations on quantile crossing constraints and quantile levels.
B97em83zBy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory clearly stated and the framework well organized, with experiments across datasets, base predictors, and encoders supporting DSCP-Local and identifying limits of DSCP-QFE.
B97em83zBy.main_concern: Advances over closely related prior methods (SPCI-T, CoRNN, HopCPT, CT-SSF) are insufficiently differentiated, and the guarantees are asymptotic under restrictive assumptions rather than finite-sample distribution-free.

LlFRODPGr8.one_liner: Lightweight history-aware model decides per planning step whether to run candidate search after generating a base trajectory.
LlFRODPGr8.problem: Generative motion planners that run candidate generation and scoring at every step incur extra computation, although the benefit of search varies greatly across planning steps.
LlFRODPGr8.method: A lightweight history-aware model decides, after the base trajectory is generated, whether to invoke the original search module; if not, the base trajectory is used directly.
LlFRODPGr8.key_idea: Predict from current planning information and recent history whether search will improve the trajectory, and skip search when it is predicted not to.
LlFRODPGr8.evidence: Closed-loop experiments on nuPlan, compared with Full Search and fixed search schedules, across multiple planners.
LlFRODPGr8.claimed_gains: Average score of 86.59 with search on 55.44% of planning steps, comparable to Full Search at 85.68 with 100% calls, and better than fixed search schedules at similar search rates.
LlFRODPGr8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives a practical computation-performance trade-off with reasonable analysis, clear writing, and applicability across several planners.
LlFRODPGr8.main_concern: The margin over Full Search is small with no multi-run variance, and local search-benefit supervision may not reflect closed-loop benefit, nor is timely operation or retention of safety-critical search shown.

k6Pd98Z9pu.one_liner: Prior-fitted network for node classification whose synthetic prior generates tasks via advection-diffusion-reaction graph dynamics.
k6Pd98Z9pu.problem: Priors of existing PFN-based node classifiers generate features independently of the graph or only aggregate over neighbours, covering a narrow range of feature-structure relations found in real graphs.
k6Pd98Z9pu.method: GadrPFN generates each task by evolving a node state on a random graph under an advection-diffusion-reaction equation for a randomly drawn time and reading node features from that state. It is trained from scratch on about half a million synthetic tasks in two hours on a single GPU.
k6Pd98Z9pu.key_idea: Sample synthetic node-classification tasks from randomized graph neural diffusion (advection, diffusion, reaction, separate label time) so feature smoothness and label homophily vary independently.
k6Pd98Z9pu.evidence: 28 homophilous and heterophilous node classification benchmarks, with controlled comparisons to existing priors and ablations (per reviews).
k6Pd98Z9pu.claimed_gains: Best mean accuracy and average rank for in-context node classification on 28 homophilous and heterophilous benchmarks, trained from scratch in two hours on one GPU.
k6Pd98Z9pu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the limitation of existing graph PFN priors is real and that the diffusion-based prior is a well-structured design space, evaluated on 28 graphs.
k6Pd98Z9pu.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate which prior components drive the gains, and the controlled comparison uses different inference settings for existing priors than for GadrPFN, so gains are not cleanly attributable to the prior.

KdNQfAKUeF.one_liner: VLM predicts HOI-code changes for new object properties; kinematic optimization and RL tracking adapt reference human-object motion.
KdNQfAKUeF.problem: HOI datasets lack property-labeled supervision, so existing contact-rich HOI motion cannot be adapted to unseen object properties without extra motion data or contact-breaking pose editing.
