KdNQfAKUeF.method: A VLM predicts property-dependent changes to compact HOI-codes, kinematic optimization moves the reference toward these targets in an anatomically plausible HOI motion space, and RL-based tracking in physics simulation refines the plans for execution. A new evaluation protocol jointly assesses property response and other criteria.
KdNQfAKUeF.key_idea: Use VLM-predicted, phase-wise changes to compact HOI-codes as adaptation targets in place of property-labeled motion data, then enforce contact and physics through optimization and RL tracking.
KdNQfAKUeF.evidence: Evaluation on 30 reference motions (per reviews) with a protocol covering property response, reference preservation, naturalness, biomechanical demand, and executability, against InterMimic-based and HOI-code-only baselines.
KdNQfAKUeF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting property-agnostic HOI references to unseen object properties without labeled data is well motivated and that the pipeline separating semantic adaptation from physical constraints is coherent.
KdNQfAKUeF.main_concern: The central claim that a VLM prior can replace property-labeled data is not directly tested, evidence rests on only 30 reference motions, and the contribution of HOI-code matching after RL fine-tuning is not isolated.

Mj6Wz4S1Sm.one_liner: Multi-agent harness where a Tool Agent retrieves and executes while an RL-trained GUI Coder generates front-end interfaces for users.
Mj6Wz4S1Sm.problem: Text-only human-agent interaction causes cognitive overload, ambiguity, and slow input on complex tasks, and training an interactive UI coder with RL faces costly verifiable rewards and reward-hackable LLM judges.
Mj6Wz4S1Sm.method: GenUI-Harness pairs a Tool Agent with a GUI Coder Agent that identifies ambiguities and generates front-end code. Dynamic UX supports interaction and reward collection in one sandbox, Reward Auditor distills diagnostic patterns into a shared rubric, and UI-TAU Bench on 10 real-world domain databases evaluates the task.
Mj6Wz4S1Sm.key_idea: Reward Auditor monitors reward distributions and distills diagnostic patterns into a shared rubric and scoring specification, countering LLM-as-a-Judge reward hacking while the GUI coder is trained with RL.
Mj6Wz4S1Sm.evidence: UI-TAU Bench built on 10 real-world domain databases and Tau-Bench tool setups, with comparisons to smolagents and off-the-shelf models, controlled GUI-Coder comparisons across five models, and a human study (per reviews).
Mj6Wz4S1Sm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is interesting and practical and that the benchmark, harness, and trained agents together form a well-rounded contribution, with controlled evidence that generated interfaces improve task performance.
Mj6Wz4S1Sm.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the gain comes from the generated UI as a communication medium versus agent organization or training differences, since no text-only clarification ablation of the same architecture is run.

jSkzXJ24qU.one_liner: Evaluation framework using predefined self-disclosure trajectories to isolate how prior disclosure history shapes LLM responses at matched current disclosure.
jSkzXJ24qU.problem: In naturally occurring conversations, disclosure history and current disclosure are confounded, so evaluations of conversational agents on isolated states cannot isolate the effect of history.
jSkzXJ24qU.method: TraDE, grounded in Social Penetration Theory, uses predefined disclosure trajectories and compares model responses under matched current disclosure across multiple models and relational behavior benchmarks, with a human comparison on the ESConv corpus.
jSkzXJ24qU.key_idea: Hold the current disclosure fixed while varying the preceding disclosure trajectory in synthetic conversations, so history effects can be measured counterfactually.
jSkzXJ24qU.evidence: Controlled experiments on four models and a human comparison across eight models against human supporters in ESConv (per reviews).
jSkzXJ24qU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the trajectory-based design for isolating history effects clear, well grounded, and carefully executed.
jSkzXJ24qU.main_concern: Findings may not generalize because the main controlled experiments cover only four models and rely on synthetic conversations from a single generator without clear quality control.

R8mMFRiveb.one_liner: Characterizes consistency-robustness trade-offs of strategyproof two-facility-location mechanisms given predictions of optimal facilities or agent preferences.
R8mMFRiveb.problem: It is unclear how predictions can improve strategyproof mechanisms for two-facility location on a line while keeping approximation guarantees when predictions are wrong.
R8mMFRiveb.method: For two prediction types (locations of an optimal facility pair, and each agent's preferred location), deterministic strategyproof mechanisms attain the characterized trade-off exactly, and randomized mechanisms give upper bounds on the consistency-robustness trade-off.
R8mMFRiveb.key_idea: Derive matching lower bounds and mechanisms that attain the optimal deterministic consistency-robustness frontier for each prediction type; agent-preference predictions help, optimal-facility predictions do not.
R8mMFRiveb.evidence: Theoretical results only: an exact deterministic frontier with matching lower bounds for both prediction types, and randomized upper and lower bounds that do not match (O(1/eps^2) versus Omega(1/eps) robustness for 1+eps consistency, per reviews).
R8mMFRiveb.claimed_gains: Predictions of optimal facility locations cannot improve on the optimal prediction-free approximation ratio, whereas predictions of agent preferences yield a nontrivial trade-off; no numeric values are stated.
R8mMFRiveb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree learning-augmented mechanism design is a natural, timely setting and that the deterministic consistency-robustness trade-off is settled with matching lower bounds.
R8mMFRiveb.main_concern: The setting is restrictive and the randomized bounds leave a gap between O(1/eps^2) and Omega(1/eps) robustness, with one reviewer also finding the presentation of statements and proofs hard to follow.

ixsjYR3sle.one_liner: Merges sequentially fine-tuned LoRA updates by keeping only each update's dominant singular directions, scaled by a damping factor.
ixsjYR3sle.problem: Each weight update in continual learning with pre-trained models risks erasing prior knowledge, and there is little theory explaining why merged models perform well.
ixsjYR3sle.method: Incremental spectral merging keeps only the dominant singular directions of each task's low-rank update, scales them by a damping factor, and realigns the classifier after the merge. A theorem bounds the merged model's loss by the classification-head change and the weight step between consecutive modules.
ixsjYR3sle.key_idea: Truncate each LoRA update to its top singular directions and damp it to limit the weight step, then realign the classifier to limit head drift, following a two-term loss bound.
ixsjYR3sle.evidence: Four class-incremental benchmarks plus robustness to input corruptions, compared with prior continual learning methods and published merging methods, with ablations (per reviews).
ixsjYR3sle.claimed_gains: Ranks first in average final accuracy and in robustness to input corruptions across four class-incremental benchmarks; specific numbers are not stated.
ixsjYR3sle.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the exemplar-free class-incremental setting relevant and the approach simple, memory-efficient, and clearly written, with experiments over several datasets and robustness tests.
ixsjYR3sle.main_concern: Evidence that spectral truncation itself matters is weak: gains seem driven by damping and classifier realignment, accuracy barely changes across truncation levels, and the theorem does not justify SVD truncation.

fptX8hpejo.one_liner: Augments bash outputs with LSP symbol identifiers so coding agents retrieve definitions and references directly, cutting exploration cost.
fptX8hpejo.problem: Coding agents spend large token budgets on text searches and code reads that return line-based fragments, needing extra queries to find complete definitions and symbol relationships.
fptX8hpejo.method: SWELSP connects the Language Server Protocol to the agent's existing workflow by adding symbol identifiers to bash outputs that agents can use to fetch definitions and references, without auxiliary models or dedicated analysis pipelines.
fptX8hpejo.key_idea: Annotate shell search results with symbol IDs resolvable through LSP, so agents navigate by symbol instead of repeated text search and windowed code reads.
fptX8hpejo.evidence: SWE-bench Multilingual and SWE-QA, with comparisons to Serena and AiderMap in OpenHands and a navigation-only ablation.
fptX8hpejo.claimed_gains: Reduces API cost by 10.1-21.3% on SWE-bench Multilingual and 19.8-29.6% on SWE-QA while maintaining task performance, and gives the lowest cost per resolved task against Serena and AiderMap.
fptX8hpejo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, training-free way to connect shell commands with language-server navigation that cuts API cost, with useful comparisons to Serena and AiderMap and a navigation-only ablation.
fptX8hpejo.main_concern: Novelty is seen as incremental interface integration of existing components, and single-run results and ablations cannot isolate which factor drives the gain.

nQRR2KSNNQ.one_liner: Fine-tunes a 3B VLM on teacher-built trajectories to sequentially acquire quantitative neuroimaging evidence via tools before answering.
nQRR2KSNNQ.problem: Multimodal models fail hard neuroimaging questions from MRI even though the signal is present: direct generation is at chance (0.333) while a linear probe reaches 0.897 balanced accuracy.
nQRR2KSNNQ.method: Multi-step evidence-seeking trajectories are built with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 2.5 Pro and used to fine-tune a 3B VLM to call quantitative measurement tools adaptively. Frontier comparators use the same interface zero-shot.
nQRR2KSNNQ.key_idea: Distill teacher trajectories that interleave tool calls for quantitative MRI measurements with reasoning, so the student learns which evidence to acquire and when.
nQRR2KSNNQ.evidence: Representation probing (CNN 0.962, Qwen2.5-VL linear probe 0.897, direct generation 0.333, language-side fine-tuning 0.743), nine models with and without tools, and ablations with static evidence, image removal, and donor-value substitution.
nQRR2KSNNQ.claimed_gains: Reaches 89.3% L3 accuracy without frontier-model calls at inference; four frontier models improve with tools to 75.6% to 80.0% L3 accuracy from Tool-OFF accuracy of 36.4% to 56.4% across models.
nQRR2KSNNQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the representation-probing study clearly separates accessible information from generated answers, and credit controlled diagnostics such as static-evidence, image-removal, and evidence-feedback tests.
nQRR2KSNNQ.main_concern: Adaptive acquisition adds little over static relevant-evidence selection (89.3% versus 88.9% L3, not significant), and evaluation is confined to recurring question forms and a single 3B backbone.

0sPW3yfUIh.one_liner: Shows simple adaptive changes to high-resolution model inversion attacks reveal far higher leakage, tracking adversarial robustness.
0sPW3yfUIh.problem: Standard evaluations of high-resolution model inversion attacks can mistake optimization and measurement failures for privacy, underestimating training-data leakage.
0sPW3yfUIh.method: The attack is adapted with simple changes (PPA variants per reviews) and re-evaluated against privacy defenses, MixUp, adversarial training, and undefended models, using different evaluator classifiers, and measured leakage is then related to adversarial robustness.
0sPW3yfUIh.key_idea: Adapt the attack to each defense and vary the evaluator's feature basis (standard versus adversarially trained Inception), exposing leakage hidden by fixed attack configurations and evaluators.
0sPW3yfUIh.evidence: 13 target models x 3 PPA variants x 2 datasets x 2 architectures = 156 conditions (per reviews), with FaceScrub evaluations using standard and adversarially trained Inception evaluators.
0sPW3yfUIh.claimed_gains: Leakage on FaceScrub is 1.16 to 6.59 times higher under simple adaptive attack changes across privacy defenses, MixUp, adversarial training, and undefended models.
0sPW3yfUIh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding that standard MIA evaluation underestimates leakage is striking and important, backed by broad experiments across defenses and architectures.
0sPW3yfUIh.main_concern: It is unclear which evaluator measures identity leakage more accurately, since evaluator disagreement shows sensitivity but does not establish that the robust evaluator is correct.

6ZdRmR5sxG.one_liner: Optimizes a single safety patch over simulated fine-tuned checkpoints, deployed by one weight addition to any fine-tuned LLM.
6ZdRmR5sxG.problem: Defenses against harmful fine-tuning either need per-request computation that scales with the number of fine-tuning jobs or add a fixed task-arithmetic safety vector that assumes translation invariance across checkpoints, which does not hold in general.
6ZdRmR5sxG.method: OPUS simulates diverse fine-tuned checkpoints with a perturbation bank built by fine-tuning and interpolation, optimizes a patch so the patched model refuses harmful queries while a KL term anchors it to the unpatched fine-tuned model, and deploys the precomputed patch by a single weight addition.
6ZdRmR5sxG.key_idea: Directly optimize a universal weight patch across simulated fine-tuned checkpoints to restore refusals, with a KL anchor preserving utility, instead of extracting a fixed safety vector from one checkpoint.
6ZdRmR5sxG.evidence: Experiments across four models, four tasks, and three out-of-distribution attack sources.
6ZdRmR5sxG.claimed_gains: Achieves the lowest average harmful score in every setting across four models, four tasks, and three attack sources while keeping utility (text truncated); no numbers are stated.
6ZdRmR5sxG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical for fine-tuning-as-a-service because the patch is trained once, and that it consistently improves safety across settings.
6ZdRmR5sxG.main_concern: It is unclear that simulated checkpoints (linear interpolation, a fixed LoRA setup, small perturbation banks) represent real fine-tuned models, so transfer to other LoRA settings, full fine-tuning, or adaptive attackers is unproven.

9D03W6kkn5.one_liner: Shows federated regression shared-head Gram matrices converge to a Bures-Wasserstein barycenter under a closest-head selection rule.
9D03W6kkn5.problem: In federated averaging, local objectives can admit multiple optimal heads, so the aggregate depends on which heads clients return.
9D03W6kkn5.method: In an unconstrained feature model for federated multivariate regression with private backbones and a shared linear head, each client returns the optimal head closest to the broadcast head, which a vanishing proximal penalty realizes. The paper derives the shared Gram recursion and its limit, decomposes the gap to centralized training, and proposes a one-time exchange of target means and covariances as a correction.
9D03W6kkn5.key_idea: Select the optimal head closest to the broadcast head, making the shared Gram matrix follow a closed recursion that converges to the Bures-Wasserstein barycenter of clients' optimal Gram matrices.
9D03W6kkn5.evidence: Theory in the unconstrained feature model, numerical verification, and tests on five tabular and five image regression datasets using deep networks with feature regularization and long local training.
9D03W6kkn5.claimed_gains: The correction recovers the centralized optimal Gram matrix in one round under exact local optimization and the same selection rule; no performance numbers are stated.
9D03W6kkn5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical insight clean and correct, in particular the closest-head rule giving a Bures-Wasserstein barycenter iteration and the three-term decomposition of the gap to centralized training.
9D03W6kkn5.main_concern: The theory assumes exact local optimization every round and an imposed proximal selection rule, so it may not describe practical FedAvg with limited local epochs.

ZvM6SAwCGk.one_liner: Immunizes images against diffusion editing by maximizing deviation of one-step clean-latent predictions from stochastic neighbors of an early denoising state.
ZvM6SAwCGk.problem: Existing immunization methods need costly full-trajectory backpropagation or use intermediate objectives weakened by later denoising, and a single inference path gives limited feedback about alternative denoising continuations.
ZvM6SAwCGk.method: Starting from an early denoising state, SPIN generates stochastic neighboring states under the same instruction, predicts their clean latents by one-step projection without full unrolling, and optimizes a bounded input perturbation to maximize the average deviation from a clean-edit reference.
ZvM6SAwCGk.key_idea: Average the deviation of one-step clean-latent predictions over stochastic neighbors of an early denoising state, so the perturbation disrupts multiple possible editing outcomes without backpropagating through the full trajectory.
ZvM6SAwCGk.evidence: Experiments on two image editors, including unseen instructions, scored with an Immunization Success Rate judged by two vision-language models (per reviews).
ZvM6SAwCGk.claimed_gains: Substantial gains in protection performance, outperforming compared methods on two image editors (text truncated); no numbers are stated.
ZvM6SAwCGk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one-step projection with stochastic neighborhood optimization is an efficient way to build protective perturbations without full-trajectory backpropagation, with strong results on both editors.
ZvM6SAwCGk.main_concern: Evaluation is limited: success rate relies only on two VLM judges, cross-model transfer to unseen editors is untested, and recent optimization-free, universal, and early-stage (DiffusionGuard) immunization methods are missing from comparisons.

6KgYPUqGcA.one_liner: Proposes a convex design criterion M_alpha that tightly characterizes estimation error for experimental design under heavy-tailed linear regression noise.
6KgYPUqGcA.problem: How to select and allocate measurements for accurate estimation when observation noise has only a bounded alpha-th moment for some 1 < alpha <= 2 (heavy-tailed linear regression).
6KgYPUqGcA.method: Defines a design criterion M_alpha(lambda; A) and shows a suitable estimator achieves error proportional to M_alpha^(1/alpha) n^(-(alpha-1)/alpha) while no estimator on that design does better up to constants. It also gives an alpha-agnostic design whose error matches the known-alpha design up to an O(sqrt(log d)) factor, with a lower bound.
6KgYPUqGcA.key_idea: A new convex criterion M_alpha(lambda; A), equal to the classical G-optimal criterion at alpha = 2, tightly characterizes the heavy-tailed estimation error rate achievable by a design.
6KgYPUqGcA.evidence: Theory: matching upper and lower bounds on estimation error, a separation from G-optimal design, and an alpha-agnostic design with a lower bound; experiments mainly compare against G-optimality (per reviews).
6KgYPUqGcA.claimed_gains: Qualitative separation from the G-optimal design by a factor of Omega-tilde(d^(1/alpha - 1/2)) in error, and an alpha-agnostic design matching the known-alpha error up to an O(sqrt(log d)) factor.
6KgYPUqGcA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the convex criterion M_alpha with nearly matching upper and lower bounds gives a near-complete, well-justified answer to heavy-tailed experimental design, including the unknown-alpha case.
6KgYPUqGcA.main_concern: Evaluating M_alpha requires solving a saddle-point problem that may be intractable at large scale, and the parameter class for the claimed optimality and baselines beyond G-optimality need clarification.

LQoIavb1mE.one_liner: Benchmark and training source factorizing action-conditioned visual transition (s, a, s') supervision to train and study MLLM world-modeling transfer.
LQoIavb1mE.problem: MLLMs show scattered failures across spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning, hypothesized to share a deficit in action-conditioned visual transition reasoning over (s, a, s') triplets.
LQoIavb1mE.method: WOVEN factorizes transition supervision along independently controllable semantic dimensions using rollouts from video-pretrained generative models. Controlled training subsets of about 2,000 examples are used to study transfer and derive a training recipe organized by query operator.
LQoIavb1mE.key_idea: Organize transition supervision by the query operator over (s, a, s'), since curricula sharing an operator show similar downstream gain profiles, and use that to select training data.
LQoIavb1mE.evidence: Post-training on controlled subsets of about 2,000 examples evaluated on 26 external benchmarks, with scale, human-evaluation, bias-control, and prospective evaluations (per reviews).
LQoIavb1mE.claimed_gains: Post-training improves 22 of 26 external benchmarks with gains up to 27.3 percentage points, using controlled subsets of only approximately 2,000 examples.
LQoIavb1mE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled transfer experiments are extensive and persuasive, showing substantial gains and that supervision organized by reasoning family transfers in structured ways.
LQoIavb1mE.main_concern: The 22-of-26 result selects the best subset and training stage per benchmark while full-dataset training degrades some capabilities, and the contribution of reasoning type is not isolated from difficulty or data budget.

001PJNwZiT.one_liner: Analyzes why shallow autoencoders detect multivariate time-series anomalies beyond PCA, showing they learn conditional relations beyond second-order statistics.
001PJNwZiT.problem: ShallowAE is highly competitive on the TSB-AD-M benchmark, yet it is unclear what it learns from normal data and how that shapes anomaly scores.
001PJNwZiT.method: Proves that mean and covariance determine the risk function for affine reconstruction but not for nonlinear objectives, then uses moment-matched interventions, fixed PCA-subspace controls, and a relation-switching experiment to show that low-residual regions and scores change with the normal conditional relations.
001PJNwZiT.key_idea: Nonlinear reconstruction depends on activation-conditioned moments, so learning normal conditional relations between variables reshapes low-residual regions and anomaly scores even when global mean and covariance are identical.
001PJNwZiT.evidence: Theorems on sufficiency of second-order statistics, moment-matched interventions on real time series, PCA-subspace controls, and an analytically tractable synthetic relation-switching experiment, with the TSB-AD-M benchmark.
001PJNwZiT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the moment-matched interventions, fixed-subspace controls, and relation-switching experiments give complementary mechanistic evidence on what ShallowAE learns beyond covariance.
001PJNwZiT.main_concern: The link between the controlled mechanism and real-data behavior is incomplete, and the theory relies on piecewise-affine ReLU structure with limited practical guidance.

9VBX8FdZtO.one_liner: Training-free, question-agnostic video token compression that keeps salient events plus the temporally preceding visual context, selected with DPPs.
9VBX8FdZtO.problem: Existing video token compression keeps key-event information but drops the temporally antecedent visual evidence needed to interpret later events, so aggressive compression degrades temporal reasoning accuracy.
9VBX8FdZtO.method: CueMiner captures salient events and mines the temporally antecedent visual context, using bidirectional and local surprisal scores, segment-wise processing, and DPP-based selection (per reviews), without training and independent of the question.
9VBX8FdZtO.key_idea: Score visual tokens bidirectionally so tokens preceding key events are retained along with the events, and select diverse tokens via DPP, preserving context for temporal reasoning.
9VBX8FdZtO.evidence: Four video LLMs and four benchmarks across multiple retention ratios and frame counts, including MLVU with LLaVA-OneVision.
9VBX8FdZtO.claimed_gains: On MLVU with LLaVA-OneVision, retains 99.4% of the accuracy at a retention ratio of 5%.
9VBX8FdZtO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving context preceding key events is well motivated and that the training-free method retains strong accuracy at about 5% of visual tokens across models and benchmarks.
9VBX8FdZtO.main_concern: DPP selection is weakly justified since simpler Top-k beats it in accuracy and latency on longer videos, the comparison to CDPruner is missing, and the end-to-end speedup is modest.

MnN0WKt0RI.one_liner: Observational corpus of human-created posts across audiences, used to compare LLMs with human creators on audience orientation and audience design.
MnN0WKt0RI.problem: Existing evaluations treat LLM-generated content as isolated text and overlook that creators target specific audiences and adapt content to their needs.
MnN0WKt0RI.method: AudCraft is an observational corpus of real-world human-created content (about 1.59 million posts per reviews). LLMs are evaluated on audience orientation (whom they create for) and audience design (how they adapt expression), plus a Tullock contest-based simulation of competition for audience attention.
MnN0WKt0RI.key_idea: Compare LLM and human content along audience orientation and audience design, and simulate a Tullock contest to show that concentrated orientation is amplified into uneven content supply.
MnN0WKt0RI.evidence: Analysis across 55 segments and four models, a Tullock contest simulation, and a human evaluation with 275 blinded comparisons (per reviews); the orientation experiment uses 100 human posts and 100 generations per model.
MnN0WKt0RI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the audience-oriented perspective on LLM-generated content relevant and well motivated, with a real-world dataset, comparisons across LLMs, and human validation.
MnN0WKt0RI.main_concern: The main audience-orientation experiment uses small samples (100 human posts and 100 generations per model) and human posts were filtered with Fast-DetectGPT, which may bias the human-LLM gap.

y20UqvGPBa.one_liner: Learns per-region geometric influence from delete-and-refill interventions on complete geometry to weight correspondences in category-level pose estimation.
y20UqvGPBa.problem: Correspondences with similar reliability can play different geometric roles in pose estimation, since a broad surface may be redundant while a small distinctive region can resolve an ambiguity.
y20UqvGPBa.method: On paired complete training geometry, regions are deleted and refilled, and the response of a frozen estimator is combined with a dense geometric proxy into four target channels (orthogonal rotation, axial rotation, translation, size). A point-cloud-only predictor learns these from partial observations and combines influence with reliability in weighted Kabsch initialization and joint pose-and-size refinement.
y20UqvGPBa.key_idea: Supervise a predictor with estimator-specific responses to region deletion and refilling on complete geometry, then use predicted influence to weight correspondences in Kabsch pose and size recovery.
y20UqvGPBa.evidence: Unseen object instances on REAL275 and HouseCat6D, with matched REAL275 ablations of regional supervision, channel removal, and sensitivity over 3 seeds (per reviews).
y20UqvGPBa.claimed_gains: Highest strict-pose mAP among compared point-cloud methods on unseen instances of REAL275 and HouseCat6D; specific numbers are not stated.
y20UqvGPBa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between correspondence reliability and geometric role is clear and well motivated, supported by thorough ablations and training-only use of complete geometry.
y20UqvGPBa.main_concern: Gains appear only at strict thresholds, with weaker results at relaxed metrics (10 degree/5cm on REAL275, both 10 degree metrics on HouseCat6D), and evidence that deletion responses carry the signal is weak.

U42YXhYvh0.one_liner: Shows Linear Datamodeling Score can be inflated by reweighting aggregation alone, and proposes SNR-LDS modeling Gaussian measurement noise.
U42YXhYvh0.problem: LDS, the common metric for training data attribution, can change by altering aggregation weights alone because noisy low-influence scores contribute to it, undermining method comparisons.
U42YXhYvh0.method: SNR-LDS models measurement noise in attribution scores as zero-mean Gaussian (with a shared scale per method and query, per reviews) and estimates its effect on LDS; the rest of the estimator description is truncated in the input.
U42YXhYvh0.key_idea: Model the sampling noise in attribution scores as zero-mean Gaussian and estimate its effect on LDS, so evaluation separates signal from noise-driven errors.
U42YXhYvh0.evidence: Analysis of long-tailed attribution score magnitudes and repeated-estimate variation, demonstrations that truncating low-influence scores and power transforms change LDS, and evaluation of deletion effects and source retrieval (per reviews).
U42YXhYvh0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree attribution scores are noisy and that LDS can shift through aggregation-side reweighting or score transformations alone, which undermines method comparisons.
U42YXhYvh0.main_concern: SNR-LDS rests on an unvalidated assumption of zero-mean Gaussian noise with a shared scale, and correcting a method's own noise may be an unfair basis for an evaluation metric.

pGIsnL2pg4.one_liner: Builds a real-vulnerability repair-pair dataset and trains code LLMs with teacher-guided token-level RL rewards for secure code generation.
pGIsnL2pg4.problem: LLM-generated code often contains security vulnerabilities, held back by scarce high-quality security data and coarse instance-level RL reward signals.
pGIsnL2pg4.method: Vul2Safe uses LLM self-reflection to build high-confidence repair pairs from real-world vulnerabilities and generates diverse implicit prompts to form the PrimeVul+ dataset. SRCode then trains with token-level rewards in RL (SFT plus PPO with teacher-guided rewards, per reviews) to reinforce critical fine-grained security patterns.
pGIsnL2pg4.key_idea: Assign RL rewards to the specific tokens carrying security-critical patterns, as identified by a teacher, instead of one instance-level reward for the whole generation.
pGIsnL2pg4.evidence: Experiments on multiple security benchmarks and general code-generation tests with Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder, and CodeLlama backbones, plus a matched-budget ablation of token-level versus uniform rewards (per reviews).
pGIsnL2pg4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SRCode improves security metrics consistently across backbones and benchmarks, and that the matched-budget ablation supports the benefit of token-level reward localization.
pGIsnL2pg4.main_concern: The method is seen as combining existing SFT, PPO, and teacher-guided localized rewards, depends on a teacher judge whose reliability on harder settings is unproven, and uses somewhat outdated models and benchmarks.

tVGabAKHGs.one_liner: Detects visual attacks on GUI agents from head-wise attention-entropy deviations during a single grounding inference, using Mahalanobis distance.
tVGabAKHGs.problem: Existing detectors of visual adversarial attacks on GUI grounding models need adversarial fitting examples or repeated inference.
tVGabAKHGs.method: AHEAD extracts head-wise attention-entropy features during a single grounding inference, measures their deviation from a clean reference, and scores it with Mahalanobis distance against a threshold calibrated on clean inputs.
tVGabAKHGs.key_idea: Visual attacks change how attention is distributed over screenshot regions during coordinate prediction, so head-wise attention-entropy deviations from a clean reference reveal them without adversarial fitting data.
tVGabAKHGs.evidence: Four grounding models, two interface datasets, and three attack settings, with ablations, mobile-to-web cross-domain adaptation, and an adaptive attack evaluation (per reviews).
tVGabAKHGs.claimed_gains: Mean AUROC of 0.997 and mean true positive rate of 99.0% at a matched 3% false positive rate, with the lowest overhead among baselines; transfers between mobile and web with 50 clean inputs at a mean 0.907 TPR@3%FPR.
tVGabAKHGs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and the clean-only, single-pass detector is practical, with extensive experiments across four models, two datasets, and three attacks, low latency overhead, and good ablations.
tVGabAKHGs.main_concern: Novelty is limited since it combines established attention-entropy and Mahalanobis detection, and the detector may flag benign distribution shift (100% false positives across domains without adaptation).

joqtZuoxrA.one_liner: Tokenizes metric point maps and fuses them into a dedicated orthonormal subspace of the LLM embedding space for spatial reasoning.
joqtZuoxrA.problem: Existing 3D-aware VLMs use expensive geometry encoders or mix compressed geometry with RGB features without ensuring the injected 3D information stays accessible, so quantitative depth and distance inference stays weak.
joqtZuoxrA.method: A Point-Map Tokenizer pretrained by masked XYZ point-map reconstruction converts dense metric observations into compact geometric tokens. Geometry-Preserving Fusion maps them through a fixed orthonormal basis into a dedicated LLM embedding subspace and adds them to spatially aligned RGB visual tokens.
joqtZuoxrA.key_idea: Map geometry tokens through a fixed orthonormal basis into a dedicated embedding subspace and add them to RGB tokens, so the injected geometry stays recoverable after fusion.
joqtZuoxrA.evidence: Controlled comparisons with an RGB-only SFT baseline and re-implemented SD-VLM and N3D-VLM injection on the same 1B base, with tokenizer and fusion ablations on CV-Bench, SPAR, and MD2 benchmarks (per reviews).
joqtZuoxrA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit controlled comparisons against RGB-only SFT and re-implemented injection baselines, and ablations showing the tokenizer and fusion avoid the collapse caused by naive geometry fusion.
joqtZuoxrA.main_concern: Most of the benchmark gain appears to come from the SFT data rather than geometry, since RGB-only SFT already provides about 86% of the gain and is missing from the main comparison table.

XX4GxBzhgE.one_liner: Post-training refinement for flow map models that mixes supervision signals using state-dependent reliability estimated from target-space disagreement.
XX4GxBzhgE.problem: Flow map model training treats supervision reliability as globally uniform, although reliability varies substantially across transport states.
XX4GxBzhgE.method: RAFL builds a flow-map-aware supervision-risk framework and estimates state-dependent reliability from target-space disagreement to construct adaptive finite-time supervision. It is applied as lightweight post-training refinement of pretrained flow map models and keeps their original inference procedure.
XX4GxBzhgE.key_idea: Estimate per-state reliability of conditional versus pretrained-teacher supervision from target-space disagreement and use it as a risk-adaptive mixing coefficient during training.
XX4GxBzhgE.evidence: Controlled analyses of state-dependent reliability and experiments across diverse flow map models, including ImageNet-256 with MF-B (per reviews).
XX4GxBzhgE.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements in generation quality without additional inference-time cost; no numbers are stated.
XX4GxBzhgE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the method works as a plug-and-play refinement with consistent gains over base flow map models on ImageNet-256.
XX4GxBzhgE.main_concern: The theory is a standard bias-variance trade-off resting on an unmeasured nearest-neighbor assumption, gains over direct gating are small (FID 3.07 to 3.01), and the notation is hard to follow.

2bKsbubhS2.one_liner: Routes on-policy self-distillation direction by token entropy: pull toward the privileged teacher at low entropy, push away at high entropy.
2bKsbubhS2.problem: On-policy self-distillation degrades complex reasoning by suppressing predictive uncertainty, which supports exploration and hypothesis revision.
2bKsbubhS2.method: DASD, derived from a token-level analysis of where each direction of teacher supervision helps or harms, pushes high-entropy tokens away from the privileged teacher and pulls low-entropy tokens toward it.
2bKsbubhS2.key_idea: Use student token entropy to choose the sign of privileged-teacher supervision: repel at high-entropy tokens to preserve exploration, attract at low-entropy tokens to stabilize step execution.
2bKsbubhS2.evidence: Six mathematical reasoning benchmarks against RLVR and self-distillation baselines (GRPO, RLSD, OPSD, SDPO per reviews), plus Pass@k, execution-and-exploration, and generalization analyses across model scales.
2bKsbubhS2.claimed_gains: Best macro Avg@16 across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks over strong RLVR and self-distillation baselines; specific numbers are not stated.
2bKsbubhS2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree on broad, consistent empirical gains across benchmarks, model scales, and domains, with thorough ablations and a well-motivated link from diagnostic analysis to the training rule.
2bKsbubhS2.main_concern: The diagnostic probes do not firmly establish the causal entropy-routing explanation, and closely related methods that reverse teacher supervision (RLRT, AntiSD) are neither discussed nor compared.

77pnh3sHhV.one_liner: Long-video benchmark with annotated temporal intervals and key-frame boxes, scoring answer correctness jointly with spatio-temporal evidence grounding.
77pnh3sHhV.problem: Answer accuracy alone does not show whether video MLLMs can locate the evidence needed to answer a question.
77pnh3sHhV.method: VideoZeroBench has manually annotated QA pairs across 13 video domains targeting fine-grained cues and fleeting events, with two rounds of cross-verification. A five-level protocol compares answering with and without evidence hints and then combines correctness with independently evaluated temporal and spatial grounding.
77pnh3sHhV.key_idea: Evaluate video QA in five levels that combine answer correctness with separately measured temporal and spatial grounding, exposing models that answer correctly without localizing evidence.
77pnh3sHhV.evidence: 19 models evaluated, with analyses of atomic abilities, evidence spans, input modalities, and thinking-with-videos inference, plus a human study on a shared subset (per reviews).
77pnh3sHhV.claimed_gains: Best standard QA accuracy is 24.8% (Level-3), by Gemini-3.7-Flash, and no model exceeds 1.8% when correct answers and accurate spatio-temporal localization are jointly required (Level-5).
77pnh3sHhV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evidence annotations are the main value and that the human reference makes the low model scores interpretable as a real gap rather than unfair questions.
77pnh3sHhV.main_concern: Level-5 scores are too low to discriminate models (top score 1.8%, 11 of 19 models at 0.0), and cross-model comparison mixes reasoning ability with differences in evidence availability in model inputs.

nOIach0c6D.one_liner: Fine-tuning video generators on abstract reasoning data transfers to perception, robot manipulation, and world simulation in a 4x4 cross-domain study.
nOIach0c6D.problem: It is unanswered whether the reasoning-like competences needed when video generators act as world models can be acquired by training and whether they generalize beyond the training domain.
nOIach0c6D.method: XVReason and XVReason-Bench pair training data with matched evaluation across abstract visual reasoning, low-level perception, embodied manipulation, and world simulation, supporting a 4x4 cross-domain study on two video backbones. ReasonGraft blends a reasoning LoRA with another component (text truncated).
nOIach0c6D.key_idea: Fine-tune video generators on abstract reasoning, whose gains transfer through instruction following, goal completion, and scene stability and are mostly recovered via the high-noise expert.
nOIach0c6D.evidence: 4x4 cross-domain transfer matrices on two video backbones (including Wan2.2), with ablations over adaptation regime, data scale, denoising stage, expert loading, and task composition.
nOIach0c6D.claimed_gains: Abstract reasoning is the only fine-tuning domain that improves all four task domains on both backbones, with gains of +42.3/+20.6/+10.7% on the three application domains of Wan2.2.
nOIach0c6D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the complete 4x4 transfer matrices on two backbones are a useful systematic study, with substantial perception and manipulation gains and informative diagnostic ablations.
nOIach0c6D.main_concern: The contribution of reasoning itself is not isolated, since instruction-following-only training beats reasoning-only training on all three application domains, and ReasonGraft adds only 0.2 to 0.3 points over in-domain fine-tuning.

5ONtXYudap.one_liner: Accelerated Bregman proximal gradient exploiting geometry in proximal and mirror-space updates, without triangle-scaling, with backtracking acceptance tests.
5ONtXYudap.problem: Existing accelerated BPG algorithms for convex objectives need extra assumptions on Bregman divergences, notably triangle-scaling conditions, which can lead to slower convergence rates.
5ONtXYudap.method: A family of geometry-accelerated BPG algorithms exploits Bregman geometry in both proximal-gradient and mirror-space updates and adapts stepsizes and mirror-space updates by local backtracking with computable acceptance criteria, without a global relative-smoothness constant as input.
5ONtXYudap.key_idea: Adapt stepsizes and mirror-space updates by local backtracking with computable acceptance criteria, and bound convergence by the accepted parameters instead of assuming triangle scaling.
5ONtXYudap.evidence: Convergence theory for convex, relatively strongly convex, and nonconvex objectives, with experiments on inverse problems, entropy-regularized least squares, D-optimal design, and nonnegative matrix factorization against Bregman baselines.
5ONtXYudap.claimed_gains: O(k^-2) rate for convex and a linear rate for relatively strongly convex objectives when acceleration parameters stay uniformly bounded, O(k^-1) for a stationarity measure in the nonconvex case, and faster practical convergence than established Bregman baselines.
5ONtXYudap.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework treats convex, relatively strongly convex, and nonconvex cases with well-established rates, is adaptive without needing problem parameters, and avoids the triangle-scaling condition.
5ONtXYudap.main_concern: Acceleration rates depend on algorithmic parameters staying uniformly bounded, which is verified only for Burg geometry, and novelty relative to ABPG-g is unclear.

LaMTigvqom.one_liner: Restricts on-policy distillation teacher supervision to rollouts whose prefixes remain viable, estimated from the teacher's conditional success probability.
LaMTigvqom.problem: Once a student-generated prefix deviates from the task objective, teacher supervision is conditioned on an erroneous context, making distillation at such states ineffective or harmful.
LaMTigvqom.method: Prefix viability is the teacher's success probability given the prefix, normalized by its success probability from the original input. ViableOPD identifies viable rollouts for supervision, adjusts token-level supervision strength within them, and adapts the rollout horizon by the fraction of viable rollouts.
LaMTigvqom.key_idea: Gate on-policy teacher supervision by prefix viability, the normalized probability that the task can still be achieved from the student's prefix, at rollout, token, and horizon levels.
LaMTigvqom.evidence: Multiple benchmarks and teacher-student pairs against OPD baselines; diagnostics show 38% of rollouts enter a low-viability zone, and results are from a single seed (per reviews).
LaMTigvqom.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms strong OPD baselines while reducing training time by 33.6% on average relative to standard OPD.
LaMTigvqom.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the observation that visited states are not necessarily viable is clear and underexplored, supported by diagnostic experiments and ablations of each design choice.
LaMTigvqom.main_concern: Empirical evidence is thin (single seed without variance, modest gains, missing oracle and PRM controls) and the 33.6% training-time saving excludes the cost of building the viability judge.

9fAgUx2f15.one_liner: Shows weight-tied recursive reasoners collapse under per-tensor 4-bit quantization and recover with per-block MXINT4 scaling.
9fAgUx2f15.problem: Quantizing weight-tied recursive reasoning models causes severe error accumulation because quantization error is incurred at every reuse step.
9fAgUx2f15.method: Diagnoses that the collapse is governed by activation-scaling granularity rather than bit-width or number format, and applies MXINT4, a blockwise integer format with power-of-two block scales for weights and activations, to recursive reasoning models without retraining.
9fAgUx2f15.key_idea: Use per-block activation scaling (MXINT4) so quantization error contracts across recursion steps, instead of a per-tensor scale that applies the same systematic error at every step.
9fAgUx2f15.evidence: TRM, HRM, and five models in total, on Sudoku exact-solution accuracy over three training seeds and ARC-AGI-1, with noise-injection, single-step, and weight-reuse experiments and comparison to blockwise float formats.
9fAgUx2f15.claimed_gains: Per-tensor 4-bit with an unclipped scale drops Sudoku exact-solution accuracy from 83.3% to 0.8%; per-block scaling restores most of the lost accuracy on all five models tested.
9fAgUx2f15.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the collapse under per-tensor W4A4 is striking and that blockwise MXINT4 recovers most full-precision accuracy without retraining.
9fAgUx2f15.main_concern: The headline recovery is measured against a deliberately coarse per-tensor baseline, and experiments do not separate a recursion-specific problem from ordinary quantization error relative to reasonable fine-grained W4A4 baselines.

iiyHf08NTv.one_liner: Learns transferable attribute-induced textual residuals that improve fine-grained real-time open-vocabulary detection while text embeddings stay cacheable.
iiyHf08NTv.problem: Real-time open-vocabulary detectors lag significantly behind heavy open-vocabulary detectors on fine-grained detection tasks.
iiyHf08NTv.method: TRP is a lightweight adaptation that learns textual residuals instead of modifying the detector or relearning full textual representations, so the adapted text embeddings can still be cached before inference in the prompt-then-detect paradigm.
iiyHf08NTv.key_idea: Fine-grained attributes correspond to stable semantic directions in text embedding space (residuals consistent across base categories), so learn those residuals to raise discriminability.
iiyHf08NTv.evidence: Fine-grained detection experiments with YOLO-World on FG-OVD data against full fine-tuning, head fine-tuning, visual prompts, and other parameter-efficient methods, plus reference comparisons with heavier detectors (per reviews).
iiyHf08NTv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree TRP is a practical, lightweight adaptation that preserves cached prompt-then-detect inference with nearly unchanged latency and beats the closest internal baseline across YOLO-World benchmark settings.
iiyHf08NTv.main_concern: The comparison with heavier detectors uses inconsistent evaluation settings (fixed N for the references versus TRP averaged over all valid N), and cross-category transferability of residuals is not directly validated on held-out categories.

n4iNw5dLd7.one_liner: Plug-in repair aligns quantized diffusion models' high-noise clean estimates with full precision to restore minority generation.
n4iNw5dLd7.problem: Low-bit diffusion models keep standard sampling quality but degrade minority generation, because quantization error is large in the high-noise clean estimates that minority samplers rely on.
n4iNw5dLd7.method: A lightweight plug-in repair combines selective bit allocation with a quantization-consistent low-rank adapter that stays on the deployed quantization grid and is activated only when computing the high-noise clean estimates, leaving the ordinary sampling path unchanged.
n4iNw5dLd7.key_idea: Align the high-noise clean estimates of the quantized model with those of the full-precision model using a grid-consistent low-rank adapter and selective bits, activated only for those estimates.
n4iNw5dLd7.evidence: Experiments across diverse diffusion architectures (including ADM and DiT per reviews), bit widths, and minority samplers, with score-fidelity diagnostics and component ablations.
n4iNw5dLd7.claimed_gains: Substantially improves minority generation with negligible overhead while retaining low-bit efficiency; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
n4iNw5dLd7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of why minority sampling collapses under quantization while standard sampling survives is clear and quantitative, and the targeted repair is deployment-compatible with broad evidence across architectures and samplers.
n4iNw5dLd7.main_concern: The contribution of the repair machinery is not isolated from simpler fixes such as high-noise-weighted recalibration, and some theoretical conditions do not cover all evaluated settings.

t09qJcvW7h.one_liner: Distills adversarial training curricula into in-context RL policies that infer disturbances from context, reducing robust RL conservatism without parameter updates.
t09qJcvW7h.problem: Robust RL uses max-min optimization to withstand worst-case disturbances, often sacrificing nominal performance when the encountered environment admits a less conservative policy.
t09qJcvW7h.method: The CORE pretraining pipeline distills the adversary curriculum and specialized intermediate policies from max-min training into an in-context RL model, and uses the final robust controller to collect its initial deployment context. BRIDGE further uses adversarial experience to strengthen in-context generalization to unseen tasks under deployment disturbances.
t09qJcvW7h.key_idea: Reuse the adversaries and intermediate policies generated by max-min robust training as pretraining experience for in-context RL, so the model infers the disturbance and activates a tailored policy.
t09qJcvW7h.evidence: Theory with a bound (Theorem 5.1, per reviews) and experiments across tasks and benchmarks, including MuJoCo physical-parameter settings (per reviews), with ablations.
t09qJcvW7h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the core insight is simple and compelling: max-min training already produces a curriculum of adversaries and specialized policies that can supervise in-context policies, supported by theory and ablations.
t09qJcvW7h.main_concern: Reviewers question the total cost of building the expert curriculum, scaling and target conflicts when distilling many experts, and the loose link between the theory's coverage assumptions and the experiments.

7u9QRzksL5.one_liner: Generates efficiency-exposing test cases from problem statements alone by saturating constraint bounds and injecting retrieved adversarial structures.
7u9QRzksL5.problem: Existing symbolic-execution and performance-fuzzing methods for finding costly inputs need analysis or execution of a target implementation.
7u9QRzksL5.method: STAB resolves large admissible input sizes with a rule-based and CP-SAT constraint saturator, retrieves adversarial construction principles from a curated scenario catalog by keyword matching and KNN, and encodes both into a specification from which an LLM synthesizes a Python generator.
7u9QRzksL5.key_idea: Separate input scale from adversarial structure: solve maximal constraint-respecting sizes with CP-SAT and add catalog-retrieved adversarial patterns, so the LLM writes the generator without implementation access.
7u9QRzksL5.evidence: CodeContests across multiple LLMs and languages, compared with EvalPerf, WEDGE, and HardTestGen (per reviews), with supplementary ablations.
7u9QRzksL5.claimed_gains: Increases the rate of generated test cases that expose algorithmic bottlenecks from 51.52% to 74.61% on average (text truncated).
7u9QRzksL5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating size saturation from adversarial structure is intuitive, needs no target implementation, training, or execution feedback, and gives consistent gains across LLMs and languages.
7u9QRzksL5.main_concern: Evaluation relies on a noise-sensitive success-rate metric on one corpus, without comparison to related work such as AutoCode or a test of catching actually inefficient solutions.

e5KXqZiozQ.one_liner: Redistributes the second chunk's data-parallel workload across the DP group to balance MoE prefill under chunk pipelining.
e5KXqZiozQ.problem: In DP-EP deployment of MoE prefill with long, variable requests, severe DP imbalance arises from two synchronous all-to-all communication barriers and degrades performance.
e5KXqZiozQ.method: ChunkBalance, built on two-chunk splitting and compute-communication overlap, redistributes the DP workloads of the second chunk across the DP group so workloads across chunks compensate for one another. It operates offline, combines with request-level scheduling and heterogeneous parallelism, and hides its state-migration overhead by self-overlapping.
e5KXqZiozQ.key_idea: With chunk pipelining there is no synchronization barrier inside the DP stage, so the second chunk's DP workloads can be moved across ranks to offset imbalance from the first chunk.
e5KXqZiozQ.evidence: Experiments on synthetic workloads (text truncated) across three models, including with TP/PP enabled (per reviews).
e5KXqZiozQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the DP imbalance problem is clearly defined and the method is simple and practical, needing no extra GPUs, expert replication, or EP kernel changes, and combining with request scheduling and TP/PP.
e5KXqZiozQ.main_concern: Baselines and attribution of gains are unclear, the evaluation uses synthetic padded workloads, and the design is limited to two-chunk pipelining.

sLpTzI6XxI.one_liner: Cuts end-to-end overhead of history-based speculative rollout in MoE RL by bounding draft length and reusing verification probabilities.
sLpTzI6XxI.problem: History-based speculative rollout saves generation time, but expensive actor verification, redundant old-log-probability computation, and actor drift offset the savings, especially for MoE models.
sLpTzI6XxI.method: HiGAP adaptively bounds historical draft lengths, uses verification probabilities to partially bypass old-log-probability recomputation, and counters history staleness through post-update probability caching and advantage-guided history updates.
sLpTzI6XxI.key_idea: Optimize the full RL pipeline around history reuse: bound draft length, reuse verification probabilities in place of old-log-probability recomputation, and refresh stale histories by advantage.
sLpTzI6XxI.evidence: Three MoE models and one dense model compared with vanilla GRPO and SPEC-RL on nine mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
sLpTzI6XxI.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, reduces step time by 11.6% and improves throughput by 12.7% over vanilla GRPO while improving the average score by 12.3 points across nine mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
sLpTzI6XxI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree HiGAP gives consistent end-to-end step-time reductions across MoE actors where rollout-only speculation falls short, with a useful timing breakdown and low-overhead history reuse.
sLpTzI6XxI.main_concern: On-policy correctness is not established, since the acceptance rule and the effect of cached probabilities and advantage-selected histories on the sampling distribution are unspecified, and the accuracy gains lack controls.

1jCtiCG5Hb.one_liner: Scores a sample's reasoning quality from geometric signatures of layer-wise hidden-state trajectories in a low-dimensional reasoning subspace.
1jCtiCG5Hb.problem: A model's reasoning quality is rarely legible from its surface output, and prior work overlooks how reasoning evolves across layers.
1jCtiCG5Hb.method: CUBE tracks the reasoning trajectory in a low-dimensional reasoning subspace, identifies characteristic cross-layer transformations, and summarizes them with geometric signatures, used in CUBE-Eval (label-free assessment) and CUBE-Selector (flagging low-quality samples for targeted training).
1jCtiCG5Hb.key_idea: Track hidden states across layers inside a reasoning subspace and summarize the trajectory with geometric signatures, where concise and direct trajectories indicate better reasoning.
1jCtiCG5Hb.evidence: Experiments across models and domains (mathematical reasoning, code generation, and multi-hop question answering per reviews), including a fixed-size data-selection experiment.
1jCtiCG5Hb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the geometric signatures compact and interpretable and the evaluation across models, domains, and a data-selection application broader than a single-task demonstration.
1jCtiCG5Hb.main_concern: The interpretation as reasoning quality is weakly supported because the projection is trained on outcome labels, so the signal may reflect correctness, and stronger supervised baselines on terminal or pooled hidden states are missing.

gb9trSifkT.one_liner: Rotates latent token vectors with a secret orthogonal key for equivariant server inference, then audits leakage via rotation invariants.
gb9trSifkT.problem: Failure of a no-key decoder is not sufficient evidence of representation privacy, since rotation-invariant quantities may still leak information.
gb9trSifkT.method: The client rotates latent token vectors with a secret orthogonal transform, a rotation-equivariant server computes on them for any key without retraining, and the client decrypts returned features; they then test leakage from norms, pairwise similarities, and Gram matrices under closed-reference auxiliary knowledge.
gb9trSifkT.key_idea: Rotation-equivariant server layers let one server process any orthogonal key, but norms, similarities, and Gram matrices are invariant under rotation and so remain observable.
gb9trSifkT.evidence: Controlled Food-101 experiments comparing salted or input-protected rotation with noise-only perturbation, plus additional leakage experiments that are cut off in the available abstract.
gb9trSifkT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is honest about scope, stating its leakage results are closed-reference and that no mechanism gives a formal privacy guarantee, and that the equivariant server design is clean.
gb9trSifkT.main_concern: Novelty is unclear because the leakage results follow from the known rotation invariance of norms and Gram matrices, the introduction cites no prior work, and many symbols are undefined.

odUbsN8hMU.one_liner: Explains why on-policy learning reduces forgetting as implicit rehearsal, formalized by a Selection, Function, and Persistence (SFP) framework.
odUbsN8hMU.problem: The mechanism by which on-policy new-task updates preserve old capabilities is insufficiently understood beyond mode-seeking or KL-based explanations.
odUbsN8hMU.method: Proposes that the current policy carries previously learned behaviors into newly generated responses, so new-task feedback can reinforce them without replaying old data. The SFP framework analyzes which historical contributions updates reinforce (Selection), how they connect to old-task capability (Function), and how their effects evolve as policy and data change together (Persistence).
odUbsN8hMU.key_idea: Retention arises because the policy's own new-task trajectories contain old behaviors that new-task rewards reinforce, and SFP derives conditions under which this reinforcement persists.
odUbsN8hMU.evidence: Derived conditions under which reinforcing historical behavior improves retention after further training, plus controlled intervention experiments in language models (Math and Code settings, AIME pass@128 per reviewers) and control reinforcement learning.
odUbsN8hMU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find implicit rehearsal an interesting perspective and value the distinction between historical behavior being expressed and being useful for the old task, studied through controlled interventions.
odUbsN8hMU.main_concern: The experiments do not fully establish the mechanism: reducing historical expression also changes overall policy movement (TARGET shows 3.55-6.35 times larger policy KL than SHUFFLED) and its link to old-task performance is weak.

jJVJZqm1pc.one_liner: Compares one long PPO run against two- and four-candidate splits with validation selection under a shared accounted training budget.
jJVJZqm1pc.problem: It is unclear whether a fixed budget for delivering one LM agent is better spent on one long RL run or on several shorter runs followed by selection.
jJVJZqm1pc.method: On Qwen2.5-1.5B and SmolLM2-1.7B with one PPO text-game recipe, they compare paired long-run and split allocations against a calibrated reference budget, seal selection before independent evaluation, and evaluate every candidate to separate selection loss from the delivered gap.
jJVJZqm1pc.key_idea: Charge training plus selection costs to a calibrated reference budget and evaluate every candidate after sealing selection, so selection loss and delivered gap are measured separately.
jJVJZqm1pc.evidence: Qwen2.5-1.5B and SmolLM2-1.7B on one PPO text-game recipe with block-paired comparisons, an independent pool, and a registered reserved-pool check.
jJVJZqm1pc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is practical and the sealing plus evaluate-every-candidate protocol is a useful design, with the four-way splitting deficit holding across both models, the reserved pool, and block deletions.
jJVJZqm1pc.main_concern: Candidate count is confounded with each candidate's training horizon and learning-rate schedule, and the small reference budget leaves four-way candidates under-trained, so the deficit may not generalize.

05lGoopIpp.one_liner: TaoGraph builds task-oriented scene graphs from multi-view observations using task-conditioned spatial features and change-aware procedure distillation.
05lGoopIpp.problem: Generic spatial representations lack task-aware adaptation, and conventional graph supervision lacks procedural guidance for inferring action prerequisites and valid action orders.
05lGoopIpp.method: Semantics-Induced Spatial Reorganization (SISR) modulates generic spatial features by task instruction and scene semantics, and Change-Aware Procedure Distillation (CAPD) distills procedure-enriched graph predictions guided by discrepancies between two graphs.
05lGoopIpp.key_idea: Modulate generic spatial features by task instruction and scene semantics, and supervise graphs with procedure-enriched predictions distilled using discrepancies between two graphs.
05lGoopIpp.evidence: Graph reconstruction (Node, Spatial and Edge F1) and action-order planning metrics compared with open- and closed-source VLMs, with ablations and external evaluation on BLINK and MMSI-Bench (per reviews).
05lGoopIpp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the two modules a coherent, straightforward response to the two identified limitations, with clear writing and strong experimental improvements.
05lGoopIpp.main_concern: The comparison is limited (original VLMs and one prior method, no specialized scene-graph methods), and gains may reflect fine-tuning to the output format rather than better spatial knowledge.

AUvIm4pym9.one_liner: LVM learns per-instance representative metrics once, then forms each iteration's metric from them with basis functions, with convergence guarantees.
AUvIm4pym9.problem: Learned variable metrics for proximal splitting would need an expensive network evaluation at every iteration and are hard to make satisfy the conditions the theory imposes on the whole infinite sequence of metrics.
AUvIm4pym9.method: A network generates a few representative metrics once per problem instance, and each iteration's metric is obtained by combining them with basis functions of the normalized iteration index. Convergence is proved for proximal gradient with a quadratic term and for PDHG under a mild spectral condition ensured by rescaling the representative metrics.
AUvIm4pym9.key_idea: Form each iteration's metric as the inverse of a convex combination of inverse representative metrics, reducing the infinite-sequence conditions to conditions on a few metrics.
AUvIm4pym9.evidence: Deblurring and inpainting experiments (wavelet-sparse and TV restoration per reviews) comparing iteration counts and computation time, plus convergence proofs.
AUvIm4pym9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the construction clean and provably convergent, with training separated from the convergence guarantee and a single network evaluation per instance.
AUvIm4pym9.main_concern: The practical benefit is weakly supported (untuned FISTA needs fewer iterations at 10^-6 in both proximal-gradient tasks), the guarantee does not strictly cover the implemented rescaling, and scope is limited to classical restoration models.

tSg3SQEBMa.one_liner: Plug-in Bayesian module placing a Brownian-bridge Gaussian-process prior on deformation trajectories to quantify aleatoric uncertainty of pretrained registration models.
tSg3SQEBMa.problem: Prior uncertainty methods for registration focus on pairwise registration and do not model posterior uncertainty over spatiotemporal deformation trajectories in time-series image registration.
tSg3SQEBMa.method: BridgeUQ uses a hierarchical Gaussian-process prior (Brownian bridge with an inverse-Gamma hyperprior on the diffusion variance) around the predicted registration, an energy-based likelihood from the pretrained objective, and an amortized MAP scheme with conditional diffusion sampling to approximate the posterior, without retraining.
tSg3SQEBMa.key_idea: Sample deformation trajectories from a Brownian-bridge prior centered on the pretrained prediction, weighted by an energy likelihood derived from the registration objective.
tSg3SQEBMa.evidence: Cardiac and brain MRI datasets on widely used registration networks (abstract truncated before results).
tSg3SQEBMa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling uncertainty over whole deformation trajectories with a bridge prior centered on an existing prediction is well chosen, suits cardiac cycles, and makes the plug-in design practical.
tSg3SQEBMa.main_concern: The sigma-update (inference) equations are inconsistent with the stated model (a spurious gradient term and a dimension mismatch), and the experiments do not fully substantiate the claimed advantages.

UFhrCgyAS1.one_liner: Shared latent maps images and EEG/MEG/fMRI responses with per-participant heads and a consistency tie, enabling cross-participant response translation.
UFhrCgyAS1.problem: It is untested whether visual encoding and decoding share one interchangeable latent, such that one participant's neural response can be read as another participant's response.
UFhrCgyAS1.method: BiSURE maps images and EEG, MEG, and fMRI responses into a common latent from which the stimulus is retrieved and each participant's response is predicted, keeping private interfaces per instrument and participant. A single consistency term ties the image-derived and brain-derived routes.
UFhrCgyAS1.key_idea: One consistency term ties the image-derived and brain-derived latent routes, so a response from one participant passes through the shared latent to another participant's response head.
UFhrCgyAS1.evidence: Cross-participant and EEG-to-MEG translation, a latent-tie ablation, and retrieval and encoding comparisons against specialist models on three recording instruments.
UFhrCgyAS1.claimed_gains: Cross-participant translation reaches 87--96% of the level from the image itself, EEG-to-MEG reaches 84%, without the latent tie translation falls to at most 6%, and the tie improves encoding by 15--31%.
UFhrCgyAS1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the latent-tie ablation and cross-participant response prediction convincingly show the learned latent is interchangeable, with strong performance across three brain modalities.
UFhrCgyAS1.main_concern: Generality is limited (all participants seen in training, no fMRI translation, unclear benefit of combining three modalities), and one reviewer found the writing hard to follow.

lDgW053QTz.one_liner: Sub-10M speech recognizer sharing codewords by acoustic sensitivity, spending saved storage on compact bidirectional GRU decoders and local recovery modules.
lDgW053QTz.problem: Robust multi-domain ASR within a sub-10M-entry, 10 MB budget is hard because autoregressive decoders add vocabulary and cache overhead and uniform compression degrades deep acoustic representations.
lDgW053QTz.method: Guided by nonblank acoustic sensitivity, AcuFormer keeps full encoder depth and width through short-vector codeword sharing, then reallocates saved storage into compact bidirectional GRU decoders reusing acoustic token embeddings, targeted local recovery modules, and a blank-invariant prior for multi-view selection.
lDgW053QTz.key_idea: Use CTC nonblank sensitivity to decide where to share codewords while keeping encoder depth, and reinvest the saved parameters in decoders and local repair.
lDgW053QTz.evidence: All seven domains of the OpenASR benchmark against same-recipe INT4 baselines and public models over six times its size, plus profiling on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W.
lDgW053QTz.claimed_gains: AcuFormer achieves 9.95% average WER under three-view decoding and 9.97% under real-time confidence routing within 9.83M stored entries and a 9.97 MB footprint, breaking the 10% error threshold below 10 MB.
lDgW053QTz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a strong small model for its size, using targeted compression and reinvestment of saved parameters to reach good multi-domain WER on edge hardware.
lDgW053QTz.main_concern: The comparison is confounded by training data and decoding, since baselines were trained on LibriSpeech only while AcuFormer starts from a Conformer pretrained on thousands of hours, so the claimed 59% gain is not attributed to the proposed methods.

TSD5fQ0qJP.one_liner: Samples the sequence-level power distribution with stochastic beam search scored by one-token lookahead, giving k reasoning candidates per decode.
TSD5fQ0qJP.problem: Sequence-level power sampling sharpens a base model like RL does without a verifier, dataset, or weight update, but the power distribution is not autoregressive and MCMC sampling costs much time per candidate.
TSD5fQ0qJP.method: Shows stochastic beam search samples the power distribution (proportional to p^(1/beta)) exactly once every prefix is scored by its power-weighted subtree mass, and estimates that mass with a one-token lookahead. It returns k candidates without replacement from one batched decode at about the base model's cost per candidate.
TSD5fQ0qJP.key_idea: Score each prefix in stochastic beam search by its power-weighted subtree mass, estimated with one-token lookahead, so beam sampling matches the power distribution.
TSD5fQ0qJP.evidence: Three models evaluated on MATH500, HumanEval and GPQA Diamond against MCMC power sampling and GRPO (abstract truncated); reviewers cite Table 2 timing of 77 seconds for eight candidates versus 295 seconds for one MCMC sample.
TSD5fQ0qJP.claimed_gains: More accurate than MCMC power sampling and GRPO on single-shot accuracy at about the base model's cost per candidate; the remaining numbers are cut off in the abstract.
TSD5fQ0qJP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that linking power sampling to stochastic beam search is a good idea that returns distinct candidates in one pass at far lower cost per candidate than MCMC.
TSD5fQ0qJP.main_concern: The comparison looks unfair because PoBS votes over 8 candidates while baselines use a single sample, so gains may come from voting rather than the sampler; the proof of Theorem 2 is also questioned.

BXWfMwBFFz.one_liner: Compares attention and SSMs via belief geometry, decomposing in-context learning into evidence assembly, belief maintenance, and addressing.
BXWfMwBFFz.problem: Comparisons of Transformers and state-space models are mostly empirical, and existing theoretical analyses are task-specific or architecturally restricted.
BXWfMwBFFz.method: Starts from a generalized in-context linear regression formulation with cumulative Bayes regret as the measure, abstracts three capabilities (evidence assembly, belief maintenance, addressing), and studies three cases that isolate them: stationary aggregation kernels, positional assembly, and content addressing.
BXWfMwBFFz.key_idea: Decompose sequential Bayesian prediction into evidence assembly, belief maintenance, and addressing, and derive regret and memory or width bounds for each architecture class.
BXWfMwBFFz.evidence: Theorems on three cases plus experiments with LLaMA-type Transformers and Mamba-2 on a linear-regression testbed showing the predicted trade-offs also appear beyond the analytically tractable classes.
BXWfMwBFFz.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers (SSMs attain optimal regret over stationary aggregation kernels, SSMs have a memory advantage for positional assembly, and softmax attention has an exponential width advantage over sigmoid-selective SSMs for content addressing).
BXWfMwBFFz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework gives a clear, rigorous way to separate three capabilities and yields concrete regret and resource bounds, with experiments that isolate each capability.
BXWfMwBFFz.main_concern: Conclusions are narrower than the framing: the strongest results hold only for restricted classes (one-layer linear attention, fixed-transition SSMs), hybrids are not analyzed, and no unifying takeaway is given.

RMYW3cs1PU.one_liner: Trains coding agents to explore diverse repairs and verify patches against their reverted tree via weighted SFT and verifier RL.
RMYW3cs1PU.problem: Extra inference compute helps coding agents only if attempts cover diverse repair locations and edits and agent-written tests reliably select a correct patch, yet location diversity is narrow, edit diversity is unexploited, and self-written tests accept many incorrect patches.
RMYW3cs1PU.method: A test-time procedure directs search by execution feedback and scores each patch against its own reverted tree. Training moves these behaviors into the policy through weighted SFT, then an RL objective that trains the verifier against gold-labeled repairs and incorrect variants, crediting the assertions that detect them.
RMYW3cs1PU.key_idea: Credit the individual generated assertions that reject incorrect repair variants, so the policy learns to write discriminating verification tests alongside diverse repairs.
RMYW3cs1PU.evidence: SWE-bench Verified with 270 issues held out from SFT and RL training, a diagnostic study, frozen-candidate verifier comparisons, and transfer evaluations according to reviews.
RMYW3cs1PU.claimed_gains: Raises single-attempt success from 31.8% to 42.8% and eight-attempt success from 46.8% to 60.8% (TL;DR); on the 270 held-out issues pass@1 reaches 43.0% and pass@8 60.7%, and verifier precision rises from 26.8% to 41.7%.
RMYW3cs1PU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating candidate coverage (oracle@8) from correct-candidate selection is useful and that held-out gains in pass@1, pass@8, and verifier precision are substantial.
RMYW3cs1PU.main_concern: Evaluation hygiene is weak: training and test issues both come from SWE-bench Verified, method development used all 500 issues including the 270 test issues, and 180 test issues come from repositories seen in training.

Q529BQpfbS.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,202 tasks testing whether agents follow evolving rules over 300k-1M-token histories, graded deterministically via a two-layer graph.
Q529BQpfbS.problem: No benchmark systematically tests whether an agent with memory keeps a correct picture of current rules across hundreds of sessions without falling back on stale information.
Q529BQpfbS.method: A two-layer graph representation tracks the evolving rules as unambiguous current states, enabling deterministic task annotation without an LLM judge. They build 100 episodes across 6 agent settings with 300k-1M-token records and 10-15 graded tasks each, drawn from a pool of over 20,000 tasks.
Q529BQpfbS.key_idea: Keep defeated rules stored in a two-layer graph and recompute the current rule state with a solver, so tool actions can be graded deterministically.
Q529BQpfbS.evidence: 8 backbone models, with 2 of them paired with 4 memory frameworks (middleware and self-evolving) and compared against a simple heuristic baseline.
Q529BQpfbS.claimed_gains: State violation rates range from 31% to 83% across flash-tier models, frontier models do not uniformly outperform flash-tier ones, and all four memory frameworks incur more violations and complete fewer tasks than a simple heuristic baseline.
Q529BQpfbS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the deterministic, judge-free, audited grading of actions under revised rule state fills a real gap and the full-context control is useful.
Q529BQpfbS.main_concern: Headline comparisons rest on single runs whose differences fall within the paper's own noise, and the memory-framework baselines appear under-provisioned.

pLMs1pNTwD.one_liner: Studies recursive tabular foundation models and analyzes refinement steps through attention-induced Gaussian-process kernel surrogates and marginal likelihood.
pLMs1pNTwD.problem: Most tabular foundation models perform inference in a single computational pass, which may limit their ability to capture complex relationships in the context.
pLMs1pNTwD.method: Builds recursive TFMs that repeatedly revisit the context and refine predictions through latent recursion. On regression, fits attention-induced kernel predictors that reproduce the networks' predictions and tracks how the induced GP marginal likelihood changes across recursive steps.
pLMs1pNTwD.key_idea: Fit attention-induced kernel (GP) surrogates to each recursive step's predictions and read refinement as rising marginal likelihood, trading data fit against model complexity.
pLMs1pNTwD.evidence: Regression experiments with kernel-predictor surrogates and GP marginal-likelihood analysis; reviews add classification experiments, several architectures and recursion settings, and a comparable pretraining budget.
pLMs1pNTwD.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports only that recursive refinement typically improves the marginal likelihood of the induced GP surrogates.
pLMs1pNTwD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the link between recursive computation in tabular foundation models and Bayesian model selection (balancing data fit and complexity) an interesting question, and one calls the experiments sound and reasonably extensive.
pLMs1pNTwD.main_concern: The model-selection argument holds only for the kernel surrogate rather than the actual recursive model, and the marginal likelihood also improves for the non-recursive baseline.
