QT26BnHo6y.one_liner: Maps how plausibility fine-tuning moves four VLM readout channels depending on where the training loss is applied.
QT26BnHo6y.problem: Prior work reports plausibility fine-tuning gains on one readout, usually accuracy, which can hide that other readouts of the same model do not improve.
QT26BnHo6y.method: On ImPhysible, a rendered testbed of matched normal and violated images, one model's judgment is read on four channels (a 0 to 100 score, an answer-token logit, the generated verdict, and a hidden-state probe) while varying which channel and condition the training loss passes through.
QT26BnHo6y.key_idea: Compare training variants that apply the loss to different readout channels and conditions to map which cells improve and which stay at chance or fall.
QT26BnHo6y.evidence: The ImPhysible rendered testbed, mainly with Qwen2.5-VL-7B per reviews, using score, verdict and representation-alignment training variants with three seeds for several and held-out-domain tests.
QT26BnHo6y.claimed_gains: A score reward lifts score pair-rank accuracy from 0.464 to 0.685 while pushing the logit of the same answers from 0.499 to 0.385 on the nine pooled domains.
QT26BnHo6y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reading several channels addresses a real blind spot of single-accuracy reporting and that the central message is clear.
QT26BnHo6y.main_concern: Evidence is thin: experiments rely mostly on one model and mostly single seeds, and the comparisons confound the supervised channel with optimization method and training setup.

eZTenWzgyV.one_liner: Consistency-distilled dimers and joint sequence–structure resampling train an all-atom flow model for protein binder co-design.
eZTenWzgyV.problem: Jointly generating protein sequences and structures does not by itself ensure that they are mutually compatible.
eZTenWzgyV.method: CODesign trains on approximately 105,000 consistency-distilled dimers using a joint flow model over sequences, backbones, and local atomic configurations. Consistency-aware resampling iteratively revises sequences and side chains.
eZTenWzgyV.key_idea: Combine consistency-filtered dimer training with trajectory-level joint resampling of sequences and local atomic states.
eZTenWzgyV.evidence: In silico protein-target and ligand-target binder evaluations include ablations of the distilled dataset and resampling mechanism.
eZTenWzgyV.claimed_gains: The abstract reports that the distilled dataset increases performance by 70.9%.
eZTenWzgyV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong in silico binder-design results and the usefulness of addressing sequence–structure consistency.
eZTenWzgyV.main_concern: The methodological advance over existing co-design and distillation pipelines is insufficiently isolated from the benefit of an additional complex-specific dataset.

3SkVxoAkR0.one_liner: Hand-geometry heatmaps modulate visual features to disambiguate pointing targets in egocentric videos.
3SkVxoAkR0.problem: Multimodal language models struggle to resolve pointing references amid spatial and dynamic distractors.
3SkVxoAkR0.method: PointConfusion organizes a target-selection benchmark around five pointing-ambiguity categories. PointMod predicts spatial reference heatmaps from hand geometry and uses them to modulate visual representations without adding gesture tokens.
3SkVxoAkR0.key_idea: Convert hand geometry into spatial reference heatmaps that directly modulate visual features before target selection.
3SkVxoAkR0.evidence: PointConfusion contains 5,000 synthetic and 160 real-world egocentric videos, with category-wise comparisons, heatmap ablations, and text-only controls.
3SkVxoAkR0.claimed_gains: PointMod-8B reaches 88.33% synthetic and 68.13% real-world target-selection accuracy, improving over task-fine-tuned InternVL3.5-8B by 8.13 and 12.71 percentage points.
3SkVxoAkR0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled ambiguity taxonomy and simple, effective use of explicit spatial guidance.
3SkVxoAkR0.main_concern: Reviewers question how well the controlled synthetic ambiguities and hand-based guidance transfer to realistic pointing conditions.

JudpgR1CQ3.one_liner: Matched rollout contexts supply higher-quality action chunks as corrective targets for failed flow-matching robot actions.
JudpgR1CQ3.problem: Reward- and preference-based post-training identifies good behavior without specifying corrections for failed actions.
JudpgR1CQ3.method: RedFlow groups action chunks by estimated task progress and proprioceptive state, assigns signed quality scores, and aggregates better chunks into corrective targets. Offline training reinforces good chunks, suppresses poor ones, and redirects correctable failures.
JudpgR1CQ3.key_idea: Match rollout chunks by execution context and use higher-quality actions in each group to redirect failed chunks.
JudpgR1CQ3.evidence: Experiments cover four LIBERO suites and three real-robot tasks, with ablations of context matching and action-level correction.
JudpgR1CQ3.claimed_gains: Average LIBERO success rises from 56.2% to 68.2%, exceeding AWR at 62.3% by 5.9 percentage points.
JudpgR1CQ3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extracting explicit action corrections from mixed-quality offline rollouts without further human intervention or online collection.
JudpgR1CQ3.main_concern: Matching only progress and proprioception can ignore object poses and contact states, producing inappropriate corrective action targets.

tKztB3lRwI.one_liner: Separates modality-specific and cross-modal sparse features to score visual grounding for preference optimization.
tKztB3lRwI.problem: Language-model judges can favor linguistic style over visual grounding when labeling responses for hallucination reduction.
tKztB3lRwI.method: MA-SAE partitions sparse features into vision-specific, text-specific, and cross-modal banks. A grounding score from cross-modal features labels response preferences for DPO and related tuning methods.
tKztB3lRwI.key_idea: Modality-partitioned sparse autoencoders isolate cross-modal features whose grounding scores determine preferred responses.
tKztB3lRwI.evidence: Experiments cover three multimodal backbones, five feature-quality metrics, three hallucination benchmarks, and DPO, mDPO, and on-policy preference tuning.
tKztB3lRwI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful grounding signals and consistent hallucination reductions across multiple models and preference-optimization settings.
tKztB3lRwI.main_concern: The grounding score's ability to reliably rank semantic correctness, beyond shared object content, remains insufficiently validated.

c2kIMaUCXj.one_liner: Shares one fast-weight memory across layers so test-time updates propagate through both sequence time and network depth.
c2kIMaUCXj.problem: Layer-private test-time memories prevent writes from one layer from directly informing other layers across chunks.
c2kIMaUCXj.method: uTTT lets all layers read and update shared memory while keeping layer-specific backbone parameters. Its MoE variant routes token heads to shared experts, while its dense variant uses the entire memory at every layer.
c2kIMaUCXj.key_idea: A shared fast-weight state recurs across chunks and layers, allowing deep-layer writes to influence shallow-layer reads in later chunks.
c2kIMaUCXj.evidence: Language-model experiments compare 124M and 760M bounded-state models at matched state and active compute, alongside routed and dense novel-view-synthesis evaluations.
c2kIMaUCXj.claimed_gains: uTTT-MoE reaches 15.5 and 27.9 RULER accuracy at 124M and 760M, gains of 2.6 and 2.1 points, while view-23 PSNR improves by 0.92 dB for routed and 0.76 dB for dense models.
c2kIMaUCXj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple shared-memory design and targeted comparisons and analyses of cross-layer information flow.
c2kIMaUCXj.main_concern: Retrieval gains weaken at longer contexts and larger evaluated scale, leaving practical long-context benefits uncertain.

4v3uOW1W9q.one_liner: Develops robot toolboxes through simulated experiments, then uses physical trials to revise the simulator and screen repairs.
4v3uOW1W9q.problem: Direct code generation lacks sufficient physical understanding, while extensive real-world trial-and-error incurs substantial cost.
4v3uOW1W9q.method: SimEX first runs open-ended simulation probes and optimization to build reusable robot capabilities. A few physical trials then guide joint toolbox and simulator adaptation, with corrected simulations diagnosing failures and screening repairs.
4v3uOW1W9q.key_idea: Simulation builds a robot toolbox, and physical feedback revises the simulator used to test candidate toolbox repairs.
4v3uOW1W9q.evidence: Evaluation includes sim-to-sim settings and physical manipulation tasks such as towel folding, barcode scanning, and plate manipulation, with stage ablations.
4v3uOW1W9q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find simulation-led capability development followed by few-trial real-world adaptation practically promising.
4v3uOW1W9q.main_concern: Missing procedural details, including toolbox selection and iteration mechanics, prevent reliable reproduction.

f9p9jdJJrE.one_liner: Distills a frozen teacher steered by activation contrasts between verified successful and unsuccessful reasoning trajectories.
f9p9jdJJrE.problem: Privileged reference information alone does not ensure useful token-level supervision throughout long reasoning responses.
f9p9jdJJrE.method: ACSD constructs a steering vector from activation contrasts between verified correct trajectories and remaining trajectories. A frozen base-model teacher applies this vector at each position and supervises student-generated prefixes through next-token distributions.
f9p9jdJJrE.key_idea: Success-conditioned activation contrasts define a reusable teacher steering direction whose token distributions supervise on-policy student prefixes.
f9p9jdJJrE.evidence: Experiments evaluate five models on four mathematical benchmarks, plus LiveCodeBench v6, direction perturbations, alternative contrasts, and cross-dataset reuse.
f9p9jdJJrE.claimed_gains: On DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B, ACSD reaches 71.9% mean mathematical accuracy and 70.9% LiveCodeBench v6 pass@12, versus 69.0% and 66.3% for reference-conditioned OPSD.
f9p9jdJJrE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple reusable direction, lack of inference intervention, and gains across multiple models.
f9p9jdJJrE.main_concern: The activation contrast may capture positional, stylistic, or response-length effects rather than improved reasoning, and current analyses do not disentangle them.

DqMk93PaTC.one_liner: Predicts instruction-conditioned corrections to residual feature components and supervises their cumulative composition for video retrieval.
DqMk93PaTC.problem: Global target alignment can retrieve visually similar videos that fail to satisfy the requested semantic modification.
DqMk93PaTC.method: MORSE decomposes reference features into ordered additive residual components and predicts instruction-conditioned corrections using each component's residual context. Shared-codebook target decompositions supervise cumulative transformed features without intermediate change labels.
DqMk93PaTC.key_idea: Instruction-conditioned residual corrections alter ordered feature components, while target decompositions constrain their cumulative composition.
DqMk93PaTC.evidence: Experiments span three composed-video-retrieval benchmarks, including FineCVR-1M and TF-CoVR, with ablations of component inputs and refinement.
DqMk93PaTC.claimed_gains: MORSE reports relative improvements of 17.81% in R@1 on FineCVR-1M and 10.25% in mAP@50 on TF-CoVR.
DqMk93PaTC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the framework yields competitive retrieval results with useful component ablations.
DqMk93PaTC.main_concern: The semantic meaning of residual components and their suitability for coordinated modifications remain insufficiently explained.

QGBpTRMOBc.one_liner: Distills an interleaved visual-text reasoning teacher into a student that reasons textually without generating intermediate images.
QGBpTRMOBc.problem: Intermediate images or latent visual tokens can introduce errors and interfere with textual reasoning.
QGBpTRMOBc.method: V2T trains a teacher on interleaved visual and textual chains of thought, then distills its logits with ground-truth textual supervision. Optional attention transfer and bounding-box-guided reinforcement learning provide additional grounding.
QGBpTRMOBc.key_idea: A visually privileged teacher transfers token distributions and optional region attention to a student trained for textual reasoning.
QGBpTRMOBc.evidence: Experiments span multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks, a held-out set, and a broader visual evaluation suite, including comparisons with visual-reasoning baselines.
QGBpTRMOBc.claimed_gains: V2T reports average accuracy gains of 14.3% on a held-out set and 3.7% on the broader visual suite, plus up to 42× speedup.
QGBpTRMOBc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical idea of retaining visual reasoning benefits through distillation while simplifying inference.
QGBpTRMOBc.main_concern: Missing or insufficiently specified matched-data baselines leave the source of gains, particularly attention supervision, unclear.

HIfy7iJvJX.one_liner: Autoregressively deletes and adds mesh faces using bidirectional draft context to repair topology while preserving untouched regions.
HIfy7iJvJX.problem: Generated artisan meshes can contain local defects, while full regeneration may discard desirable topology or create new errors.
HIfy7iJvJX.method: MeshRepair uses a prefix language model to read the draft bidirectionally and generate a deletion phase followed by an addition phase. Its heads select faces to remove and vertices for new faces, adding vertices when necessary.
HIfy7iJvJX.key_idea: A bidirectional mesh prefix conditions autoregressive face-deletion and face-addition edits, passing untouched faces through unchanged.
HIfy7iJvJX.evidence: Benchmarks compare repair tools on scripted defects and held-out MeshCarve- and LATO.2-derived drafts, with edit and connectivity measurements.
HIfy7iJvJX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find sparse explicit edits a natural and practical way to repair local defects while preserving satisfactory mesh regions.
HIfy7iJvJX.main_concern: Evaluation uses ground-truth vertices and generators seen during training, leaving performance on ordinary imperfect or unseen-generator meshes unclear.

B5VdkrAUP4.one_liner: Gated fusion of task-guided histology and spatial-transcriptomics prototype banks with Owen-value attribution predicts clinical outcomes.
B5VdkrAUP4.problem: Integrating co-registered H&E histopathology images and spatial transcriptomics for cohort-level clinical diagnosis and prognosis is difficult under limited patient-level supervision.
B5VdkrAUP4.method: PathoSpatial learns modality-specific morphological and molecular prototype banks through supervised adaptation and cohort-level updates within a multiple-instance learning framework, fusing them via gated attention. It characterizes prototypes biologically and computes grouped Owen values to attribute patient predictions back to specific histological patches and transcriptomic spots.
B5VdkrAUP4.key_idea: Learn modality-specific morphological and transcriptomic prototype banks fused via gated attention and attribute predictions across modalities using Owen values.
B5VdkrAUP4.evidence: Experiments evaluate three cohort-level spatial transcriptomics datasets covering survival prediction, treatment-response classification, and disease-status classification under patient-level splits.
B5VdkrAUP4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that integrating paired H&E histology and spatial transcriptomics through task-guided prototypes and Owen-value attribution addresses a relevant precision-pathology problem with interpretable outputs.
B5VdkrAUP4.main_concern: Reviewers highlight optimistic model-selection bias from choosing checkpoints by peak pooled held-out AUC without an independent validation split, alongside tiny predictive margins over SurvPath and Patch-GCN.

Hm8hHTDcyZ.one_liner: Object-level grouping, cost-aware selection, and budgeted rendering allocate repository evidence to coding-agent contexts.
Hm8hHTDcyZ.problem: Redundant retrieved views can crowd out distinct useful code when final model context is limited.
Hm8hHTDcyZ.method: VITAL-RAG groups retrieved fragments by code object, selects and orders objects by relevance and estimated cost, and renders them under local and global token budgets.
Hm8hHTDcyZ.key_idea: Code-object grouping precedes relevance-and-cost selection and budgeted rendering to control which retrieved evidence reaches the coding model.
Hm8hHTDcyZ.evidence: Evaluation covers 13,121 RepoBench tasks, 460 CoderEval tasks, 355 RepoExec tasks, and 227 reference-bearing RepoClassBench tasks.
Hm8hHTDcyZ.claimed_gains: CoderEval direct-generation pass rates improve by 1.30–2.83 percentage points, while a two-candidate RepoExec workflow reaches 65.63% with Claude Sonnet 4.6 versus 54.65% for the strongest evaluated control.
Hm8hHTDcyZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical context-allocation problem and controlled decomposition of grouping and packing effects.
Hm8hHTDcyZ.main_concern: Reviewers question whether improved evidence-retention metrics establish useful downstream code-generation gains.

52XFLazzqc.one_liner: Automated hypothesis generation and controlled simulations test causal influences on AI-agent behavior.
52XFLazzqc.problem: Causal behavioral evaluation of agents remains manual and labor intensive.
52XFLazzqc.method: Abs2Sim and AEROBAT automate hypothesis generation, experimental design, simulation, behavioral assessment, statistical analysis, and reporting. Matched conditions and validity checks structure the experiments.
52XFLazzqc.key_idea: An automated research pipeline turns a target behavior into hypotheses and controlled simulation experiments with behavioral and statistical assessments.
52XFLazzqc.evidence: For 12 target behaviors, the system tests 73 hypotheses through 1,160 controlled experiments and 22,954 simulation rounds, with human-rating comparisons and model retests.
52XFLazzqc.claimed_gains: Moderate-to-strong statistical evidence emerges for 30 hypotheses.
52XFLazzqc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the integrated behavioral-research pipeline and its efforts to assess experimental validity.
52XFLazzqc.main_concern: Incomplete blinding can expose expected effects or manipulated variables to design and assessment agents, weakening causal interpretation.

XRYCup6Ddo.one_liner: Partner-conditioned cross-attention adapts frozen RNA representations for joint target identification and interaction-site localization.
XRYCup6Ddo.problem: Local-window scoring and independently encoded RNA sequences do not directly address unknown targets and sites in full sequences.
XRYCup6Ddo.method: SnoBench evaluates full-sequence snoRNA interactions using contact-derived annotations and controlled splits. The model applies bidirectional cross-attention with signed base-pairing biases and separate target-compatibility and site-interaction heads.
XRYCup6Ddo.key_idea: Bidirectional cross-attention conditions each RNA representation on its partner, with signed nucleotide-pair biases and granularity-specific prediction heads.
XRYCup6Ddo.evidence: SnoBench contains 9,156 snoRNA-target pairs and 31,790 interaction regions, comparing controlled candidate ranking with complete-sequence target and site prediction.
XRYCup6Ddo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating local discrimination from full-sequence target identification and localization addresses a meaningful evaluation gap.
XRYCup6Ddo.main_concern: Incomplete or inconsistent model details, including discrepancies between the described scoring objective and supplied implementation, impede assessment.

ANJncE9rO4.one_liner: Joint calibration counts any generator error to certify one acceptance gate against all candidate-set routers.
ANJncE9rO4.problem: Input-dependent candidate routing can invalidate selective-risk guarantees established separately for individual label-shortlist generators.
ANJncE9rO4.method: SetGuard-R runs every fixed generator on each labeled calibration image and counts an error when any prediction is wrong. These joint counts certify a shared acceptance rule across routers.
ANJncE9rO4.key_idea: Calibrating a shared gate against union errors across all generators controls selective risk uniformly over input-dependent routing rules.
ANJncE9rO4.evidence: Router-uniform risk and shared-gate proofs accompany Flowers-102 experiments and comparisons across six CLIP systems.
ANJncE9rO4.claimed_gains: At a 10% risk target on held-out Flowers-102, joint counting certifies 44.9% coverage, while separate error bounds certify no positive coverage for the same score.
ANJncE9rO4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a meaningful routing-induced risk problem and useful theory and evidence for joint certification.
ANJncE9rO4.main_concern: The guarantees and experiments assume fixed generators and an unchanged image-label distribution, limiting deployment applicability.

GnJIcgtMXL.one_liner: Entity-property indexes retrieve original episode evidence through query-specific requirements and adaptive memory access.
GnJIcgtMXL.problem: Generic summaries and anonymous chunks make it difficult to recover the correct entities, properties, and supporting conversational evidence.
GnJIcgtMXL.method: EnSIMem organizes interactions into thematic episodes and indexes entity-type-property facts while retaining source turns, temporal metadata, and multimodal fields. It decomposes queries into evidence requirements, aligns them to index properties, and adaptively retrieves original evidence for answering.
GnJIcgtMXL.key_idea: Index entity-property facts as pointers to preserved episode evidence, then retrieve according to decomposed query requirements.
GnJIcgtMXL.evidence: Experiments include LoCoMo and LongMemEval, baseline comparisons, and component ablations on a fixed LoCoMo subset.
GnJIcgtMXL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge strong benchmark results and the usefulness of structured indexing that preserves original evidence.
GnJIcgtMXL.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate the core roles of episode expansion and requirement-aware planning.

QxSKr5cpsJ.one_liner: Projected route candidates carry topological exploration states directly into egocentric views for zero-shot object navigation.
QxSKr5cpsJ.problem: Separating exploration history from visual route choices forces VLMs to reconstruct their correspondence when selecting where to search.
QxSKr5cpsJ.method: MarvisNav maintains a topological graph and projects candidate nodes with their exploration states onto egocentric perception. The VLM jointly evaluates target relevance and local exploration progress to select a route without separate fusion or reranking.
QxSKr5cpsJ.key_idea: Bind topological exploration states directly to projected route candidates in the VLM's egocentric visual input.
QxSKr5cpsJ.evidence: Reported comparisons use the same VLM and measure navigation success, SPL, and call counts, with ablations of alternative memory presentations.
QxSKr5cpsJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find linking exploration states to candidate routes a coherent way to make navigation memory usable.
QxSKr5cpsJ.main_concern: The representational contribution is insufficiently distinguished from prior visual-memory navigation methods through controlled comparisons.

0Ak6YfrqMe.one_liner: Predicts how activation steering shifts linear safety monitors using one backward pass and optimizes monitor-aware steering vectors.
0Ak6YfrqMe.problem: Activation steering vectors that preserve output fluency and task accuracy can silently shift downstream linear activation monitors, causing high false-positive rates or missed detections.
0Ak6YfrqMe.method: The authors predict to first order the score shift that a steering vector induces in a linear activation monitor using a single backward pass per monitor input without running the steered model. They analyze missed-detection and false-alarm conditions under a Gaussian mean-shift model and formulate a monitor-aware steering objective that penalizes predicted monitor score shifts.
0Ak6YfrqMe.key_idea: Uses a first-order Taylor approximation from one backward pass to predict linear-probe score shifts under activation steering and regularizes steering vectors against monitor disruption.
0Ak6YfrqMe.evidence: Evaluated with Gaussian mean-shift analysis and experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and five additional models (1B–32B) across three model families.
0Ak6YfrqMe.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Llama-3.2-3B, the predicted shift has rank correlation 0.972 with the measured shift; a standard difference-of-means vector keeping output KL within 0.05 nats and accuracy loss within 5 points raises monitor FPR by at least 0.2 in 18% of cases, while monitor-aware steering cuts score shift to a quarter of Euclidean steering's.
0Ak6YfrqMe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that quantifying and mitigating the interference between activation steering and linear internal safety monitors addresses a practically relevant deployment issue.
0Ak6YfrqMe.main_concern: Open-ended generation evaluations of the joint monitor-aware steering method are inconclusive regarding task-level quality trade-offs, and one reviewer noted dense, unnatural writing terminology.

ouLvKKPNOH.one_liner: Steers compositional diffusion toward collision-free pure modes using a model-intrinsic terminal reward approximated via denoising errors.
ouLvKKPNOH.problem: Diffusion models fail on multi-concept prompts due to mode collision with single-concept distributions, and heuristic intermediate-timestep correctors do not guarantee sampling from pure modes in the final clean data space.
ouLvKKPNOH.method: TILT (Test-time model-Intrinsic reward aLignment via Tilting) formulates collision-free pure-mode generation as terminal reward alignment at t=0 rather than a ratio of intermediate noised distributions. Using a variational approximation, it estimates the joint-versus-individual concept likelihood ratio from the diffusion model's own denoising errors at the predicted clean sample and applies a Jacobian-free gradient update during sampling.
ouLvKKPNOH.key_idea: Defines a terminal t=0 pure-mode contrast reward estimated from the generator's own denoising errors on the Tweedie clean estimate and steers sampling via Jacobian-free guidance.
ouLvKKPNOH.evidence: Evaluated on compositional text-to-image and text-to-audio diffusion generation benchmarks against CO3 and FKS baselines.
ouLvKKPNOH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the observation that mode collision should be defined at terminal data time t=0 rather than intermediate noisy steps and value using the generator's own denoising errors without an external reward model.
ouLvKKPNOH.main_concern: The practical algorithm relies on a point-estimate Tweedie expectation and drops the score Jacobian (following DPS and MPGD) where smoothness assumptions may fail, yielding modest empirical gains at higher inference cost.

FpLkYRSl73.one_liner: Coordinates training-free progressive high-resolution image generation in an orthonormal wavelet domain via noise coupling and scale-time phase matching.
FpLkYRSl73.problem: Progressive high-resolution diffusion pipelines suffer from initialization, sampling-phase, and structural mismatches between coarser parent stages and finer child stages.
FpLkYRSl73.method: WAVEALIGN formulates progressive high-resolution generation as a cross-resolution correspondence problem in a shared orthonormal wavelet representation. It couples sampled noise with a mixed clean anchor for initialization, applies a scale-time conjugacy mapping to query phase-matched parent trajectory references, and selectively guides shared coarse wavelet structures while releasing high-frequency detail synthesis.
FpLkYRSl73.key_idea: Aligns progressive multi-resolution diffusion stages in an orthonormal wavelet basis through coupled noise initialization, scale-time phase matching of parent trajectories, and coarse-subband structural guidance.
FpLkYRSl73.evidence: Evaluated on progressive 1K to 2K to 4K text-to-image generation using FLUX.1-dev against FLUX-based high-resolution baselines.
FpLkYRSl73.claimed_gains: On FLUX.1-dev progressive 1K->2K->4K generation, WAVEALIGN achieves the lowest FID, KID, pFID, and pKID at 4K among evaluated FLUX-based pipelines.
FpLkYRSl73.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified wavelet-based framework for coordinating initialization, temporal phase, and coarse structure across progressive resolution stages clear and well-ablated.
FpLkYRSl73.main_concern: Experiments are restricted to a single FLUX.1-dev backbone without testing SDXL or SD3, and the advantage of dynamic phase-matched parent trajectory queries over simply referencing the final denoised parent image is not directly isolated.

0FaPTsSr9C.one_liner: Stops self-evolving LLM loops via anytime-valid sequential testing and rolls back to the pre-saturation artifact via change-point estimation.
0FaPTsSr9C.problem: Self-evolving LLM systems run for fixed iteration budgets without a principled stopping rule, wasting compute after saturation and risking overfitting to the validation signal in late rounds.
0FaPTsSr9C.method: The authors decouple when to stop evolution from which artifact to output using the per-item paired evaluation outcomes already generated during self-evolution. They construct an online anytime-valid sequential restart detector to halt evolution when progress stalls and solve a change-point estimation problem to roll back and output the artifact from the estimated transition point before overfitting.
0FaPTsSr9C.key_idea: Pairs an anytime-valid sequential restart detector on paired per-item validation outcomes for early stopping with change-point rollback to select the pre-plateau artifact.
0FaPTsSr9C.evidence: Evaluated across two self-evolving frameworks (SkillOpt and GEPA), three LLM families, and five benchmarks including SearchQA, GSM8K, and OfficeQA.
0FaPTsSr9C.claimed_gains: Saves 48.4%–91.6% of tokens across main experiments with no significant difference in unseen-test accuracy (e.g., saving 91.6% tokens with +0.43 pp unseen-test accuracy on SearchQA).
0FaPTsSr9C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the plug-and-play decoupling of stopping detection from change-point artifact rollback and note substantial token savings without losing test accuracy.
0FaPTsSr9C.main_concern: The theoretical martingale guarantee assumes conditional independence across rounds even though the exact same fixed validation set is reused every round, and experiments omit simple patience-based or threshold-based early-stopping baselines.

PY3KXZSSWn.one_liner: Interpolates between reward regression and the projected Bellman equation for estimating task vectors in successor-feature reinforcement learning.
PY3KXZSSWn.problem: In successor-feature reinforcement learning, reward regression and the projected Bellman equation (PBE) generally produce different task-vector estimates with uncharacterized trade-offs between off-policy stability and value-approximation accuracy.
PY3KXZSSWn.method: The authors formalize reward regression and PBE task-vector estimators, prove when they diverge or coincide, and unify them via a continuous interpolation parameter eta. Based on this stability-approximation trade-off, they develop SF-Bellman to estimate task vectors for continual and goal-conditioned reinforcement learning.
PY3KXZSSWn.key_idea: Unifies reward-regression and projected-Bellman-equation task-vector objectives via an interpolation parameter to trade off off-policy stability against value-approximation error in successor features.
PY3KXZSSWn.evidence: Supported by theoretical equivalence and approximation bounds, an illustrative tabular counterexample, and experiments on continual-learning and goal-conditioned control tasks.
PY3KXZSSWn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical clarification and counterexample showing that reward regression and projected Bellman equation task-vector estimators are not interchangeable in successor-feature RL.
PY3KXZSSWn.main_concern: Online experiments test only extreme interpolation values (eta=0, 0.99, 1) without directly measuring training instability or intermediate trade-offs, and theory assumes fixed features and policies under restrictive invertibility conditions.

OiLVLIZy0i.one_liner: Samples vertices independently using Laplace-perturbed degrees to construct large nearly independent sets under noninteractive local edge differential privacy.
OiLVLIZy0i.problem: Under local edge differential privacy, any algorithm guaranteed to output a strictly valid independent set can select at most one vertex.
OiLVLIZy0i.method: The authors relax strict independence by allowing edges between selected vertices as counted defects and design a noninteractive epsilon-local edge-private algorithm that samples vertices independently using Laplace-perturbed node degrees. They prove upper bounds on expected defect count and output size on bounded-degeneracy or sparse graphs and establish a matching asymptotic lower bound on expected defects.
OiLVLIZy0i.key_idea: Perturbs vertex degrees with local Laplace noise and samples vertices independently in a single noninteractive round to maximize set size while bounding edge defects.
OiLVLIZy0i.evidence: Supported by theoretical upper and lower bounds on expected set size and defect count for n-vertex graphs with bounded average degree or degeneracy.
OiLVLIZy0i.claimed_gains: For fixed epsilon>0 on n-vertex graphs with bounded average degree or degeneracy, expected output size is Omega_epsilon(n/log n) with expected defects O_epsilon(n/log^2 n), matching the Omega(n/r^2) defect lower bound at approximation ratio r=Theta(log n).
OiLVLIZy0i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written with clean, self-contained theoretical proofs and a tight lower bound that holds even against centralized edge-DP algorithms.
OiLVLIZy0i.main_concern: On sparse graphs with at most n edges, a trivial graph-blind sampler that selects each vertex independently with probability 1/r using zero privacy budget achieves the exact same asymptotic size and defect bounds, and the purely graph-theoretic scope has limited connection to representation learning.

c9KYUJ6YGW.one_liner: Trains vision-language models for five-stage wafer defect diagnosis using cascaded reward truncation and oracle-clue logit-difference guidance.
c9KYUJ6YGW.problem: Existing wafer defect analysis methods stop at visual pattern localization and classification, leaving root-cause diagnosis and actionable process prevention unaddressed.
c9KYUJ6YGW.method: TRACE formulates wafer defect diagnosis as a five-stage cascade (position, appearance, type, root cause, and prevention) with sequential verification that halts rewards at the first failed stage. During reinforcement learning, a frozen oracle-conditioned snapshot of the policy provides natural-language clues and a dense token-level pointwise mutual-information signal computed from the centered difference between clue-conditioned and unconditioned logits, requiring no teacher at inference.
c9KYUJ6YGW.key_idea: Combines sequential five-stage reward truncation with token-level guidance from the centered logit difference between oracle-clue-conditioned and unconditioned policy snapshots during RL.
c9KYUJ6YGW.evidence: Evaluated on semiconductor wafer defect map diagnosis tasks comparing against vision-language and reasoning baselines.
c9KYUJ6YGW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate extending wafer defect analysis to five-stage root-cause and prevention reasoning and using clue-induced self-guidance during RL without teacher overhead at inference.
c9KYUJ6YGW.main_concern: Core experimental data come from proprietary semiconductor fab production records that cannot be disclosed, preventing external reproduction, and the RL state-action formulation and model-based evaluation grader lack clarity.

ft6eiUcLPk.one_liner: Bounds Byzantine influence in decentralized optimization by assigning softmax aggregation weights based on neighbor models' excess local loss.
ft6eiUcLPk.problem: Byzantine-robust decentralized learning must limit damage from malicious neighbors without discarding high-loss honest updates that provide useful cross-node cooperation under data heterogeneity.
ft6eiUcLPk.method: The authors introduce aggregation budgets that bound the weighted excess local loss of neighbor candidates relative to a node's self-candidate. They propose the Local-Loss Aware Softmax Aggregator (LASA), which assigns positive softmax weights inversely related to local loss without knowing the Byzantine fraction, and derive global stationarity bounds for smooth convex objectives without assuming an honest majority.
ft6eiUcLPk.key_idea: Weights neighbor updates via a temperature-controlled softmax of their evaluated local loss to satisfy an explicit excess-local-loss aggregation budget without an honest-majority assumption.
ft6eiUcLPk.evidence: Supported by global stationarity bounds for smooth convex objectives (and under quadratic growth) and experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 across multiple graph topologies and Byzantine attacks.
ft6eiUcLPk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the aggregation-budget framework well-written and insightful for connecting local-loss control to global stationarity without an honest-majority assumption, showing strong worst-node accuracy under Dissensus attacks.
ft6eiUcLPk.main_concern: Theoretical convergence guarantees are restricted to convex objectives, comparisons omit recent decentralized defenses like Balance and Resist, and experiments lack a controlled ablation isolating the retention of higher-loss candidates from the softmax weighting rule.

7sGDiOzoVT.one_liner: Analyzes confidence ranking in guided masked image generation as implicit cooling and derives a sampling temperature calibration rule.
7sGDiOzoVT.problem: In masked image generation, the advantage of confidence ranking over random position commitment varies with sampling temperature, confounding whether gains come from better positions or modified token value distributions.
7sGDiOzoVT.method: The authors derive a temperature rule for text-to-image models with classifier-free guidance by extending an implicit cooling analysis to multi-step simultaneous commits and temperature-one position scores. They also construct a value-only intervention that draws committed values from the conditional commitment law at random positions.
7sGDiOzoVT.key_idea: Models confidence ranking as implicit temperature cooling on committed token distributions and isolates value changes from position selection by sampling from the conditional commitment law at random positions.
7sGDiOzoVT.evidence: The temperature rule is developed on one text-to-image model and evaluated on three additional models across 12 held-out evaluations, including MMaDA-8B.
7sGDiOzoVT.claimed_gains: On MMaDA-8B, confidence ranking improves FID by up to 51.8 at a high temperature but worsens FID by 14.1 at the best tested temperature for random positions, with a one-sided 95% upper limit of FID gain below 2 across all 12 held-out evaluations after per-sampler temperature calibration, while value-only sampling at random positions reproduces 95–104% of the effect.
7sGDiOzoVT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the rigorous evaluation design with separate temperature calibration and held-out tests, as well as the value-only control experiment that clarifies the role of committed token distributions.
7sGDiOzoVT.main_concern: Reviewers note that position selection and token values remain coupled, full-generation predictions have noticeable errors compared to fixed-state analysis, and confidence intervals are too wide to prove strict equivalence.

i1kAVtxyJY.one_liner: Formulates KL-constrained distributionally robust RLHF under context and joint context-preference shifts with tractable PPO-based algorithms.
i1kAVtxyJY.problem: Standard RLHF relies on static, offline preference data, leaving aligned language models vulnerable to deployment shifts in contexts and user preferences.
i1kAVtxyJY.method: The paper introduces two KL-divergence distributionally robust alignment formulations and corresponding PPO-based algorithms: CoRAL for context shifts with a fixed preference model, and JoRAL for joint context-preference shifts. Using duality, robustness is implemented via per-prompt weights in the PPO objective.
i1kAVtxyJY.key_idea: Reweights per-prompt PPO updates via dual optimization under KL-divergence ambiguity sets over context distributions alone (CoRAL) or joint context-preference distributions (JoRAL).
i1kAVtxyJY.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs establishing O(n^{-1/2}) sample complexity for frozen-backbone last-layer log-linear LLM policies and empirical evaluations on LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct.
i1kAVtxyJY.claimed_gains: Both CoRAL and JoRAL achieve O(n^{-1/2}) sample complexity for the frozen-backbone, last-layer LLM policy class.
i1kAVtxyJY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the distinction between context shift and joint context-preference shift is well formulated, the dual reduction to per-prompt PPO weights is simple to use, and the theoretical guarantees are non-trivial.
i1kAVtxyJY.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the main empirical evaluation relies primarily on a small 1B model, and the theoretical guarantees assume a frozen backbone whereas experiments perform full-network fine-tuning.

GeL7NntZTU.one_liner: Co-evolves medical vision-language models and multi-agent supervision principles alongside adaptive curriculum allocation.
GeL7NntZTU.problem: Training medical vision-language models across changing learner capabilities typically requires costly repeated manual error analysis and static task-specific training data construction.
GeL7NntZTU.method: CoEvoMed couples a medical vision-language model with a multi-agent supervision pipeline where a revision agent updates reusable supervision-construction principles based on factual consistency and task alignment comparisons. Under fixed task budgets, a curriculum allocation module dynamically adjusts data construction effort according to the learner's capability profile and progress.
GeL7NntZTU.key_idea: Iteratively updates natural-language supervision-construction principles and task-level curriculum budgets using multi-agent feedback on the medical vision-language learner's evolving factual consistency and capability profile.
GeL7NntZTU.evidence: Evaluated by training 8B and 32B models on 2D and 3D medical tasks, including four 2D VQA benchmarks, MIMIC-CXR, IU-Xray, and 3D recognition, question answering, and report generation.
GeL7NntZTU.claimed_gains: The 8B model surpasses Hulu-Med-7B by 1.15–4.80 percentage points on four 2D VQA benchmarks and achieves higher RaTEScore on MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray.
GeL7NntZTU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the adaptive stage-dependent supervision concept and the broad experimental coverage across 2D and 3D medical VQA and report generation tasks.
GeL7NntZTU.main_concern: Reviewers find that the ablations do not sufficiently isolate the effects of individual agent roles, principle evolution, curriculum adaptation, and synthetic data quality.

tzKXgKSmXx.one_liner: Stabilizes end-to-end value-gradient reinforcement learning for generative control policies by reconstructing the denoising path at each iteration.
tzKXgKSmXx.problem: Optimizing iterative generative control policies such as diffusion and flow-matching models with value-gradient reinforcement learning often suffers from training instability when backpropagating through the full generation chain.
tzKXgKSmXx.method: The authors propose VINE, a sampling strategy for flow-matching policies that predicts the clean target state and reintroduces Gaussian noise to reconstruct the generation path at each sampling step. This modification enables stable end-to-end value-gradient backpropagation through the entire iterative sampling chain with minimal code changes.
tzKXgKSmXx.key_idea: Reconstructs intermediate states along the iterative flow-matching generation path by predicting clean actions and re-injecting Gaussian noise at each step during end-to-end value-gradient backpropagation.
tzKXgKSmXx.evidence: Evaluated against full-BPTT baselines on OGBench tasks, off-policy RL adaptation of the pretrained pi_0.5 VLA model, LIBERO, and real-robot manipulation tasks.
tzKXgKSmXx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that stabilizing RL for iterative generative policies is an important problem and praise VINE for its simplicity, ease of implementation, and broad experiments across simulation and real robots.
tzKXgKSmXx.main_concern: Reviewers note that VINE closely resembles existing re-noising and stochastic flow samplers, and the ablations do not disentangle whether gains come from stochastic exploration, altered marginal path distributions, or improved gradient propagation.

5IBvYYspZv.one_liner: Formalizes a mechanism-response-decision sufficiency hierarchy for planning world models and proposes a modular query-guided planner.
5IBvYYspZv.problem: Accurate physical prediction requires preserving fine distinctions that may be unnecessary for planning decisions, leaving unclear what information a world model must retain across queries, candidate sets, and search procedures.
5IBvYYspZv.method: The paper formalizes a three-level hierarchy of mechanism, response, and decision sufficiency to characterize how query resolution and adaptive candidate search determine required world-model fidelity. It also proposes a modular planning architecture where the query guides candidate search while an action-conditioned world model predicts outcomes.
5IBvYYspZv.key_idea: Separates physical mechanism, response, and decision sufficiency over candidate action sets and decouples query-conditioned candidate search from action-conditioned outcome prediction.
5IBvYYspZv.evidence: Investigated through theoretical regret bounds and empirical studies in a collision system, nonlinear dynamics, and robotic planning tasks including Push-T.
5IBvYYspZv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written and appreciate the clean formulation of what world models must preserve for candidate selection versus search, supported by illustrative experiments.
5IBvYYspZv.main_concern: Reviewers view the theoretical results and sufficiency definitions as closely related to classical state-abstraction and value-equivalence literature, with limited formal integration across the paper.

SwGfNy9TAP.one_liner: Learns nonparametric Poisson DAGs from count data by integrating conditional-uncorrelatedness screening and equidispersion hypothesis testing.
SwGfNy9TAP.problem: Existing ranking-based Poisson DAG discovery methods force causal orderings by picking the least overdispersed node without testing statistical compatibility with equidispersion, and rely on restrictive prespecified link functions.
SwGfNy9TAP.method: PoET replaces score ranking with test-based layer eligibility using cross-fitted tests for conditional uncorrelatedness and equidispersion based on Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (CMP) kernel smoothing. Conditional-uncorrelatedness tests screen parent candidates to reduce conditioning dimension, equidispersion tests guide layer assignment and parent recovery, and a diagnostic stopping rule halts when no candidate satisfies equidispersion.
SwGfNy9TAP.key_idea: Uses cross-fitted Conway-Maxwell-Poisson kernel smoothing to nonparametrically test conditional uncorrelatedness for parent screening and equidispersion for layer eligibility with a diagnostic stopping rule.
SwGfNy9TAP.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs of graph-recovery consistency under correct specification and empirical evaluations on synthetic count datasets and real-world datasets including NBA and Lending Club.
SwGfNy9TAP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the nonparametric CMP-kernel estimation without fixed link functions and the principled diagnostic stopping rule that avoids forcing invalid graph structures.
SwGfNy9TAP.main_concern: Reviewers note that real-world overdispersion and confounding mimic the missing-parent variance signal, sample sizes below 1000 are not well supported, and methodological novelty mainly combines existing identification and testing tools.

wlgozgAf7a.one_liner: Constructs an interval quasimetric lower-bound heuristic over partial states for classical planning regression search with conditional suboptimality guarantees.
wlgozgAf7a.problem: Few informative heuristics exist for backward regression search over partial states in classical planning, and classical h^m heuristics lose additive cost information across serial subgoals due to max aggregation.
wlgozgAf7a.method: Partial-State IQE (PS-IQE) embeds partial planning states as lower-bound representations in an Interval Quasimetric Embedding (IQE) latent space, trained with an extended QRL objective incorporating relative and absolute local transition constraints via log-sum-exp aggregation. After transition-system preprocessing, A* regression search guided by PS-IQE evaluates m-fact subsets in time and space polynomial in the number of grounded facts for fixed m.
wlgozgAf7a.key_idea: Constructs vector-valued lower-bound representations of partial states in a learned Interval Quasimetric Embedding space subject to local transition constraints for backward A* search.
wlgozgAf7a.evidence: Supported by conditional bounded-suboptimality proofs and empirical evaluations on classical planning instances including Gripper, Logistics, and VirtualHome.
wlgozgAf7a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting learned quasimetric embeddings to partial states for backward regression search with conditional suboptimality guarantees is a sound and well-motivated theoretical formulation.
wlgozgAf7a.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the narrow empirical evaluation covering only a few problem instances, the lack of comparisons against learned cost-partitioning baselines, and the conditional guarantee failing on domains like Logistics.

LwhvBZFV8Z.one_liner: Mitigates training-image memorization in text-to-image diffusion models by smoothing cross-attention and reinforcing content-token contributions.
LwhvBZFV8Z.problem: Text-to-image diffusion models can memorize and reproduce training images, while existing memorization mitigation methods often degrade prompt information needed to generate valid alternative depictions.
LwhvBZFV8Z.method: The authors propose a training-free inference intervention that applies Gaussian smoothing to redistribute cross-attention across token positions, then reinforces content-token contributions while attenuating padding contributions without extra denoiser calls. A local theoretical analysis characterizes when content reinforcement preserves shared value directions while smoothing dilutes localized attention peaks.
LwhvBZFV8Z.key_idea: Redistributes cross-attention weights via positional Gaussian smoothing before amplifying content-token contributions and attenuating padding tokens during diffusion sampling.
LwhvBZFV8Z.evidence: Evaluated on Stable Diffusion v1.4, Stable Diffusion v2.0, and transferred without retuning to DeepFloyd IF, accompanied by a local theoretical analysis.
LwhvBZFV8Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training-free attention intervention is simple, adds no extra denoiser evaluations, and achieves a favorable Pareto trade-off between reducing training-image similarity and preserving prompt alignment.
LwhvBZFV8Z.main_concern: Reviewers note a mismatch between the normalized operator in the mechanistic controls and the unnormalized main operator, strong theoretical assumptions not verified on actual model activations, and evaluation limited to older diffusion models and 500 memorized prompts.

YeJfe5W0RD.one_liner: Compresses Transformer KV caches during pretraining by decomposing per-layer KV states into a shared base and low-dimensional layer deltas.
YeJfe5W0RD.problem: Caching separate full key-value representations at every Transformer layer incurs large memory overhead despite substantial redundancy across neighboring layers.
YeJfe5W0RD.method: KVPath connects key-value representations across network depth during pretraining by organizing them into a layer-invariant shared base component and a compact, layer-specific low-dimensional delta component. The parameterization integrates with attention architectures including grouped-query attention (GQA) and multi-head latent attention (MLA).
YeJfe5W0RD.key_idea: Parameterizes each token's key-value state across layers as a shared depth-invariant base vector plus a low-dimensional layer-specific delta learned during pretraining.
YeJfe5W0RD.evidence: Evaluated across multiple pretraining model scales (up to 0.6B parameters), context lengths (up to 32K), and attention architectures including GQA and MLA against GQA and cross-layer attention (CLA) baselines.
YeJfe5W0RD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared-base plus low-dimensional delta formulation intuitive, clearly presented, and well validated under exact parameter- and KV-cache-matched pretraining budgets.
YeJfe5W0RD.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty relative to recent learnable cross-layer KV sharing methods and note that requiring full pretraining (evaluated only up to 0.6B parameters) limits practical applicability to existing pretrained checkpoints.

iar956oed7.one_liner: Trains neural vehicle routing solvers using post-processing basin priors and refined-outcome entropy to preserve diversity after local search.
iar956oed7.problem: In hybrid neural-classical vehicle routing solvers, distinct neural candidate solutions often collapse to the same local optimum after deterministic post-processing, wasting construction-level diversity.
iar956oed7.method: The authors propose a basin-guided reinforcement learning framework where neural candidates are converted into feasible routes and refined via bounded local moves. Training combines refined solution costs with a Refined-Edge Prior (REP) that learns customer adjacencies from refined solutions and a Refined-Outcome Entropy (ROE) signal that rewards rare post-processed outcomes, followed by parallel post-processing and route recombination at inference.
iar956oed7.key_idea: Guides policy training with customer-adjacency priors extracted from locally refined routes and an entropy bonus computed over the frequencies of distinct post-processed outcomes.
iar956oed7.evidence: Evaluated across 16 vehicle routing problem (VRP) variants against RouteFinder, PoMtVRS, CCL, MoSES, and RL-RFCS under matched post-processing settings and against PyVRP with a 60-second budget.
iar956oed7.claimed_gains: Across 16 VRP variants, the full pipeline reduces macro-average gaps to PyVRP with a 60-second per-instance budget by 69.2–81.7% relative to RouteFinder, PoMtVRS, CCL, MoSES, and RL-RFCS.
iar956oed7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that measuring and encouraging diversity after deterministic local refinement is a well-motivated insight and that the pipeline achieves strong empirical results across 16 VRP variants.
iar956oed7.main_concern: Reviewers point out incomplete ablations that fail to isolate refined-cost rewards, auxiliary supervision versus decoding priors in REP, and normalization differences between ROE and standard action entropy.

28IzJ92I5L.one_liner: Redesigns looped Mixture-of-Experts Transformers by flattening experts into fewer, wider layers with more passes and untying attention weights.
28IzJ92I5L.problem: When combining looped Transformers with sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) under fixed parameter and compute budgets, it is unclear how to distribute experts across layers and loop passes or whether attention parameters should be tied.
28IzJ92I5L.method: Foil holds total expert parameters and per-token expert compute fixed while flattening the expert hierarchy—halving expert layers, doubling experts per layer, and doubling loop passes—so routers select from a larger pool at each step. Simultaneously, Foil unties attention parameters across loop passes while keeping experts and routers shared.
28IzJ92I5L.key_idea: Halves the number of MoE layers while doubling experts per layer and loop passes at fixed compute, and assigns distinct attention parameters to each loop pass.
28IzJ92I5L.evidence: Evaluated on language model pretraining at 20B and 100B token budgets across multiple flattening degrees and downstream accuracy tasks against unflattened looped MoE baselines.
28IzJ92I5L.claimed_gains: At 100B tokens, the most flattened Foil model achieves a pretraining loss 0.012 nat below the unflattened looped baseline at equal parameters and compute.
28IzJ92I5L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled parameter- and compute-matched empirical study across 20B and 100B token budgets and the clear, intuitive design principles for looped MoE architectures.
28IzJ92I5L.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty relative to recent cross-layer expert-sharing works, a lack of theoretical justification, and missing fine-grained analysis of cross-pass expert activation overlap.

VrogB6afMl.one_liner: Adds an action-conditioned value token trained with synthetic negative perturbations to VLAs for test-time action selection and physical backtracking.
VrogB6afMl.problem: Imitation-trained vision-language-action (VLA) models lack an internal mechanism to evaluate candidate actions or detect and recover when a poor action drives the robot into an unfamiliar state.
VrogB6afMl.method: VaSeR inserts a value token into the VLA backbone to score candidate actions in a single forward pass, trained solely on demonstrations by pairing expert actions with synthetically perturbed negatives whose pseudo-labels decay with action distance. At inference, VaSeR selects the highest-scoring sampled action and triggers physical backtracking through recent poses whenever predicted values drop or stagnate.
VrogB6afMl.key_idea: Trains an in-backbone value token on distance-labeled perturbations of demonstrated actions to rank sampled candidates and trigger pose backtracking when predicted values drop or stagnate.
VrogB6afMl.evidence: Evaluated on 10 RLBench simulation tasks and two real-robot manipulation tasks using pi_0.5 and a diffusion-only HybridVLA backbone.
VrogB6afMl.claimed_gains: On 10 RLBench tasks, VaSeR raises success from 60.2% to 76.5% on pi_0.5 and from 52.3% to 65.3% on HybridVLA; on two real-robot tasks, it improves success from 58.3% to 73.3% and from 53.3% to 78.3%, respectively.
VrogB6afMl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the practical simplicity of combining action evaluation and failure recovery within a single VLA backbone using only demonstrations without external verifiers or failure rollouts.
VrogB6afMl.main_concern: Reviewers question using Euclidean distance to expert actions as a value label in multimodal manipulation tasks, note incomplete reproducibility details for the main 10-task checkpoints, and observe that gains concentrate on tasks where the baseline is unusually weak.

P0gQg03evi.one_liner: Characterizes video-LLM sensitivity to low-rank KV-cache compression as sparse, unpredicted by spectral signals, and repeatable per video-question pair.
P0gQg03evi.problem: Low-rank key-cache compression in video LLMs is commonly calibrated using aggregate accuracy curves or static spectral summaries, without testing which specific inputs actually change predictions under rank reduction.
P0gQg03evi.method: The authors treat key-cache rank compression as a controlled intervention holding the video and query fixed, measuring the disagreement set of inputs whose answers change across rank budgets. They evaluate sparsity, predictability from spectral signals, and repeatability across perturbations, compressors, and architectures to determine the proper unit of rank calibration.
P0gQg03evi.key_idea: Measures input-level prediction changes under controlled key-cache rank interventions across repeated views, compressors, and questions on the same video.
P0gQg03evi.evidence: Evaluated on MVBench using Qwen2-VL-7B across option orders, frame samplings, rank pairs, real video, a second compressor, and a second model architecture (n=2,392, 798 distinct questions).
P0gQg03evi.claimed_gains: The accuracy-versus-rank knee is carried by 5–14% of inputs, per-task allocation gains +1.3pp (CI [-0.3, +3.0]), failure prediction reaches AUC 0.755 while recovery prediction is at chance (AUC 0.47, [0.38, 0.57]), answer changes repeat with 56% probability against a 12% base rate (n=2,392, kappa=0.50), and cross-question video profiling gains +0.19pp against a +8.3pp oracle.
P0gQg03evi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous controlled-intervention methodology that separates individual prediction flips from aggregate accuracy and shows that static spectral metrics fail to predict rank recovery.
P0gQg03evi.main_concern: Reviewers note that because rank sensitivity does not transfer across different questions on the same video, the proposed profile-and-reuse deployment requires identical video-question pairs to repeat many times to amortize profiling costs, and some sparsity and cross-compressor transfer claims are overstated.

ChOPovfJX1.one_liner: Disentangles shared inter-regional and private region-specific latent dynamics from continuous multi-region local field potentials under deep brain stimulation.
ChOPovfJX1.problem: Separating coordinated inter-regional neural activity from region-specific activity in continuous local field potentials (LFPs) is confounded by nonlinear observations, autocorrelation, spectral structure, and temporal delays.
ChOPovfJX1.method: SPIRE (Shared-Private Inter-Regional Encoder) pairs region-specific sequence encoders with constrained temporal correspondence, shared-only reconstruction, and variance regularization to separate shared and private latent spaces. Representations trained on baseline recordings are frozen to analyze network reorganization under deep brain stimulation (DBS) perturbations.
ChOPovfJX1.key_idea: Combines region-specific sequence encoders with delay-tolerant temporal correspondence, shared-only cross-reconstruction, and variance regularization to separate inter-regional and region-private LFP dynamics.
ChOPovfJX1.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic LFP benchmarks with known ground-truth factors under nonlinear mappings, time-varying delays, and spectral confounds, as well as held-out human GPi-STN recordings during deep brain stimulation.
ChOPovfJX1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-designed synthetic LFP benchmarks incorporating realistic temporal and spectral confounds and the practical application to human GPi-STN deep brain stimulation data.
ChOPovfJX1.main_concern: Reviewers find the methodological novelty limited relative to existing shared-private architectures like CTAE and question why CTAE performs poorly even on the simplest synthetic regime without stronger nonlinear baselines.

bF5uaZckWR.one_liner: Shows that input Jacobian norm and negative-branch activation leak outperform Rényi sharpness in predicting generalization when varying activation functions.
bF5uaZckWR.problem: Prior evidence that weight-space Rényi sharpness strongly predicts neural network generalization was established by varying optimizers under a fixed activation function, leaving untested whether it holds when varying activations under a fixed optimizer.
bF5uaZckWR.method: The authors invert the standard experimental setup by fixing the optimizer to SGD (plus a sharpness-aware transfer check) and varying the activation function across seven common choices. They compare weight-space Rényi sharpness, the input Jacobian norm, and a mechanistic activation-level metric called negative-branch leak—defined as the mean squared activation slope on negative pre-activations—using signed Kendall rank correlation with the generalization gap.
bF5uaZckWR.key_idea: Measures the mean squared activation derivative on negative pre-activations (negative-branch leak) and input Jacobian sensitivity to predict generalization gaps induced by varying activation functions under fixed optimizers.
bF5uaZckWR.evidence: Evaluated across seven activation functions, multiple image classification datasets, and architectures including ResNet-18 and ResNet-20 under SGD and sharpness-aware optimization, alongside controlled gating interventions.
bF5uaZckWR.claimed_gains: In the main activation-varying comparison, Rényi sharpness has a mean Kendall tau of +0.22 with the generalization gap, whereas the input Jacobian and negative-branch leak achieve mean Kendall tau values of +0.63 and +0.77, respectively.
bF5uaZckWR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the experimental inversion from varying optimizers to varying activation functions insightful, clearly written, and helpful for showing that geometric generalization predictors depend on what component varies.
bF5uaZckWR.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the Rényi sharpness comparison departs from prior protocols by using full-network rather than layer-wise sharpness and accuracy gap rather than loss gap, while correlation sample sizes across seven activations are small.

zjKHi24Uxh.one_liner: Uses an offline reasoning agent and runtime rule monitor to select request-specific LLM watermarking configurations from natural-language principles.
zjKHi24Uxh.problem: Applying a single fixed text-watermarking configuration across all LLM requests forces an inflexible trade-off between text quality, edit robustness, and forgery resistance.
zjKHi24Uxh.method: Constitution-Guided Watermarking translates provider requirements written as natural-language constitutional rules into rule-specific watermark parameter configurations using an offline reasoning agent that iteratively refines settings against empirical feedback. At deployment, a lightweight monitor matches incoming requests to applicable constitutional rules and retrieves the corresponding watermark policy or exemption without modifying the serving LLM.
zjKHi24Uxh.key_idea: Maps natural-language constitutional principles to request-specific watermark parameter configurations via offline agentic search and runtime rule-matching monitor routing.
zjKHi24Uxh.evidence: Evaluated on KGW watermarking configurations across prompt categories and paraphrasing attacks such as DIPPER against fixed KGW settings and random configuration search.
zjKHi24Uxh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving from uniform watermarking to prompt-appropriate trade-offs governed by auditable natural-language rules without modifying the serving model is a timely and practical idea.
zjKHi24Uxh.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical robustness gains over random configuration search are mostly statistically insignificant, search relies on only 10 reference prompts per rule, and evaluation is limited to a single watermark family (KGW), model, and seed.

NA2cQSx16N.one_liner: MMCSP-Bench pairs text and image puzzles, while DeCSP selects predefined constraint operators to separate recovery failures from symbolic solving.
NA2cQSx16N.problem: Final-answer accuracy does not reveal whether visual symbolic reasoning fails during problem recovery or downstream solution generation.
NA2cQSx16N.method: MMCSP-Bench provides matched text, standard-image, and OOD-image views of Sudoku, Nonogram, and Graph Coloring with source-constraint verification. DeCSP restricts solver construction to predefined constraint-operator selection and deterministic execution, enabling controlled diagnostic comparisons.
NA2cQSx16N.key_idea: Pair equivalent multimodal problems with constrained operator selection and fixed-solver controls to distinguish visual recovery from symbolic-generation errors.
NA2cQSx16N.evidence: Seven LVLMs are evaluated using matched puzzle views, correct-structure and shared-transcription controls, fixed solvers, and stage-targeted training.
NA2cQSx16N.claimed_gains: DeCSP achieves 96.24% mean valid-solution accuracy on structured text versus 8.19% for direct answering and 43.43% for PAL, falling to 42.57% on standard images and 28.19% on OOD images.
NA2cQSx16N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value matched views and verification against original constraints for separating transcription errors from valid symbolic solving.
NA2cQSx16N.main_concern: Task identity largely determines the small predefined operator set, so DeCSP demonstrates restricted routing more clearly than general symbolic problem formulation.

I0YNpRTZmT.one_liner: Representative Attention gathers all image tokens into learned representatives, mixes them, and redistributes content through separate query attention.
I0YNpRTZmT.problem: Fixed spatial partitions can separate similar visual tokens and merge dissimilar ones, misaligning efficient attention with feature structure.
I0YNpRTZmT.method: Learned projections assign every image token to input-dependent representatives, which interact through lightweight self-attention. Separate attention weights distribute the refined representative content back to spatial queries.
I0YNpRTZmT.key_idea: Gather feature-dependent global representatives, refine them by self-attention, and redistribute information with independently computed attention weights.
I0YNpRTZmT.evidence: Experiments span image classification, object detection, instance segmentation, and semantic segmentation across multiple vision backbone families.
I0YNpRTZmT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Gather-Interact-Distribute pipeline clear and feature-driven global communication well motivated.
I0YNpRTZmT.main_concern: The contribution over existing intermediate-token attention methods is limited and the benefit of removing spatial pooling is insufficiently isolated.

MQaEQYxIgI.one_liner: LEDGER retains dialogue and attribute histories and varies query-dependent readers to diagnose selective correction of outdated premises.
MQaEQYxIgI.problem: Agent memory must reject stale premises without harming valid answers or current and historical recall.
MQaEQYxIgI.method: LEDGER preserves raw dialogue and attribute histories and uses query-dependent answering procedures. Controlled reader swaps, matched-history queries, and oracle state replacements separate effects of stored evidence from its interpretation.
MQaEQYxIgI.key_idea: Hold stored evidence fixed while changing the reader, then intervene on current values and transitions to separate memory and interpretation effects.
MQaEQYxIgI.evidence: Evaluation spans eight systems and three benchmarks, with matched queries over 117 histories and oracle interventions on 131 held-out histories.
MQaEQYxIgI.claimed_gains: With LEDGER evidence fixed, its query-dependent reader raises GPT-4.1 premise resistance from 0.020 to 0.725.
MQaEQYxIgI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled experiments revealing interactions between stored state, readers, and premise correction.
MQaEQYxIgI.main_concern: Improved stale-premise resistance comes with substantial losses in valid-premise accuracy and recall, so selective correction remains unestablished.

NBrar41wnf.one_liner: Human conversation annotations separate failures in attribute extraction, relevance selection, and personalized response generation.
NBrar41wnf.problem: Synthetic personalization evaluations may not reveal how LLM systems perform on human conversations and judgments.
NBrar41wnf.method: The study collects human conversations and annotations for extracting user attributes, selecting relevant attributes, and incorporating them into responses. It evaluates each stage and explores lightweight training interventions to bring automated evaluation closer to human judgments.
NBrar41wnf.key_idea: Evaluate attribute support, prompt relevance, and response usefulness separately using human conversations and stage-specific human judgments.
NBrar41wnf.evidence: The dataset contains 550 conversations and 5,949, 11,919, and 1,101 judgments for extraction, relevance pairing, and response incorporation, respectively.
NBrar41wnf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value human-grounded, staged evaluation for revealing personalization failures that synthetic or end-to-end scores can obscure.
NBrar41wnf.main_concern: The broad claims about real-user personalization exceed comparisons that mix synthetic-versus-human data with third-party rather than target-user judgments.

3PiZOeBSWn.one_liner: A four-stage Bayesian pipeline distinguishes arithmetic decodability, geometric shape, concept ownership, and causal use in LLM activations.
3PiZOeBSWn.problem: Accurate linear probes do not establish that a recovered geometry belongs to the target concept or drives model computation.
3PiZOeBSWn.method: The pipeline verifies decoding, compares candidate shapes with an evidence threshold, removes prespecified related concepts to test ownership, and intervenes on the geometry at the final prompt token. All four stages evaluate the same data.
3PiZOeBSWn.key_idea: Combine Bayesian shape comparison, removal of related concepts, and targeted interventions to separate representation geometry from causal computational use.
3PiZOeBSWn.evidence: Experiments examine two-digit addition and multiplication in GPT-J 6B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Pythia 6.9B.
3PiZOeBSWn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate explicitly separating decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use instead of treating probe success as evidence of computation.
3PiZOeBSWn.main_concern: The ownership criterion may label geometry inherited by construction or because removing related concepts also destroys target information.

qLUShoitxy.one_liner: LLM report mining, report-constrained tumor masks, and a radiomics verifier target hard errors in CT cancer detection.
qLUShoitxy.problem: Cancer segmentation models miss small tumors and mistake non-cancer abnormalities for tumors during clinical deployment.
qLUShoitxy.method: DREAM mines radiology reports for hard positive and negative cases and refines predicted masks using reported tumor size, count, and location. A cascade combines segmentation outputs with a radiomics-based abnormality classifier to revise tumor scores.
qLUShoitxy.key_idea: Mine difficult cases from reports, constrain pseudo-masks with reported tumor attributes, and combine segmentation with radiomics verification.
qLUShoitxy.evidence: LLMs mine 440,000 reports, and experiments evaluate tumor detection in the pancreas, bladder, and gallbladder.
qLUShoitxy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the focus on clinically important hard cases and scalable report-based acquisition well motivated.
qLUShoitxy.main_concern: Report-refined masks depend on potentially incomplete reports and unreliable initial predictions without sufficient independent spatial validation.

Rc6m0gXk1Z.one_liner: Paired prompts change one physical variable to test whether video world models generate appropriately different futures.
Rc6m0gXk1Z.problem: Single-video plausibility scores can miss models that fail to change predicted outcomes when physical conditions change.
Rc6m0gXk1Z.method: What-If World pairs prompts grounded in nuScenes and DROID frames, altering one variable from a shared six-variable taxonomy. APEO scores prompt adherence, physical consistency, scene preservation, and expected outcome differences.
Rc6m0gXk1Z.key_idea: Hold the scene fixed, alter one physical condition, and judge whether paired generated videos diverge in the expected outcome.
Rc6m0gXk1Z.evidence: The benchmark evaluates nine video models on 319 prompt pairs drawn from driving and robotic manipulation scenarios.
Rc6m0gXk1Z.claimed_gains: None of the nine models exceeds 53% on the paired score, and the four open-source models average 28.6%.
Rc6m0gXk1Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that paired evaluation exposes failures in physical responsiveness that single-video metrics miss.
Rc6m0gXk1Z.main_concern: Semantic interventions lack explicit physical parameters, making expected outcomes ambiguous and weakening claims about quantitative physical simulation.

s8akRvJHQg.one_liner: Poisson closure and cycle-scale regularization stabilize neural-operator rollouts for radio-frequency-driven plasma dynamics.
s8akRvJHQg.problem: Autoregressive neural operators accumulate errors across the oscillatory, multiscale RF cycles of capacitively coupled plasmas.
s8akRvJHQg.method: The tailored operator predicts transport variables while a numerical Poisson solve reconstructs electric potential during rollout. Floquet-Poincaré-inspired regularization and random subsequence training address cycle-scale dynamics and long trajectories.
s8akRvJHQg.key_idea: Close neural transport predictions with a numerical Poisson solve and regularize evolution across RF cycles using auxiliary cycle-scale supervision.
s8akRvJHQg.evidence: A parameterized one-dimensional CCP benchmark tests component variants, different trajectory lengths, and extrapolation beyond the training horizon.
s8akRvJHQg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the use of plasma structure, particularly Poisson reconstruction, physically motivated for long-horizon prediction.
s8akRvJHQg.main_concern: The methodological distinction from existing neural-numerical solvers, operator architectures, and temporal training strategies needs clearer justification.

LZ4tZQT9dJ.one_liner: Entropy-based commitment timing and counterfactual tool returns reward video agents for waiting on decisive visual evidence.
LZ4tZQT9dJ.problem: Video agents may ignore tool returns or accept uninformative returns, so tool use alone does not establish evidence use.
LZ4tZQT9dJ.method: ERA tracks high-entropy tokens and detects when uncertainty resolves relative to tool calls. A turn-level RL reward combines this commitment timing with reasoning contrasts under uninformative and decisive returns.
LZ4tZQT9dJ.key_idea: Reward commitment after decisive evidence by contrasting entropy-resolution timing under informative and uninformative tool returns.
LZ4tZQT9dJ.evidence: Tests use tool-required questions from four video benchmarks, substituted uninformative first returns, pressure assertions, and comparisons with counterfactual re-seek fine-tuning.
LZ4tZQT9dJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing evidence-sensitive reasoning from tool-call frequency or answer accuracy alone.
LZ4tZQT9dJ.main_concern: Using the same entropy-based commitment proxy in training and evaluation risks circular validation without independently establishing actual evidence use.

g8ODF0GTa0.one_liner: Counterfactual continuation preferences select image-grounded repairs before radiology report errors propagate into later sentences.
g8ODF0GTa0.problem: An image-inconsistent statement can become context for subsequent sentences and cause partial-report drift during autoregressive generation.
g8ODF0GTa0.method: The framework proposes minimal image-grounded repairs and trains a lightweight preference model on corrected versus unchanged full-report continuations. Online selection uses short lookahead and a validation-calibrated threshold without updating the report generator.
g8ODF0GTa0.key_idea: Learn whether repairing a partial report improves its continuation, then apply image-supported repairs selectively using short lookahead.
