g8ODF0GTa0.evidence: Experiments cover MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray, multiple report generators, and hallucination-mitigation baselines.
g8ODF0GTa0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separating whether a correction is image-supported from whether applying it during generation improves the eventual report.
g8ODF0GTa0.main_concern: Missing controlled comparisons against post-hoc correction and other relevant generation strategies leave the benefit of online repair insufficiently isolated.

GgKxm3egaa.one_liner: Compression sensitivity and counterfactual ranking feedback teach rerankers which representations to retain and how much computation each pair needs.
GgKxm3egaa.problem: Fixed compression configurations cannot adapt to differences in evidence location and required evidence volume across query-document pairs.
GgKxm3egaa.method: AREA preserves selected full-resolution intermediate representations in deeper layers and learns an instance-specific retention budget. Relevance-objective sensitivity supervises evidence localization, while counterfactual ranking feedback supervises budgets without explicit token or budget labels.
GgKxm3egaa.key_idea: Learn representation retention from compression sensitivity and learn instance budgets from counterfactual ranking feedback.
GgKxm3egaa.evidence: Evaluation includes BRIGHT, a constructed BRIGHT-Long setting, industrial search, and controlled model-forward timing comparisons.
GgKxm3egaa.claimed_gains: On BRIGHT, AREA reports 28.81 nDCG@10 versus LTC's 27.72 at 50% retention; adaptive budgeting reaches 30.21 at an average retention ratio of 0.49 versus the separately optimized full-context variant's 30.10, with a 1.33× controlled model-forward speedup.
GgKxm3egaa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value learning both evidence location and per-instance computation requirements without explicit budget annotations.
GgKxm3egaa.main_concern: Unclear terminology and insufficiently specified training and comparison settings make the approach difficult to follow and reproduce.

5EqmkQN9bK.one_liner: Failure-attributed procedural memory updates jointly adapt agent executors and safety guards without changing model weights.
5EqmkQN9bK.problem: Independently developed executors and guards can allow harmful actions, block legitimate work, or enter unresolved revise-retry loops.
5EqmkQN9bK.method: InterlockBench pairs benign tasks with malicious environmental injections to test safe task completion after intervention. Concord assigns failed interactions to the executor, guard, or both and evolves their complementary procedural memories with fixed model weights.
5EqmkQN9bK.key_idea: Attribute each failed interaction to executor and guard roles, then update their procedural memories jointly to guide subsequent coordination.
5EqmkQN9bK.evidence: The study evaluates deployed executor-guard pairings, introduces InterlockBench, and reports comparisons on AgentHarm and within AgentDyn-based environments.
5EqmkQN9bK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that recovering authorized task progress after guard intervention is an important agent deployment problem.
5EqmkQN9bK.main_concern: Unvalidated failure attribution and unmatched one-sided adaptation baselines leave the specific benefit of attributed joint adaptation unclear.

Xkg6l5hJ18.one_liner: Overlapping main and private decoding lanes advance the next diffusion-language-model block before the current block finishes.
Xkg6l5hJ18.problem: Serial block decoding lets a few unresolved positions delay all progress on the next block.
Xkg6l5hJ18.method: AsyncLane completes the current block in a main lane while a private lane accumulates next-block candidates, computing both in one batched forward pass. It transfers private progress after completion and can reuse opening predictions through lookahead prefill.
Xkg6l5hJ18.key_idea: Batch current-block refinement with private next-block prediction, retaining candidate progress for handoff when the current block completes.
Xkg6l5hJ18.evidence: Evaluation covers LLaDA, Dream, and DiffusionGemma on five benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and instruction following.
Xkg6l5hJ18.claimed_gains: Effective output throughput reaches up to 2.35× AdaBlock's on LLaDA and Dream and up to 1.23× on DiffusionGemma, whose comparator is truncated in the supplied abstract.
Xkg6l5hJ18.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free overlap of adjacent decoding blocks well motivated and recognize measured speed gains.
Xkg6l5hJ18.main_concern: Unmatched confidence thresholds, stopping rules, and configuration selection confound the speed gains attributed to scheduling.

Sl9gPx4gk3.one_liner: Query-time anchor selection and session-neighborhood restoration organize conversational evidence without changing stored turns.
Sl9gPx4gk3.problem: Write-time memory organization precedes knowledge of future queries, while independent retrieval can waste evidence budgets on redundant or fragmented turns.
Sl9gPx4gk3.method: Chain on Demand selects a fixed budget of anchors from a broad candidate pool using relevance, lexical diversity, and newly covered query terms. It restores each anchor's same-session neighborhood to form a temporary evidence chain while preserving the underlying memory.
Sl9gPx4gk3.key_idea: Select complementary query-relevant anchors and deterministically restore their session neighborhoods only when answering the current query.
Sl9gPx4gk3.evidence: Paired evaluation covers all 1,986 LoCoMo questions and all 500 LongMemEval-S questions, with matched allocation controls.
Sl9gPx4gk3.claimed_gains: COD reports 82.2% accuracy on 1,540 non-adversarial LoCoMo questions, 76.3% on all 1,986 questions, and 86.6% across all 500 LongMemEval-S questions.
Sl9gPx4gk3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value organizing coherent evidence at query time over unchanged conversational memory and examining allocation with controlled comparisons.
Sl9gPx4gk3.main_concern: The specific benefit of set-aware allocation over strong existing selection methods and neighborhood reconstruction remains insufficiently established.

MbZMdLS9uz.one_liner: Synthesis diagnostics redirect a World Tree acquisition distribution toward under-covered LLM post-training capabilities.
MbZMdLS9uz.problem: Open-web curation is costly, and static synthesis pipelines cannot adapt data acquisition to intermediate outcomes.
MbZMdLS9uz.method: ANDES organizes a data-synthesis space as a self-evolving World Tree and maintains an acquisition distribution for a trainer-specified capability target. Diagnostics of effective quantity, topical allocation, and logical diversity redirect later synthesis rounds before model training.
MbZMdLS9uz.key_idea: Update a structured data-acquisition distribution from synthesis-round coverage and diversity diagnostics before spending resources on model training.
MbZMdLS9uz.evidence: Experiments evaluate four base models under compute constraints, including PostTrainBench, cross-task generalization, and component ablations.
MbZMdLS9uz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find feedback-directed acquisition well motivated for obtaining useful post-training supervision under limited resources.
MbZMdLS9uz.main_concern: Ablations change multiple components and lack sufficiently matched synthesis baselines to isolate adaptive feedback and the World Tree.

hSwCTccrjq.one_liner: A skill curator navigates raw agent trajectories on demand to synthesize procedures suited to the current task.
hSwCTccrjq.problem: Fixed procedural summaries can discard experience details that later tasks need while retaining irrelevant instance-specific information.
hSwCTccrjq.method: ExpVoyager lets a curator inspect accumulated trajectories through multiple views and resolutions. The curator extracts reusable procedures while tracking unresolved knowledge needs that determine where it navigates next.
hSwCTccrjq.key_idea: Use remaining task-specific knowledge needs to guide iterative inspection of raw trajectories and synthesis of procedural skills.
hSwCTccrjq.evidence: Downstream experiments include ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop, with navigation-budget comparisons and end-to-end token accounting.
hSwCTccrjq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the information-loss problem in fixed skill abstractions and the practical value of task-specific experience access.
hSwCTccrjq.main_concern: Sequential navigation incurs substantial inference cost, and budget-matched comparisons do not sufficiently establish the efficiency of the gains.

MKj8vnmQaz.one_liner: Comparisons of auditory cortical prediction and perceptual judgments test whether self-supervised model alignment transfers across neural and behavioral targets.
MKj8vnmQaz.problem: Self-supervised sensory models may align with cortical responses without predicting human perceptual behavior equally well.
MKj8vnmQaz.method: The study compares acoustic, semantic, supervised, self-supervised, and fine-tuned auditory models using cortical response prediction and behavioral similarity judgments. It examines rankings across cortical regions, learning objectives, and pretraining data.
MKj8vnmQaz.key_idea: Evaluate the same model families against cortical responses and behavioral similarity judgments to test whether their rankings transfer across targets.
MKj8vnmQaz.evidence: Comparisons include six supervised auditory networks, fourteen self-supervised pretrained networks, and three supervised fine-tuned variants using fMRI and sound/word similarity data.
MKj8vnmQaz.claimed_gains: Four self-supervised models appear among the top five in each of three higher-order regions, but all four supervised sound-event classifiers outperform them on both behavioral tasks.
MKj8vnmQaz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of comparing model alignment across cortical and behavioral targets.
MKj8vnmQaz.main_concern: The observational comparisons do not provide a sufficiently clear, generalizable explanation for differences across objectives, architectures, and pretraining data.

oq73QnNnrP.one_liner: Hierarchically resolved denoising losses expose learning lag, which a regularizer reduces to shorten diffusion hallucination during training.
oq73QnNnrP.problem: Aggregate denoising loss can plateau before global generalization and therefore fail to distinguish hallucination from successful structure learning.
oq73QnNnrP.method: The paper resolves and rescales denoising loss across a hierarchy to identify asynchronous learning of local and global structure. It regularizes this hierarchical lag in a diffusion transformer trained on a random hierarchy model.
oq73QnNnrP.key_idea: Measure the lag between hierarchically resolved learning dynamics and penalize that lag during diffusion training.
oq73QnNnrP.evidence: Analysis and diffusion-transformer experiments use a synthetic random hierarchy model with separate local correctness and global generalization measures.
oq73QnNnrP.claimed_gains: The abstract reports shrinking the hallucination window in training time by an order of a magnitude.
oq73QnNnrP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the local-versus-global learning discrepancy interesting and appreciate testing a regularizer aimed at hallucination.
oq73QnNnrP.main_concern: Evidence from a single synthetic hierarchy setup does not justify broad conclusions or establish applicability to real data.

5O1pQDQLvs.one_liner: Within-block transformer states predict brain responses to test how modality, stimulus, and positional encoding affect alignment.
5O1pQDQLvs.problem: Layer-output analyses overlook internal states, and the generality of text-model intermediate-state alignment findings remains unclear.
5O1pQDQLvs.method: The study uses within-block states from audio, music-generation, vision, and text transformers to predict brain responses. It also compares models with shared basic architectures but different positional encodings.
5O1pQDQLvs.key_idea: Compare brain-response prediction across internal transformer states, modalities, stimuli, and positional-encoding variants rather than only block outputs.
5O1pQDQLvs.evidence: Experiments use fMRI responses to speech, music, and images and compare intermediate states, including RoPE-rotated queries and keys.
5O1pQDQLvs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value examining internal block states across multiple modalities and brain datasets.
5O1pQDQLvs.main_concern: The reported state rankings lack sufficient statistical significance analysis to establish reliable differences in brain alignment.

8Sii4peZI1.one_liner: Self-supervised echocardiography JEPA routing historical motion through an explicit circular phase state and single-frame predictor bottleneck
8Sii4peZI1.problem: Action-free video pretraining leaves autonomous physiological dynamics implicit in high-dimensional features or relies on short-range frame shortcuts rather than tracking explicit cardiac cycle phase.
8Sii4peZI1.method: CardiacState pretrains a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) on 1.88 million unlabeled echocardiogram videos by inferring an explicit circular phase state from video history, regularized to advance smoothly with elapsed time. Its future-feature predictor sees only the single current frame, forcing historical motion information to pass solely through the cyclic phase state and time interval.
8Sii4peZI1.key_idea: Restrict a video JEPA predictor to one current frame so future-feature prediction must condition on an inferred circular phase variable regularized by elapsed physical time.
8Sii4peZI1.evidence: Pretrained on 1.88 million unlabeled clinical echocardiogram videos without ECG gating and evaluated on frozen Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction estimation and non-parametric ED/ES keyframe localization across datasets and views.
8Sii4peZI1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling endogenous cardiac dynamics with an ECG-free circular latent state is clinically well motivated and yields useful representations across echocardiography tasks.
8Sii4peZI1.main_concern: The angular progression loss does not guarantee true one-cycle-per-heartbeat physiological alignment, prior work already uses circular cardiac states, and ablations lack a matched standard JEPA while showing marginal gain from the bottleneck itself.

2mzHlw5ctC.one_liner: Montage-agnostic self-supervised intracranial EEG foundation model pretrained on 5,310 hours with spatio-temporal resampling and multi-domain masked reconstruction
2mzHlw5ctC.problem: Patient-specific electrode layouts, variable channel counts, and heterogeneous recording setups across clinical centers hinder transferable foundation models for intracranial EEG.
2mzHlw5ctC.method: DIVER-1 combines any-variate electrode-time attention, spatio-temporal resampling (at 0.1s and 1s granularities), input-conditioned positional embeddings, and multi-domain masked reconstruction to handle arbitrary electrode montages. It is pretrained on 5,310 hours (352k channel-hours) of task-free clinical ECoG and SEEG recordings alongside a compute-controlled scaling analysis.
2mzHlw5ctC.key_idea: Handle variable intracranial electrode montages via spatio-temporal resampling, input-conditioned positional embeddings, and any-variate electrode-time attention trained with multi-domain masked reconstruction.
2mzHlw5ctC.evidence: Pretrained on 5,310 hours of external clinical ECoG and SEEG data and evaluated with leakage-aware protocols on held-out iMINDBench naturalistic movie-decoding and MAYO seizure detection benchmarks, plus compute-aware scaling experiments.
2mzHlw5ctC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the leakage-aware cross-dataset evaluation on iMINDBench and MAYO and the scaling study showing that lower pretraining loss does not reliably translate into downstream iEEG gains.
2mzHlw5ctC.main_concern: Changing architecture and scaling closed-source pretraining data by 54x simultaneously confounds comparisons with prior models like PopT-v2, and downstream tasks are limited in clinical breadth and subject count.

Ndu4FV6h3f.one_liner: Model-free agent memory compaction that selects archived messages using persistent attention-derived importance scores, query relevance, and dependency-graph traversal
Ndu4FV6h3f.problem: Irreversible history summarization and KV-cache eviction in long-horizon LLM agents either lose earlier details needed by shifting user requests or require costly model calls to re-summarize and re-encode context.
Ndu4FV6h3f.method: ReCAP archives interaction history externally and records past attention-derived message importance scores and inter-message dependency edges in a lightweight persistent context graph. When a new user request arrives, it combines stored importance with lexical query relevance and traverses dependency edges to reconstruct active context without invoking an LLM.
Ndu4FV6h3f.key_idea: Persist attention-derived block importance and dependency edges in an external graph so future turns retrieve query-relevant messages and their dependencies without LLM summarization calls.
Ndu4FV6h3f.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen3-Coder and gpt-oss on SWE-Together, Lost-in-Conversation, and coding benchmarks against full history, recency, KV eviction, compression, and Codex-style summarization baselines.
Ndu4FV6h3f.claimed_gains: Reduces estimated latency for compaction and cold restoration by approximately 95% compared with Codex's default summarization-based compaction on both Qwen3-Coder and gpt-oss, while roughly halving historical context per call on SWE-Together at comparable quality.
Ndu4FV6h3f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that maintaining a non-destructive archive indexed by past attention and current query relevance is practical for multi-turn agents and performs well on Lost-in-Conversation and coding tasks.
Ndu4FV6h3f.main_concern: The main ablation removes scalar importance scores, dependency edges, and staleness rules all at once—leaving the benefit of graph traversal unisolated—while the 95% latency reduction relies on partial cost estimates.

eY7xwFYJKY.one_liner: Unsupervised low-light image enhancer decoupling bright-anchor relative illumination structure from per-image dual-metering global exposure adjustment
eY7xwFYJKY.problem: Unsupervised low-light enhancement methods entangle spatial illumination patterns with global exposure, allowing noisy dark regions to bias illumination estimates while enforcing rigid scene-agnostic exposure targets.
eY7xwFYJKY.method: Relative Illumination Structure Estimation (RISE) separates spatially varying relative illumination from global exposure, inferring the structural illumination field from higher-SNR bright anchor regions. A Dual-Metering Exposure Reference (DMER) computed directly from each input image guides scene-adaptive global exposure scaling without paired normal-light training data.
eY7xwFYJKY.key_idea: Disentangle spatial illumination structure—inferred from reliable bright image regions—from global exposure strength guided by an input-derived dual-metering reference.
eY7xwFYJKY.evidence: Trained unsupervised on LSRW-Nikon and evaluated across seven paired low-light benchmarks and five unpaired real-world datasets using PSNR, IQA, and IAA metrics.
eY7xwFYJKY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that RISE achieves strong cross-dataset PSNR and perceptual scores across paired and unpaired low-light benchmarks while training without paired normal-light supervision.
eY7xwFYJKY.main_concern: Reviewers question whether DMER and the relational illumination field reduce to handcrafted global gain plus spatially varying gamma correction, alongside unisolated KIC ablations and architectural inconsistencies.

ImyrQKmvTo.one_liner: Demonstrates unconditional Shrink-and-Perturb collapses offline-to-online RL policies and introduces diagnostic capacity gating to block unnecessary resets
ImyrQKmvTo.problem: Unconditionally scheduled plasticity interventions such as periodic Shrink-and-Perturb destroy structured pretrained policy and value representations during offline-to-online reinforcement learning.
ImyrQKmvTo.method: The paper conducts a seed-matched factorial audit of periodic Shrink-and-Perturb and dormant-neuron recycling (ReDo) in offline-to-online continuous control, including actuator-failure regimes. It introduces CapacityGate, a closed-loop diagnostic gate based on feature rank and neuron dormancy thresholds that abstains from parameter perturbations when network capacity remains healthy.
ImyrQKmvTo.key_idea: Gate plasticity-restoration perturbations on online feature-rank and neuron-dormancy diagnostics so pretrained offline-to-online policies are not perturbed unless capacity degradation occurs.
ImyrQKmvTo.evidence: Evaluated over 150 D4RL continuous-control locomotion runs (45 seed-matched pairwise comparisons plus 15 frozen reference runs) and actuator-failure stress tests using IQM and paired Wilcoxon tests.
ImyrQKmvTo.claimed_gains: Demonstrates that unconditional periodic Shrink-and-Perturb causes a 68.3% collapse in aggregate IQM normalized return (38.78 → 12.30, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank W = 18.0, p = 1.44 × 10⁻¹¹, mean paired difference +26.03 ± 19.09).
ImyrQKmvTo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides statistically rigorous negative evidence that blind periodic Shrink-and-Perturb severely degrades offline-to-online RL locomotion policies.
ImyrQKmvTo.main_concern: On the main D4RL benchmark CapacityGate triggers zero interventions—making it numerically identical to the no-intervention baseline—while positive intervention regimes are tested narrowly on single-seed stress tests.

ctKipVwyzz.one_liner: Adapts a frozen tabular foundation model to one-class anomaly detection by optimizing trainable pseudo-anomaly context rows
ctKipVwyzz.problem: In-context tabular foundation models require labeled classes for classification, preventing direct application to tabular anomaly detection where only normal reference samples are observed.
ctKipVwyzz.method: GradPAO keeps a pretrained tabular foundation model frozen and introduces trainable pseudo-anomaly context rows initialized using the model's inter-sample attention weights. It optimizes these pseudo-anomalies by backpropagating through the frozen model to maximize separability from normal context samples and mutual diversity across pseudo-anomaly classes.
ctKipVwyzz.key_idea: Supply missing anomaly classes to a frozen in-context tabular foundation model by initializing and gradient-optimizing trainable pseudo-anomaly context rows for normal-versus-anomaly separability and diversity.
ctKipVwyzz.evidence: Evaluated on two large-scale tabular anomaly detection benchmarks (ADBench with 57 datasets and OddBench with 690 datasets) alongside initialization and diversity ablations.
ctKipVwyzz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, clearly presented, and broadly evaluated across roughly 750 tabular anomaly detection datasets without retraining the tabular foundation model.
ctKipVwyzz.main_concern: Ablations indicate most gains stem from simply adding synthetic anomaly context rows to a frozen TFM rather than the attention initialization or diversity loss, with concerns about ADBench hyperparameter tuning.

s1fL3aqi34.one_liner: Replaces shared InfoNCE temperature with a learned pair-dependent scale and introduces an appearance-varied cross-view geo-localization benchmark
s1fL3aqi34.problem: Cross-view geo-localization methods focus on street-to-satellite viewpoint shifts while using fixed contrastive temperatures and benchmarks that overlook sample ambiguity from weather and daylight variation.
s1fL3aqi34.method: Motivated by a latent factor decomposition separating location content from viewpoint and appearance nuisances, ProbInfoNCE predicts query- and reference-dependent scales via a lightweight MLP to form a pair-specific contrastive temperature. The authors also construct CAV-Geo, a benchmark of 256K street-view locations and 440K satellite images augmented with FLUX-generated weather and illumination changes and a cross-continental split.
s1fL3aqi34.key_idea: Replace the global InfoNCE temperature with an additive pair-dependent scale predicted from query and reference embeddings to downweight ambiguous cross-view pairs during contrastive training.
s1fL3aqi34.evidence: Evaluated with DINOv3 initialization on VIGOR, CVUSA, CVACT, and the newly constructed 11-city CAV-Geo cross-continental benchmark with controlled temperature ablations.
s1fL3aqi34.claimed_gains: Improves R@1 over InfoNCE by 5.1% on VIGOR with the same DINOv3 initialization.
s1fL3aqi34.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ProbInfoNCE is lightweight and consistently improves Recall@1 across standard geo-localization benchmarks, and that CAV-Geo targets an underexplored appearance-variation gap.
s1fL3aqi34.main_concern: Sample-dependent contrastive temperatures are already well established in prior work, and CAV-Geo relies on FLUX-synthesized weather and daylight edits for both training and testing without isolating ProbInfoNCE on real weather shifts.

0MkDhexPax.one_liner: Regularizes online RL actors by estimated distance to a sampled union-of-balls approximation of a base policy's support
0MkDhexPax.problem: Behavioral-cloning regularizers force online RL actors to retain suboptimal modes of multimodal imitation base policies, whereas hard support constraints block beneficial actions just outside the prior support.
0MkDhexPax.method: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization (GSBR) approximates a pretrained diffusion or flow base policy's support as a union of balls around a finite batch of sampled base actions, requiring only black-box sample access. Actions inside the estimated support incur zero penalty while out-of-support actions receive a penalty growing smoothly with distance.
0MkDhexPax.key_idea: Approximate the pretrained base policy's support from finite action samples as a union of balls, applying zero penalty inside and a smooth distance-based penalty outside.
0MkDhexPax.evidence: Supported by a pointwise support-approximation bound and online RL experiments across 19 manipulation and control tasks spanning four robotic simulation benchmarks.
0MkDhexPax.claimed_gains: Raises the average success rate from 33% for the base policy to 95% across 19 tasks on four robotic benchmarks.
0MkDhexPax.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the zero-inside, smooth-outside support-distance regularizer intuitive, theoretically grounded via union-of-balls approximation, and effective across robotic benchmarks using only sample access.
0MkDhexPax.main_concern: Conditioning the actor on sampled base-policy action buffers adds inference-time sampling overhead untested on real hardware, starts the actor uninitialized, and suffers density bias in finite-sample ball estimation.

OdAytArL8j.one_liner: An early-denoised Thought stream of boxes and step prompts guides RGB video diffusion for embodied manipulation.
OdAytArL8j.problem: Video world models can produce plausible manipulation videos while choosing wrong objects, misordering subtasks, or using incorrect targets.
OdAytArL8j.method: Reasoning Canvas adds a Thought stream that renders object-following boxes and step-wise text on a black canvas alongside RGB generation. Timestep-Bias Reasoning Routing resolves this stream earlier, and the RoboCasa-derived HierCanvas dataset supplies hierarchical programs, boxes, and prompts.
OdAytArL8j.key_idea: A simplified spatial-temporal Thought canvas is denoised before RGB so subsequent pixel generation conditions on a more stable visual plan.
OdAytArL8j.evidence: Experiments assess visual quality, instruction alignment, tracking, ambiguous instructions, out-of-distribution compositions, and Thought-stream ablations.
OdAytArL8j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly generating a spatial-temporal plan before detailed RGB frames is useful and supported by encouraging empirical gains.
OdAytArL8j.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the Thought-generator design insufficiently justified relative to an LLM or VLM planner and broader embodied settings.

EStLDl52c7.one_liner: Incremental artificial consumers and wealth redistribution approximate aggregate demand under a revealed-preference learning framework.
EStLDl52c7.problem: Learning collective consumption from aggregate demand is difficult when strong individual-rationality assumptions and generalization guarantees are undesirable.
EStLDl52c7.method: Constructive Rationalization Method builds a surrogate market of artificial consumers with easy-to-compute demand functions. It adds consumers on the fly and redistributes wealth under empirical risk minimization, with an application to proportionally fair allocation approximation.
EStLDl52c7.key_idea: Incrementally adding artificial consumers and redistributing their wealth fits aggregate demand without recovering individual utilities.
EStLDl52c7.evidence: The paper provides generalization-risk guarantees and theoretical analysis of convergence, oracle complexity, approximation limits, and proportionally fair allocations.
EStLDl52c7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the surrogate-market construction is interesting and supported by careful problem-specific theoretical analysis.
EStLDl52c7.main_concern: The paper lacks theoretical or experimental comparisons with alternative aggregate-demand learning methods.

GR40fJzkSg.one_liner: Snapshot versions and scope watermarks let agents reject stale tool evidence and refresh state atomically.
GR40fJzkSg.problem: Asynchronous agents can mistake the latest-delivered tool result for the latest world state even when its snapshot predates subsequent changes.
GR40fJzkSg.method: Event-time reasoning attaches snapshot versions and scope watermarks to tool results for decision-time validation. Watermark combines exact version invalidation, query influence, and optional service cost, while atomic cuts prevent incompatible partial refreshes.
GR40fJzkSg.key_idea: Versioned snapshots and scope watermarks rank evidence by event-time validity and influence rather than tool-result arrival order.
GR40fJzkSg.evidence: Evaluation spans 97,200 controlled tasks, 747,600 paired outcomes, five seeds, unseen transition regimes, 265 commits from ten unseen repositories, and repeated OpenCode sessions on five models.
GR40fJzkSg.claimed_gains: A preregistered five-seed confirmation raises exact accuracy from 87.0% to 90.1% (+3.09 points [2.53,3.62]), retains a +4.15-point gain [3.68,4.61] under unseen regimes, and matches 96.50% accuracy while refreshing 48.7% fewer sources than full refresh.
GR40fJzkSg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that snapshot freshness is clearly distinguished from arrival order and that the protocol is practical, reusable, and rigorously evaluated.
GR40fJzkSg.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether influence scoring and its required metadata transfer beyond structured query families to open-ended agent decisions.

TreNQ0xS5A.one_liner: A shared autoregressive backbone unifies driving scene tokens, language, trajectories, and action-conditioned future generation.
TreNQ0xS5A.problem: Existing autonomous-driving systems often use separate visual representations for scene understanding and future generation.
TreNQ0xS5A.method: Doe-3 encodes synchronized multi-view observations with a pretrained driving world representation and processes scene, language, and action modalities through a shared autoregressive backbone. A diffusion head produces future scene latents, and three-stage joint training aligns the interface, backbone, and task objectives.
TreNQ0xS5A.key_idea: Shared autoregressive world tokens provide a common temporal context for language responses, trajectory planning, and action-conditioned future prediction.
TreNQ0xS5A.evidence: Experiments evaluate planning on NAVSIMv1 and NAVSIMv2, include nuScenes results, and use multi-task ablations to study language and future-generation supervision.
TreNQ0xS5A.claimed_gains: Doe-3 achieves a PDMS of 94.0 on NAVSIMv1 and an EPDMS of 90.8 on NAVSIMv2, outperforming the strongest prior methods.
TreNQ0xS5A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying scene understanding, planning, and generation is useful and supported by strong benchmark performance.
TreNQ0xS5A.main_concern: Reviewers most often find that the experiments do not establish how language and future prediction mechanistically improve planning beyond auxiliary supervision.

P4m0cat4Ec.one_liner: Safe-set covariance weighting combines partially labeled and unlabeled observations to suppress batch effects in PCA.
P4m0cat4Ec.problem: Batch effects can dominate leading principal components, while partial batch labels make their removal without discarding observations difficult.
P4m0cat4Ec.method: Weighted hybrid PCA uses a factor model with shared factor loadings and batch-specific intercepts, then combines covariance estimates from labeled and unlabeled observations. Observed labels select a weight from a safe set that excludes components induced by between-population variation.
P4m0cat4Ec.key_idea: Partial labels define a safe covariance-weight set that avoids batch-induced components while retaining information from unlabeled observations.
P4m0cat4Ec.evidence: Simulations compare safe-set and oracle weights, and two A549 single-cell RNA perturbation datasets with p53-related responses test common-structure recovery.
P4m0cat4Ec.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the procedure is simple and that its safe-set weighting and asymptotic analysis carefully address a practical problem.
P4m0cat4Ec.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the empirical evaluation too narrow, with limited external baselines and little coverage of small-label or misspecified settings.

OM8Gu9uXNq.one_liner: Ensemble-weighted inverse-folding scores select mutations that reshape protein conformational populations.
OM8Gu9uXNq.problem: Inverse-folding protein design does not constrain the equilibrium populations of accessible conformational states.
OM8Gu9uXNq.method: Ensemble-IF combines pretrained inverse-folding models with machine-learned conformational ensemble generation. It scores sequence-structure compatibility across sampled conformations to identify mutations that directionally reshape the conformational landscape.
OM8Gu9uXNq.key_idea: Sequence mutations are proposed from inverse-folding compatibility scores aggregated across generated conformations according to target population preferences.
OM8Gu9uXNq.evidence: Molecular-dynamics simulations on events defined from reference trajectories evaluate target-band distance error and structural integrity beyond the ensemble-generation screening model.
OM8Gu9uXNq.claimed_gains: Ensemble-IF achieves an over 90% reduction in mean target-band distance error relative to baselines while maintaining structural integrity.
OM8Gu9uXNq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that controlling equilibrium conformational populations is an important protein-design objective and that molecular-dynamics validation strengthens the evidence.
OM8Gu9uXNq.main_concern: Reviewers most often find comparisons insufficiently controlled for mutation counts and candidate-evaluation budgets.

HlpFERaw9o.one_liner: Decomposes VLM spatial reasoning into cognitive subquestions (CogVSR) and probes and intervenes on specialized attention heads.
HlpFERaw9o.problem: How large vision-language models internally organize and execute spatial reasoning across attention heads remains poorly understood.
HlpFERaw9o.method: The authors build CogVSR, a human-verified decomposition of spatial tasks into cognitive subquestions, train probes to locate specialized attention heads across VLM families, and test them via head masking, activation, and spatial-head disentanglement (SHA).
HlpFERaw9o.key_idea: Probes VLM attention heads using cognitive subquestion decompositions (CogVSR) and validates head roles via targeted ablation and activation interventions.
HlpFERaw9o.evidence: Evaluated across InternVL, Qwen-VL, and Llama-Vision families from 2B to 90B parameters using probing, head masking, and positive interventions.
HlpFERaw9o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CogVSR is a useful decomposed benchmark and that consistent sparsity of functional heads across 2B–90B VLM families is a credible finding.
HlpFERaw9o.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about probing selection bias (trained only on correct answers), lack of cross-function specificity controls, and potential information leakage from external Gemini2.5-Flash boxes in SHA.

IYZa7Wx1yb.one_liner: Trains an implicit recurrent sparse-coding denoiser via implicit differentiation and decomposes its Jacobian to link V1 circuits and diffusion.
IYZa7Wx1yb.problem: Standard black-box diffusion models lack circuit-level interpretability, leaving the mechanistic connection between denoising inference and primary visual cortex (V1) computations unclear.
IYZa7Wx1yb.method: The authors generalize sparse coding inference with learnable pairwise lateral interactions in an implicit recurrent network trained via implicit differentiation for image denoising, then decompose the denoising Jacobian to analyze learned orientation connectivity and contour completion.
IYZa7Wx1yb.key_idea: Models denoising as an implicit recurrent sparse-coding network with pairwise lateral couplings whose Jacobian decomposes into interpretable dictionary, interaction, and gating terms.
IYZa7Wx1yb.evidence: Trained on natural images for denoising and contour completion, analyzed via receptive-field orientation tuning and Jacobian spectral decomposition.
IYZa7Wx1yb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the analytical decomposition of the denoising Jacobian and the emergence of V1-like orientation-selective lateral connectivity without prespecification.
IYZa7Wx1yb.main_concern: Reviewers note hard-to-parse notation, a mismatch between the simplified single-scale analytical model and the multi-scale convolutional implementation, and limited transferability of insights to UNet/DiT diffusion models.

JRCs5DMSdV.one_liner: Pretrains an intracranial EEG encoder by predicting which persistent implanted electrode produced each channel waveform.
JRCs5DMSdV.problem: Existing iEEG foundation models adapt pretraining objectives from other modalities instead of leveraging the persistent physical identity of implanted electrodes.
JRCs5DMSdV.method: PUPPET trains a shallow encoder (one main Transformer block plus a local-context module) with an electrode-origin prediction objective that classifies which training electrode generated each waveform segment across varying neural activity.
JRCs5DMSdV.key_idea: Uses multi-class electrode-origin classification across time as a self-supervised pretraining target for persistent intracranial EEG contacts.
JRCs5DMSdV.evidence: Evaluated with frozen features and linear readouts on iMindBench and four additional public iEEG datasets (working memory, picture naming, attention, free recall) against ten baselines.
JRCs5DMSdV.claimed_gains: Reaches 0.661 Overall AUROC on iMindBench versus 0.645 for the prior leader, and matches the prior leader's mean using 10 minutes of recordings (0.41% duration) or 71k transferred parameters (0.36% size).
JRCs5DMSdV.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers praise the intuitive iEEG-specific objective and matched-control efficiency results, while one reviewer sees no strengths.
JRCs5DMSdV.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to prior channel-identification SSL work (e.g., PPi), note missing contrastive baselines, and point out that the 10-minute efficiency gain is within seed variance and matched by joint reconstruction.

DaYvZlXF7i.one_liner: Decouples domain-specific deterministic process verifiers from RL optimization to provide bounded step-level rewards alongside outcome rewards.
DaYvZlXF7i.problem: Outcome-only RL methods like GRPO cannot distinguish partially useful failed trajectories from unproductive ones over long reasoning horizons.
DaYvZlXF7i.method: The framework extracts intermediate reasoning artifacts from agent trajectories through a unified interface, scores them with domain-specific verifiers into bounded process rewards, and combines them with sparse outcome rewards in a two-stage post-training schedule.
DaYvZlXF7i.key_idea: Extracts intermediate trajectory artifacts into external domain verifiers to compute bounded process rewards decoupled from the RL optimizer.
DaYvZlXF7i.evidence: Evaluated across four domains (including HotpotQA), two model sizes (including 4B), and both GRPO and PPO.
DaYvZlXF7i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling deterministic process verification from RL optimization is practical and consistently improves over outcome-only GRPO and PPO.
DaYvZlXF7i.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments mostly test short 3–5 turn horizons without directly measuring stability, use single seeds, and omit comparisons with existing verifiable process-reward methods like VPR and VPRMs.

gGGjmjPJi4.one_liner: Converts 2D wildfire simulations into 3D-proxy-guided video episodes to build multimodal memory for training-free VLM reporting.
gGGjmjPJi4.problem: Effective wildfire monitoring needs visual evidence linked to physical fire dynamics, but real videos with synchronized physical annotations are scarce and 3D simulation is costly.
gGGjmjPJi4.method: A fixed Blender mapping turns 2D wildfire simulations into low-detail 3D proxies, which controllable video generation enriches into labeled episodes. These episodes form a reusable multimodal memory for a training-free multi-agent VLM system that retrieves references, reconciles visual and memory predictions, and writes structured reports.
gGGjmjPJi4.key_idea: Maps 2D wildfire simulations to 3D proxies and generated videos to populate a training-free multimodal retrieval memory for VLM reasoning.
gGGjmjPJi4.evidence: Evaluated on held-out generated episodes with component ablations, cross-generator tests, and three real-UAV monitoring evaluations.
gGGjmjPJi4.claimed_gains: Video memory achieves 51.5% exact four-tag accuracy versus 22.6% for direct VLM querying and 16-17% for text-only memory, while the complete system reaches 77.3% accuracy on six report fields.
gGGjmjPJi4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the simulation-to-video memory pipeline is practical, coherent, and yields solid gains on synthetic evaluation tasks.
gGGjmjPJi4.main_concern: Real-world UAV evaluations lack sufficient protocol details and test simpler perception tasks rather than proving physical-driver transfer from synthetic videos.

esu5y4lEiL.one_liner: Separates longitudinal patient history into outcome-relevant and environment subspaces for treatment-conditional counterfactual diffusion forecasting.
esu5y4lEiL.problem: EHR treatment practices and data collection vary across environments, entangling patient clinical state with setting-induced artifacts and making multi-step counterfactual forecasting unreliable.
esu5y4lEiL.method: DeCaf decomposes a patient's longitudinal history into an outcome-relevant latent subspace and an environment/nuisance subspace. It then pairs this representation with a treatment-conditional diffusion trajectory generator operating in the outcome-relevant subspace.
esu5y4lEiL.key_idea: Factorizes longitudinal EHR histories into outcome-relevant and environment-nuisance latent subspaces before rolling out treatment-conditional diffusion trajectories.
esu5y4lEiL.evidence: Evaluated against baselines across simulated tumor data, semi-synthetic MIMIC-III, and real MIMIC-IV clinical datasets with three random seeds and ablations.
esu5y4lEiL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating outcome-relevant and environment subspaces for longitudinal counterfactual generation is well-motivated and outperforms most tested baselines.
esu5y4lEiL.main_concern: The ablation design does not isolate the environment branch's causal contribution, and multi-step counterfactual evidence relies mainly on a simulator.

ZC6BNRIvl2.one_liner: Learns query-conditioned linear feature projections via quadruplet attention to explain outliers beyond axis-aligned subspaces.
ZC6BNRIvl2.problem: Axis-aligned feature subspace explanations fail to isolate many outliers from inliers under low dimensionality or practical cardinality budgets.
ZC6BNRIvl2.method: TMQ samples quadruplets consisting of the query, another outlier, a near inlier, and a far inlier, embeds them, and applies global attention to re-estimate query-specific weighted feature combinations.
ZC6BNRIvl2.key_idea: Re-estimates query-specific weighted feature projections from sampled outlier-inlier quadruplets using global attention instead of searching axis-aligned subspaces.
ZC6BNRIvl2.evidence: Enumerates coordinate subspaces across 47 ADBench Classical benchmarks (33,170 outliers) and evaluates TMQ with ablations and sensitivity analyses across dataset-detector pairs.
ZC6BNRIvl2.claimed_gains: Enumerating all subspaces leaves 94.9% of outliers unseparated for d<=6, 56.0% for 21<=d<=40 under |S|<=3, and 47.7% overall (16.7% at 99th-percentile).
ZC6BNRIvl2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the exhaustive subspace separability study clearly establishes a limitation of axis-aligned explanations and that the query-specific contrast formulation is promising.
ZC6BNRIvl2.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish fidelity to the underlying anomaly detector's decisions, and reported precision and F1 scores contain unresolved protocol discrepancies.

yr83U9d0C1.one_liner: Audits frozen verifier checkpoints before and after debate distillation using paraphrase counterexamples and sequential hypothesis testing.
yr83U9d0C1.problem: Debate distillation can preserve monitored-task accuracy while degrading a verifier's support for correct answers on related unmonitored hidden tasks.
yr83U9d0C1.method: ER-AUDIT is a two-stage black-box auditing framework that compares frozen pre- and post-adaptation verifier checkpoints by first searching semantic paraphrases for counterexamples and then running sequential hypothesis testing with anytime-valid lower confidence bounds.
yr83U9d0C1.key_idea: Compares pre- and post-distillation verifier checkpoints via paraphrase counterexample search followed by sequential testing with anytime-valid confidence bounds.
yr83U9d0C1.evidence: Evaluated on two newly introduced benchmarks pairing monitored and hidden task prompts with shared contexts, alongside theoretical confidence-bound derivations.
yr83U9d0C1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying hidden-task epistemic degradation in debate distillation and providing an anytime-valid black-box auditing framework are valuable contributions.
yr83U9d0C1.main_concern: The experiments do not clearly distinguish epistemic degradation from selective forgetting or prompt-phrasing sensitivity, and the monitored-to-hidden task relationship is insufficiently justified.

WNTHArc3s0.one_liner: Combines row-normalized E8 lattice quantization with tiled conditional entropy coding and fused GPU reconstruction for weight compression.
WNTHArc3s0.problem: Fixed-width weight quantization formats offer coarse storage choices, while entropy coding requires accurate rate selection and fast weight reconstruction during inference.
WNTHArc3s0.method: EntroPack applies row-normalized E8 lattice quantization with a conditional probability model, selects quantization resolution via sampled storage estimates, and entropy-codes coordinates into independently decodable tiles for fused GPU reconstruction.
WNTHArc3s0.key_idea: Pairs row-normalized E8 lattice quantization with sampled rate selection and independently decodable entropy-coded tiles for fused GPU reconstruction.
WNTHArc3s0.evidence: Evaluated on diffusion and language models including Z-Image-Turbo, measuring weight error, image fidelity, WikiText-2 perplexity, and conversion speed.
WNTHArc3s0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that EntroPack is clearly motivated and achieves a practical calibration-free compression-accuracy trade-off with fast model conversion.
WNTHArc3s0.main_concern: Downstream quality evaluation is too thin (two image prompts and mostly WikiText-2 perplexity), and ablations do not isolate gains across the stacked components.

Z0yfBNwcds.one_liner: Maintains a single Frequent Directions sketch of curvature geometry to perform one-pass generalized linear bandit updates and action selection.
Z0yfBNwcds.problem: Online mirror descent for generalized linear bandits relies on dense curvature matrices that require O(d^2) memory and O(d^3) per-round computation.
Z0yfBNwcds.method: SGLB applies Frequent Directions to incrementally compress the adaptively revealed curvature matrix into a size-m sketch, using that single sketch for both estimator updates and optimistic action selection.
Z0yfBNwcds.key_idea: Uses a single Frequent Directions sketch of curvature geometry for both one-pass mirror descent updates and optimistic action selection.
Z0yfBNwcds.evidence: Supported by regret bounds quantifying the spectral-tail penalty and experiments on synthetic logistic/Poisson bandits plus MNIST, Covertype, MFeat, and W8A datasets.
Z0yfBNwcds.claimed_gains: Reduces memory from O(d^2) to O(md) and, for small candidate action sets, amortized per-round computation from O(d^3) to O(md) for sketch size m<d.
Z0yfBNwcds.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that integrating Frequent Directions into GLB-OMD addresses a real computational bottleneck with explicit spectral-tail regret guarantees and empirical trade-offs.
Z0yfBNwcds.main_concern: The O(md) fast-projection derivation contains mathematical gaps when shrinkage is nonzero, and favorable regret relies on an unguaranteed small spectral-tail condition.

v6NPLqdZiA.one_liner: Compresses cross-layer transcoders via latent mixing to build attribution graphs and test reasoning features by causal intervention.
v6NPLqdZiA.problem: Direct cross-layer transcoders require massive decoders, and how their sparse features causally drive multi-step chain-of-thought reasoning remains unclear.
v6NPLqdZiA.method: The authors introduce a latent-mixing transcoder that shrinks decoder size, then construct direct-effect and multi-hop attribution graphs on Gemma-3-4B-IT. They select recurring candidate features across AIME reasoning traces and perform causal interventions, identifying a sentence-boundary continuation feature.
v6NPLqdZiA.key_idea: A parameter-efficient latent-mixing cross-layer transcoder generates attribution graph hypotheses whose causal roles in reasoning are tested via feature interventions.
v6NPLqdZiA.evidence: Experiments evaluate decoder compression and reconstruction on Gemma-3-4B-IT across five evaluation sets, case-study attribution graphs, and six AIME prompt templates.
v6NPLqdZiA.claimed_gains: Reduces decoder parameters by 17.4x for Gemma-3-4B-IT while maintaining comparable reconstruction quality.
v6NPLqdZiA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the latent-mixing parameterization substantially reduces cross-layer transcoder size and that distinguishing attribution scores from intervention effects is valuable.
v6NPLqdZiA.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical validation is limited to a single model, two prompt examples, six AIME templates, and subjective single-feature analysis.

4eBhaKJLoE.one_liner: Formalizes machine unlearning under partial retained-data access via ambiguity sets and decomposes retain-forget risks into floors and tradeoffs.
4eBhaKJLoE.problem: Unlearning algorithms often lack full access to the retained dataset, creating fundamental ambiguity about the retraining oracle that prior efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs ignore.
4eBhaKJLoE.method: The paper models partial information (original model, forget set, local Hessian, and retained subset) through feasible dataset ambiguity sets and defines retain-set excess risk and forget-set unlearning risk. For least-squares regression and a two-layer ReLU example, it decomposes both risks into algorithm-dependent fitting terms and algorithm-independent ambiguity floors.
4eBhaKJLoE.key_idea: Modeling partial retained-data knowledge as feasible dataset ambiguity sets decomposes unlearning risk into algorithm-independent ambiguity floors and a Pareto fitting tradeoff.
4eBhaKJLoE.evidence: Theoretical risk decompositions, lower bounds on a two-layer ReLU construction, and regression analyses support the claims without real-data experiments.
4eBhaKJLoE.claimed_gains: Shows that both ambiguity floors scale as Omega(k) where k is the forget-set size in a two-layer ReLU example.
4eBhaKJLoE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that characterizing fundamental unlearning limits under partial information is an interesting theoretical direction.
4eBhaKJLoE.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of real-data unlearning experiments, doubts about the practicality of the partial-information assumptions, and organizational or notational flaws.

SBDxMjBKdp.one_liner: Constructs an expert-annotated multi-source benchmark of 751 chemical reactions to evaluate LLMs, forward models, and classifiers.
SBDxMjBKdp.problem: Evaluating chemical reaction feasibility verifiers is hindered by scarce negative data and noisy proxies from zero-yield records or synthetic perturbations.
SBDxMjBKdp.method: The authors curate FREA, a 751-reaction benchmark annotated by expert chemists across four sources: retrosynthesis proposals, zero-yield experimental records, LLM perturbations, and five generation methods, alongside a 14M+ reaction corpus. They benchmark frontier LLMs, forward models, and learned classifiers on feasibility verification and model ranking.
SBDxMjBKdp.key_idea: Evaluating verifiers against expert-annotated reactions spanning four distinct positive and negative sources reveals source-specific failure modes missed by proxy labels.
SBDxMjBKdp.evidence: Experiments benchmark frontier LLMs, forward models, and learned classifiers on the 751 expert-labeled reactions and exploratory training on the 14M+ corpus.
SBDxMjBKdp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that FREA addresses an important gap in reaction feasibility verification and demonstrates that proxy negative sources carry substantial label noise.
SBDxMjBKdp.main_concern: Reviewers highlight moderate inter-annotator agreement (kappa = 0.55) due to unspecified reaction conditions and small minority-class sample sizes within individual sources.

mHMoQqidy6.one_liner: Replaces step-size-tuned gradient guidance with annealed backward-backward proximal splitting on the diffusion prior and condition loss.
mHMoQqidy6.problem: Training-free diffusion guidance methods require task-specific step-size tuning because loss smoothness is unknown when using pretrained networks.
mHMoQqidy6.method: ABBS formulates conditional sampling as noise-level subproblems solved by composing an approximate proximal step on the prior (one reverse diffusion step with derived schedule scale) and an inexact proximal step on the condition loss via inner Adam iterations.
mHMoQqidy6.key_idea: Composing a reverse diffusion step as a scaled prior proximal map with an inexact condition proximal step eliminates outer guidance step-size tuning.
mHMoQqidy6.evidence: Theoretical approximation error bounds and experiments on four image restoration/style tasks and controllable motion generation.
mHMoQqidy6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the proximal-splitting formulation cleanly connects sampling to condition optimization across diverse image and motion tasks.
mHMoQqidy6.main_concern: Reviewers note strong similarity to DiffPIR (differing mainly by a scaling factor c_t) and ask whether tuning simply shifted to the inner Adam learning rate and iteration count K.

PkhjH8qk2s.one_liner: Extends rotated matrix normalization optimizers to the fixed-rank LoRA manifold using thin-factor Riemannian operations.
PkhjH8qk2s.problem: Full-parameter matrix optimizers with rotation and normalization do not directly respect the gauge symmetry of low-rank LoRA factorizations.
PkhjH8qk2s.method: The paper interprets matrix optimizers as normalization in a rotated basis and implements Riemannian gradients, momentum transport, rotation, normalization, and retraction entirely in thin low-rank factors without materializing full matrices.
PkhjH8qk2s.key_idea: Performing rotated-basis normalization, tangent projection, and retraction directly in thin factors brings matrix optimizers to the fixed-rank LoRA manifold.
PkhjH8qk2s.evidence: Experiments evaluate mathematical reasoning and code generation under SFT and GRPO RL across multiple model families and sizes.
PkhjH8qk2s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that keeping all manifold, rotation, and normalization operations in thin factors is well-motivated and preserves LoRA memory efficiency.
PkhjH8qk2s.main_concern: Reviewers highlight an inconsistency between the row/column normalization objective in Eq. (16) and Algorithm 3, plus SFT downstream gains falling within seed variance.

u2GQ4lKlBF.one_liner: Couples a content-centric graph and a user-context graph via aligned anchors in DG-Mem for multi-user agent memory retrieval.
u2GQ4lKlBF.problem: Single-user agent memory systems conflate coexisting user states and miss cross-user evidence or asker-dependent relevance in shared multi-user histories.
u2GQ4lKlBF.method: The authors propose DG-Mem, an LLM-free dual-graph memory framework linking a content-centric graph (semantic, conversational, temporal edges) and a user-context graph (authorship, role, channel, phase, topic, reply edges) through aligned message anchors, followed by asker- and query-conditioned retrieval and refinement.
u2GQ4lKlBF.key_idea: Separating content relations from speaker-grounded user-context relations across aligned message anchors enables asker-conditioned retrieval over shared multi-user histories.
u2GQ4lKlBF.evidence: Evaluations on GroupMemBench (multi-user) and LoCoMo (single-user) across multiple answer models with component ablations.
u2GQ4lKlBF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multi-user agent memory is an important, underexplored problem and find the dual-graph design intuitive with promising empirical gains.
u2GQ4lKlBF.main_concern: Reviewers note unfair reliance on synthetic metadata fields (phase, topic, role) unavailable to official baselines, unclear necessity of two separate graphs over one heterogeneous graph, and evaluation/budget discrepancies.

oOFndOXCUT.one_liner: Fixes candidate responses and re-scores tokens under channel-wise evidence perturbations to detect and correct omni-modal hallucinations.
oOFndOXCUT.problem: Existing inference-time hallucination mitigation methods rarely reveal which modality evidence sustains each generated commitment.
oOFndOXCUT.method: OmniConfess freezes a candidate response and re-scores it token-by-token under controlled channel-wise evidence interventions to build a token-by-channel confession. It uses this attribution against channel-relevance rules to keep grounded tokens and revise ungrounded commitments without training.
oOFndOXCUT.key_idea: Freezes candidate responses and re-scores tokens under channel-wise evidence ablations to attribute evidential dependence and revise ungrounded tokens.
oOFndOXCUT.evidence: Evaluations on the newly constructed 3,540-example OmniGroundBench spanning text, image, audio, and video tasks in judgment and free-form generation.
oOFndOXCUT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that freezing the candidate response cleanly avoids decode-trajectory confounds and that the training-free design spans multiple modalities.
oOFndOXCUT.main_concern: Reviewers note missing specification of channel-relevance rules and judge/hyperparameter details, additive attribution ignoring cross-modal interactions, and lack of faithfulness validation for confessions.

ahoGrUAYPO.one_liner: Models a shared LLM advisor in the volunteer's dilemma to show when wider adoption narrows the social welfare gap.
ahoGrUAYPO.problem: It is unclear how the social welfare cost of an LLM optimizing only its users' payoffs changes as more players adopt the advisor.
ahoGrUAYPO.method: The authors analyze a volunteer's dilemma where a shared LLM advisor learns from user feedback while non-users follow no-regret learning, proving convergence and characterizing the welfare gap between selfish and selfless objectives across adoption levels.
ahoGrUAYPO.key_idea: Models coupled no-regret player dynamics and advisor learning in the volunteer's dilemma to characterize the welfare gap as an inverted-U function of adoption.
ahoGrUAYPO.evidence: Convergence and welfare-gap theorems alongside Qwen3 8B experiments comparing empirical action probabilities to theoretical predictions.
ahoGrUAYPO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mixed-population externality framing insightful and the convergence analysis solid.
ahoGrUAYPO.main_concern: Reviewers note that the welfare-gap theorem is restricted to type-1 policies, experiments vary SFT anchors rather than directly optimizing user vs. social welfare, and notation is dense.

EUgc49SV2C.one_liner: Trains outcome-supervised neural barrier functions to adaptively steer chain-of-thought activations toward correct final answers.
EUgc49SV2C.problem: Chain-of-thought activation steering typically relies on heuristic contrastive directions without step-level reachability feedback.
EUgc49SV2C.method: GuardSTR formulates CoT reasoning as finite-horizon stochastic reachability, trains a scalar neural barrier function from outcome-labeled trajectories, and uses its gradient to adaptively scale activation steering at each reasoning step without fine-tuning the LLM.
EUgc49SV2C.key_idea: Models CoT as stochastic reachability and uses gradients of an outcome-trained neural barrier function to adaptively steer latent reasoning states.
EUgc49SV2C.evidence: Evaluations across four LLMs and seven tasks from BBH and MMLU against unsteered baselines, Static CAA, and K-CAST.
EUgc49SV2C.claimed_gains: GuardSTR improves accuracy over unsteered baselines on all 28 model-task pairs with a macro-average gain of 5.91 percentage points, and maximum gains of 12.8 and 11.6 points over Static CAA and K-CAST.
EUgc49SV2C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the stochastic-reachability framing is novel and empirical gains across 28 model-task pairs are consistent.
EUgc49SV2C.main_concern: All reviewers identify a mathematical flaw in Proposition 1, where the proof assumes positive barrier drift after the stopped process terminates.

SGbCODJ3Pu.one_liner: Coordinates LLM-driven model searches across related tasks and scales via shared experimental evidence and subset-to-full promotion screening.
SGbCODJ3Pu.problem: LLM-driven model evolution struggles to transfer discoveries across related tasks and becomes prohibitively expensive when full-scale training is costly.
SGbCODJ3Pu.method: Population Evolution (PE) links parallel local searches by replaying and sharing code-change evaluations across related task instances to inform new proposals. For expensive targets, PE searches on small subsets and screens candidates through peer and intermediate checks before promoting them to full-target training.
SGbCODJ3Pu.key_idea: Links parallel LLM-driven searches by sharing cross-instance code evaluations and screening subset discoveries via peer checks before full-scale promotion.
SGbCODJ3Pu.evidence: Evaluated on the introduced RMD-Bench across ranking, watch-time prediction, RL algorithm discovery, and LLM/VLM pretraining under matched iterations and GPU-hours.
SGbCODJ3Pu.claimed_gains: Raises average best-design gain across ranking datasets from 7.01% to 8.97% over standalone evolution at matched source iterations.
SGbCODJ3Pu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree sharing executable discoveries across tasks and screening subset candidates for expensive targets is a practical, broad direction.
SGbCODJ3Pu.main_concern: Reviewers note Track B fails to isolate cross-task collaboration from subset screening, missing comparisons to evolutionary multitask baselines (e.g., EMO-STA), single-run evaluations, and dense benchmark presentation.

SkIpzhHcBb.one_liner: Introduces CastScriptBench and token-routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation supervising speaker tags and utterance text separately.
SkIpzhHcBb.problem: Multilingual audio-visual captioning lacks difficulty-stratified benchmarks beyond English/Chinese and optimizes speaker attribution and transcription under one coarse objective.
SkIpzhHcBb.method: CastScriptBench spans 508 videos across 13 languages with 8 scene/acoustic attributes and an edit-distance plus checklist protocol. CastScript adapts multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) by routing per-token distribution matching within each sequence: an attribution expert supervises speaker-tag tokens while a transcription expert supervises utterance text tokens.
SkIpzhHcBb.key_idea: Routes per-token on-policy distillation within a single sequence to separate speaker-attribution and transcription teacher experts.
SkIpzhHcBb.evidence: Evaluated on CastScriptBench (508 videos, 13 languages, 4,236 utterances, 1,218 speakers) with ablations across SFT, experts, mix-RL, and routed/unrouted MOPD.
SkIpzhHcBb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multilingual benchmark and attribute annotations are practical, and token-type routing between attribution and transcription experts is intuitive.
SkIpzhHcBb.main_concern: Reviewers note the joint Acc metric confounds attribution with transcription, single-run margins over experts/unrouted MOPD are tiny (0.006-0.017) without seeds, and novelty is incremental.

qHWAxYtOkp.one_liner: Adapts a frozen video generator for zero-shot restoration via dual visual conditioning and frequency-gated data consistency.
qHWAxYtOkp.problem: Applying frozen pretrained video generators to low-level restoration tasks without fine-tuning often retains input degradations or alters scene content.
qHWAxYtOkp.method: Gen4LV conditions a frozen video generator on both the degraded video (for motion and layout) and a single restored frame (for appearance), combined with frequency-gated data consistency.
qHWAxYtOkp.key_idea: Decouple motion and appearance conditioning using the degraded video plus one restored frame, and apply frequency-gated data consistency to preserve structure.
qHWAxYtOkp.evidence: Evaluations span eight benchmarks across blind video super-resolution, colorization, archival film restoration, and AI-generated video restoration.
qHWAxYtOkp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that one frozen generator handles four restoration tasks with clear ablations showing why both conditioning references and frequency gating are needed.
qHWAxYtOkp.main_concern: Reviewers highlight low pixel-level fidelity (e.g., low PSNR on UDM10), dependence on external models like Nano Banana Pro, and small 10-clip evaluations.

T4I5nd5qHf.one_liner: Trains an executable-harness proposer at test time via policy gradients while keeping the solver LLM frozen.
T4I5nd5qHf.problem: Improving language-model scientific discovery under finite search budgets typically updates the solver weights or relies on static search procedures.
T4I5nd5qHf.method: HarnessTTT trains a harness proposer using RLOO with gap-normalized rewards and max-sharpening to generate prompts, skills, tools, middleware, and controls for a frozen executor.
T4I5nd5qHf.key_idea: Optimize a proposer policy with RLOO over budgeted rollout outcomes to emit validated executable harnesses for a frozen executor.
T4I5nd5qHf.evidence: Evaluations cover 13 scientific discovery tasks across mathematics, systems, heuristic programming, astrodynamics, and biology using 9B and 27B frozen executors.
T4I5nd5qHf.claimed_gains: HarnessTTT with a frozen 9B executor improves on OpenEvolve with the same executor on all eleven benchmark tasks (e.g., from 1.17 to 2.635 on circle packing), improves on the discovery-fine-tuned Finch-9B by up to 92%, holds the best open-weight sub-10B result on nine, and reaches 0.380919 on Erdős minimum overlap, better than the best human reference of 0.380927.
T4I5nd5qHf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation between a trainable proposer and a frozen executor well-motivated and the empirical results across discovery tasks competitive.
T4I5nd5qHf.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over Meta-Harness, Harness-R1, and RLPrompt, missing compute-matched comparisons, and incomplete RL component ablations.

rd7cTsr2iI.one_liner: Weights exogenous variables per forecast step using channel and temporal utility scores over a residual forecasting pathway.
rd7cTsr2iI.problem: Existing time-series interaction strategies do not specify how exogenous variable usefulness should be weighted differently at each future prediction step.
rd7cTsr2iI.method: SCEU builds an endogenous-only base forecast, computes Channel Utility scores for exogenous variable-scale representations and Temporal Utility from historical patches, and fuses them through a gated bounded residual pathway.
rd7cTsr2iI.key_idea: Compute step-conditioned Channel and Temporal Utility scores to modulate exogenous representations added via a bounded residual pathway onto an endogenous base forecast.
rd7cTsr2iI.evidence: Experiments span 13 real-world time-series forecasting benchmarks and ablation studies on the utility branches.
rd7cTsr2iI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the step-conditioned exogenous utility problem is well motivated and the 13-dataset evaluation is broad.
rd7cTsr2iI.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations remove entire branches rather than testing matched-capacity horizon-invariant weights, leaving the step-conditioning claim unisolated.

W7Pi7omZu9.one_liner: Consolidates historical layerwise curvature matrices with Riemannian discrepancy and checkpoint anchoring for replay-free continual LLM quantization.
W7Pi7omZu9.problem: Continual post-training quantization on new domains degrades LLM accuracy on earlier domains when historical calibration data cannot be replayed.
W7Pi7omZu9.method: ARCH-CPTQ maintains one fixed-dimensional curvature matrix per layer, weights poorly reconstructed units, balances current and historical curvature via a Riemannian discrepancy, and anchors updates to the previous quantized checkpoint.
W7Pi7omZu9.key_idea: Represent historical reconstruction losses as a fixed-size per-layer curvature matrix and anchor quantized weight updates along historically sensitive directions.
W7Pi7omZu9.evidence: Evaluations test six LLMs across five precision settings against CPTQ-AVG and GPTQ under matched solver settings.
W7Pi7omZu9.claimed_gains: ARCH-CPTQ achieves a 2.16-percentage-point average performance (AP) gain over CPTQ-AVG in the main W2A16 setting.
W7Pi7omZu9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the formalization of replay-free continual PTQ and the exact collapse of weighted historical losses into a fixed-size curvature matrix.
W7Pi7omZu9.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the practical memory trade-off, noting that storing curvature matrices and the FP16 reference model takes gigabytes compared to megabytes for raw replay tokens.

FnT1urzlSH.one_liner: Tests how sign-masking gradient deviations stored in AdamW's first moment affects associative recall and language-model loss.
FnT1urzlSH.problem: One-step gradient covariance analyses overlook how noise stored in AdamW's first moment aligns with future mini-batch draws across updates.
FnT1urzlSH.method: The authors decompose sampled gradients into mean and deviation components in associative recall and apply complementary sign masks to stored deviations with matched conditional covariance.
FnT1urzlSH.key_idea: Apply complementary sign masks to gradient deviations entering AdamW's momentum buffer to isolate temporal noise alignment from one-step covariance.
FnT1urzlSH.evidence: Experiments use synthetic associative recall runs and small language models trained on every token position.
FnT1urzlSH.claimed_gains: When the mask reversed most coordinate groups, 18 of 24 runs learned recall within the training budget, compared with 5 of 24 under the complementary mask.
FnT1urzlSH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of how stored momentum noise affects recall learning interesting and the matched-covariance sign-mask setup clever.
FnT1urzlSH.main_concern: Reviewers are concerned that the setup is overly toy and constrained, with weak or unclear generalization to realistic language modeling.

7ezxQ00iGD.one_liner: Uses causal interventions on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to show number comparison relies on linear directions and local MLP intervals despite curved manifolds.
7ezxQ00iGD.problem: Observing curved representation manifolds like helices does not establish whether or how LLMs actually use that geometry during computation.
7ezxQ00iGD.method: The authors apply activation patching and causal interventions to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on 2- and 3-number comparison tasks, tracing how attention transports linear number vectors into a shared residual space where MLP neurons compare local number intervals.
7ezxQ00iGD.key_idea: Demonstrates via causal patching that Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct compares numbers using transported linear directions and interval-selective MLP neurons rather than curved manifolds.
7ezxQ00iGD.evidence: Causal intervention and activation patching experiments on 2- and 3-number comparison prompts in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
7ezxQ00iGD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the paper's core insight that geometric manifolds do not equate to causal computation and appreciate the coherent end-to-end circuit analysis.
7ezxQ00iGD.main_concern: Reviewers criticize evaluating only one model and fixed prompt templates, incomplete behavioral metrics (first-digit IIA), and unclear discovery of intervention vectors.

QOw3Z4bNoc.one_liner: Speeds up CFG-constrained diffusion language model decoding using lexing memoization, regular-cover parallel commit, and Earley validation.
QOw3Z4bNoc.problem: Prior context-free grammar (CFG) constrained decoding for diffusion language models is up to 4x slower than unconstrained decoding due to sequential validity checking.
QOw3Z4bNoc.method: EPIC accelerates exact CFG-constrained diffusion decoding via three optimizations: memoizing lexer states, selecting compatible token subsets for parallel commit using a regular-language over-approximation, and performing exact validation with an Earley-style graph parser instead of deterministic automata.
QOw3Z4bNoc.key_idea: Combines lexer memoization, regular-cover filtering for parallel token commits, and DFA-free Earley graph parsing to preserve exact CFG validity at near-unconstrained speed.
QOw3Z4bNoc.evidence: Evaluated on three benchmarks across four diffusion language models with component ablations.
QOw3Z4bNoc.claimed_gains: Brings runtime close to unconstrained levels (versus up to 4x slower for prior CFG-constrained decoding) while maintaining comparable syntactic and functional correctness.
QOw3Z4bNoc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that EPIC addresses a real inference bottleneck and achieves substantial speedups without relaxing the baseline's exact CFG validity criterion.
QOw3Z4bNoc.main_concern: Reviewers view the work as engineering/combining classical parsing techniques (memoization, regular covers, Earley parsing) and note the regular cover's benefit over simple batch splitting is not isolated.

mfl5FVIhsF.one_liner: Documents how longer interaction histories erode LLM cooperation in repeated social dilemmas and tests memory compression and LoRA.
mfl5FVIhsF.problem: Expanding an LLM agent's accessible interaction history is assumed to improve capability, yet can degrade cooperation in repeated social dilemmas.
mfl5FVIhsF.method: The authors evaluate 7 LLMs across 4 repeated games up to 500 rounds, analyze rationales and transition frequencies, and test interventions including rationale-only LoRA, compact/summary/retrieval memory views, and removing explicit CoT.
mfl5FVIhsF.key_idea: Demonstrates history-length-induced cooperation decay across repeated games and mitigates it via compact history views, CoT removal, or rationale-only LoRA.
mfl5FVIhsF.evidence: Evaluations across 7 LLMs and 4 social dilemmas up to 500 rounds, blinded evaluation of 2,016 rationales, and Mistral-7B interventions.
mfl5FVIhsF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the large-scale empirical study across models and games and the conditional transition analysis showing P(D|D) rises with longer histories.
mfl5FVIhsF.main_concern: Interventions are tested under inconsistent protocols mostly on Mistral-7B without direct comparison, and lower cooperation after defection may reflect rational adaptation rather than a dysfunction.

fU8sbiSSpE.one_liner: Encodes stepwise task, observation, and action text with multi-prefix supervision to estimate LLM agent success.
fU8sbiSSpE.problem: Existing agent confidence estimators rely on token probabilities, hand-crafted features, or post-execution signals, failing to capture environment interactions or enable early prediction.
fU8sbiSSpE.method: STEP encodes the task, observation, and action text at each execution step, models the resulting sequence temporally, and trains with multi-prefix supervision to predict task success during and after execution.
fU8sbiSSpE.key_idea: Applies temporal modeling over raw stepwise task, observation, and action text embeddings with multi-prefix supervision for online success prediction.
fU8sbiSSpE.evidence: Experiments on ScienceWorld, WebShop, and InterCode Bash under within-task and length-matched evaluation protocols.
fU8sbiSSpE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies evaluation shortcuts around task difficulty and trajectory length and provides comprehensive within-task experiments.
fU8sbiSSpE.main_concern: Reviewers question cross-agent and cross-environment generalization since STEP is retrained per environment and agent, and note missing downstream intervention experiments.

kysCZDskvT.one_liner: Compiles semantic wearable event streams into fixed-kilobyte typed RAM state using query-loss allocation for MCU execution.
kysCZDskvT.problem: Long-horizon wearable assistants on kilobyte-SRAM microcontrollers either lose joint spatio-temporal conditions with decoupled counters or exceed memory limits with raw logs and note stores.
kysCZDskvT.method: uWM maintains entity-grouped joint action, place, and temporal supports in fixed RAM, allocating precision at write time via answer-aware query-loss tradeoffs among demotion, merging, and deletion. Deterministic on-device readers answer structured queries directly and route open-ended requests via resolved entity-time anchors.
kysCZDskvT.key_idea: Maintains entity-grouped joint action-place-time state under a strict kilobyte cap via answer-aware query-loss compaction and deterministic on-device readers.
kysCZDskvT.evidence: Evaluated across 14 query families on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 under a 16.00 KiB cap, on AMB, and profiled on microcontroller hardware.
kysCZDskvT.claimed_gains: Reaches 88.10% deterministic reader accuracy on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 under a 16.00 KiB cap (13.38 KiB mean checkpoint), retains 86.9%-87.7% of unbounded baselines using 122.6x-500.6x more storage, and recovers 99.1% raw-log fidelity on AMB.
kysCZDskvT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical MCU implementation, byte-level accounting, and joint spatio-temporal representation for conditional queries.
kysCZDskvT.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about overclaiming in AMB and full-store comparisons and note that adaptive query-loss allocation does not clearly outperform fixed-precision variants.
