CjtoAFJcUU.one_liner: Benchmarks six graph foundation models against 15 tuned supervised GNNs across 51 node classification datasets with cost tracking.
CjtoAFJcUU.problem: It remains unclear whether graph foundation models deliver consistent predictive gains over tuned dataset-specific GNNs at practical computational costs.
CjtoAFJcUU.method: NodeArena establishes a unified transductive node classification benchmark with shared random splits, multiple metrics, controlled hyperparameter tuning, and runtime cost accounting across 51 datasets, comparing six GFMs and 15 supervised methods.
CjtoAFJcUU.key_idea: Evaluates graph foundation models against hyperparameter-tuned supervised GNNs under shared transductive splits and explicit training/adaptation cost accounting.
CjtoAFJcUU.evidence: Experiments across 51 node classification datasets comparing six GFMs and 15 supervised baselines.
CjtoAFJcUU.claimed_gains: Tuned GNNs remain strongest overall, while GraphPFN reaches third in Elo ranking under the label-rich split.
CjtoAFJcUU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the thorough, controlled evaluation of both predictive accuracy and computational cost across many datasets and tuned baselines.
CjtoAFJcUU.main_concern: Reviewers point out the lack of inductive, few-shot, or distribution-shift evaluations, as well as questionable real-world utility of many included classic graph datasets.

Pg1iNYmDKw.one_liner: Audits whether runtime agent evolution preserves safety and utility using paired source-target tasks and matched cold-vs-evolved controls.
Pg1iNYmDKw.problem: Static single-task evaluations cannot test whether runtime agent evolution (memory, skills, prompt revision) degrades safety or utility on subsequent tasks.
Pg1iNYmDKw.method: EvoAudit constructs directed source-target task pairs across benign and dangerous settings, comparing cold and evolved agents across five models and seven evolution mechanisms, plus controlled good/bad memory injections.
Pg1iNYmDKw.key_idea: Evaluates agent evolution-readiness via directed source-target task pairs scored jointly on safety and utility under matched cold and evolved conditions.
Pg1iNYmDKw.evidence: Controlled experiments across five models and seven evolution mechanisms on synthetic task pairs with rubric scoring.
Pg1iNYmDKw.claimed_gains: When both tasks are dangerous, evolution doubles the rate at which agents trade off utility for safety.
Pg1iNYmDKw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important, underexplored safety-utility trade-off in self-evolving agents.
Pg1iNYmDKw.main_concern: Reviewers note high baseline run-to-run variation (34.1%), reliance on unvalidated synthetic tasks and LLM rubrics without human checks, and single-step evolution scope.

rxPWc7mo7b.one_liner: Accelerates full-duplex spoken dialog by predicting multiple future frames via rolling masked diffusion and revising only unplayed divergence.
rxPWc7mo7b.problem: Fine-grained full-duplex spoken dialog models advance their backbone autoregressively at every interaction frame, creating high sequential compute.
rxPWc7mo7b.method: DiffuPlex predicts multiple future user and assistant frames in one backbone wake via rolling masked diffusion and consumes a confident prefix (silence-only in LISTEN, speech-allowed in SPEAK). When incoming user audio diverges from predictions, it preserves already-played assistant frames and revises only the unplayed future.
rxPWc7mo7b.key_idea: Predicts multi-frame user-assistant futures in one backbone wake via rolling masked diffusion and revises only unplayed frames upon user divergence.
rxPWc7mo7b.evidence: Evaluated on full-duplex runtime benchmarks, concurrent-load latency, GPU energy, conversational behavior, and human speech-quality evaluations.
rxPWc7mo7b.claimed_gains: DiffuPlex-LISTEN and DiffuPlex-SPEAK achieve 1.46x and 1.59x deployment-path wall-clock speedups, 1.61x and 1.80x Core LM speedups, and 16.1% and 19.9% GPU energy reductions within 80ms intervals.
rxPWc7mo7b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the prediction-and-revision mechanism is an interesting way to reduce sequential inference cost in full-duplex spoken dialog.
rxPWc7mo7b.main_concern: Reviewers note a quality-speed trade-off (especially reduced speech naturalness in SPEAK), limited generalization to other dual-stream architectures, and extra LoRA/MASK training.

gN7Go7KzIi.one_liner: Computes unsupervised LLM activation steering paths as geodesics under an output-pullback Riemannian metric with data-support regularization.
gN7Go7KzIi.problem: Linear activation steering pushes representations off the model's natural activation manifold, while prior spline-based manifold steering requires labeled centroids and topology assumptions.
gN7Go7KzIi.method: Riemannian Manifold Steering (RMS) equips activation space with a Riemannian metric pulled back from the model's output distributions and optimizes geodesic paths regularized to stay near observed activations via k-NN support penalties. This finds unsupervised steering trajectories that avoid off-manifold drift.
gN7Go7KzIi.key_idea: Optimizes activation steering trajectories as geodesics under an output-distribution pullback metric combined with a k-NN data-support regularizer.
gN7Go7KzIi.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic curved surfaces with known geometry, toy LLM tasks, and preliminary real-world LLM steering tasks.
gN7Go7KzIi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric combination of pullback metric and data-support penalty is well-motivated and cleanly validated on synthetic surfaces.
gN7Go7KzIi.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about in-sample evaluation where test metrics mirror training loss, ad-hoc free-endpoint handling, and preliminary real-world LLM results requiring ground-truth prompts.

vGe6Szgyft.one_liner: Constructs a 9K-sample synthetic reasoning dataset spanning 8 scientific disciplines and 1K+ topics for SFT+RL post-training.
vGe6Szgyft.problem: Open-source reasoning datasets lack long CoT seed trajectories, skew heavily toward mathematics, and face human annotation bottlenecks on frontier tasks.
vGe6Szgyft.method: CHIMERA is a 9K-sample synthetic reasoning dataset generated via an automated pipeline using a model-generated hierarchical taxonomy across 8 scientific disciplines and over 1K topics, paired with long CoT trajectories synthesized by reasoning models and cross-model verification for SFT+RL post-training.
vGe6Szgyft.key_idea: Synthesizes a 9K-sample multi-discipline CoT dataset via hierarchical topic taxonomy expansion, problem generation, and cross-model verification.
vGe6Szgyft.evidence: Evaluated by post-training models (including 4B models) on hard reasoning benchmarks such as GPQA Diamond and HLE, compared against an OpenThoughts subset.
vGe6Szgyft.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the broad scientific topic coverage (8 disciplines, 1,179 topics) and empirical gains for small models are practically useful.
vGe6Szgyft.main_concern: Reviewers find the pipeline lacks methodological novelty over existing curation/distillation works (s1, LIMO), note unclear SFT training budgets, and question the small marginal gain of topic diversity over math-only training.

Q61i0x3vFI.one_liner: Organizes LoRA updates into shared, generation-private, and editing-private subspaces modulated by property and source controllers.
Q61i0x3vFI.problem: Jointly fine-tuning an LLM for de novo molecular generation and molecular editing causes negative transfer that degrades editing performance.
Q61i0x3vFI.method: MOSA adapts a frozen language model by partitioning low-rank updates into shared, generation-private, and editing-private subspaces. A permutation-invariant property controller modulates the shared subspace using individual properties and pairwise interactions, while a source controller combines the input molecule and target properties to scale and shift editing updates.
Q61i0x3vFI.key_idea: Partitions LoRA updates into shared and task-private subspaces modulated by permutation-invariant property and source-molecule controllers.
Q61i0x3vFI.evidence: Evaluated on 6,000 common de novo generation requests and 5,000 molecular editing requests against SketchMol, single-task specialists, and joint LoRA.
Q61i0x3vFI.claimed_gains: Achieves 60.45% strict de novo success (vs. SketchMol's 54.5%) and 76.98% strict editing success at 39,500 updates, avoiding negative transfer at matched exposure.
Q61i0x3vFI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of editing-side negative transfer and the shared/private subspace design with property controllers are well-motivated with encouraging results.
Q61i0x3vFI.main_concern: Reviewers note missing confidence intervals across runs, simple SMILES-computable target properties, missing multi-task LoRA baselines, and unquantified train/test overlap.

8pehk4uecP.one_liner: Analyzes rank-induced approximation floors in epsilon- and v-prediction diffusion and adds a time-dependent input shortcut c(t)x_t.
8pehk4uecP.problem: Although x-, epsilon-, and v-prediction define the same optimal score, epsilon- and v-prediction often perform much worse in practice under limited output capacity.
8pehk4uecP.method: The authors show that noise and velocity targets inherit ambient-space components from noisy inputs that create approximation floors under limited output rank for low-dimensional data, and add a time-dependent shortcut c(t)x_t so the network predicts only the scaled clean signal.
8pehk4uecP.key_idea: Adds a time-dependent input shortcut c(t)x_t to carry the ambient noisy-input component, removing rank-limited ambient approximation floors in epsilon- and v-prediction.
8pehk4uecP.evidence: Supported by subspace/manifold approximation floor theorems, controlled synthetic experiments, and an ImageNet 256x256 experiment with JiT-B/16.
8pehk4uecP.claimed_gains: On ImageNet 256x256 with JiT-B/16, the shortcut reduces v-prediction FID from 96.53 to 7.83, compared with 8.62 for x-prediction.
8pehk4uecP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric characterization cleanly formalizes the discrepancy between x-, epsilon-, and v-prediction targets and leads to a simple modification.
8pehk4uecP.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch between theory and experiments—JiT-B/16 has no output-head rank bottleneck yet still fails under direct v-prediction—along with close similarity to JiT's x-prediction and minimal ablations.

7MtazYoYpC.one_liner: Converts psychological tasks into interactive environments and evaluates LLM-agent trajectory human-likeness with a learned human-policy model.
7MtazYoYpC.problem: Text-transcribed static psychological prompts miss closed-loop action–observation dynamics in LLM agents, while dynamic agent benchmarks rarely assess human-likeness.
7MtazYoYpC.method: mini-psych-agent transforms 25 psychological tasks into closed-loop interactive environments and scores agent behavioral trajectories using the average log-likelihood under a GRU human-policy model fitted to human data.
7MtazYoYpC.key_idea: Evaluates autonomous LLM agents in closed-loop interactive psychological environments by scoring their generated trajectories with a learned GRU human-policy likelihood model.
7MtazYoYpC.evidence: Supported by closed-loop evaluations across a 25-task psychological suite comparing models, memory strategies, and agentic scaffolds with matched seeds.
7MtazYoYpC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree closed-loop interactive psychological evaluation across 25 tasks is well motivated and captures behavioral dynamics missed by static replay.
7MtazYoYpC.main_concern: Reviewers unanimously warn that average log-likelihood under the human-policy model rewards repetitive high-probability actions over genuine human behavioral variability, and note unvalidated text interfaces and few seeds.

sAIPWZiSIs.one_liner: Benchmarks multi-agent LLM workflows by executing fixed candidate–task pairs across varying serving substrates and arrival load regimes.
sAIPWZiSIs.problem: Multi-agent workflow latency and quality rankings can flip across serving hardware, engines, and load regimes even with identical models and prompts.
sAIPWZiSIs.method: MASSys replays fixed candidate–task pairs across serving substrates and arrival rates over five workload families, recording task quality alongside completion, latency, cost, resource pressure, and runtime traces.
sAIPWZiSIs.key_idea: Treats the serving substrate and load regime as explicit experimental variables by replaying identical multi-agent candidate–task pairs while logging paired task and service traces.
sAIPWZiSIs.evidence: Supported by a controlled KV-cache motivation diagnostic and substrate sweeps across five workload families (software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control, diagram generation).
sAIPWZiSIs.claimed_gains: In the KV-cache diagnostic, the Star workflow falls from first to fourth in mean-latency rank while Chain rises from fourth to first.
sAIPWZiSIs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree treating the serving substrate as an explicit evaluation variable and separating evaluated-only quality from effective delivery quality is well motivated.
sAIPWZiSIs.main_concern: Reviewers stress that each substrate cell uses only a single run (n = 1) with no confidence intervals, hardware regimes confound model sets, and some completion/timeout figures appear inconsistent.

cQOT7zd2tr.one_liner: Trains a geometry-conditioned autoregressive second-quantized neural quantum state using orbital alignment to predict wavefunctions at unseen geometries.
cQOT7zd2tr.problem: Second-quantized neural-network quantum states require expensive per-geometry optimization because orbital identities and phases change discontinuously across molecular geometries.
cQOT7zd2tr.method: The authors align orbital identities and transport their phases across geometries to build a consistent occupation basis, then train a single geometry-conditioned autoregressive wavefunction model on sparse anchor geometries for zero-shot evaluation at query geometries.
cQOT7zd2tr.key_idea: Matches orbital identities and transports orbital phases across molecular geometries so a single geometry-conditioned autoregressive NQS can generalize across potential energy surfaces without retraining.
cQOT7zd2tr.evidence: Supported by variational Monte Carlo experiments on N2, CO, H4, and Li2Se potential energy surfaces, orbital-alignment ablations over three seeds, and observable predictions.
cQOT7zd2tr.claimed_gains: Orbital alignment reduces N2 query-geometry energy MAE from 34–37 mHa to 0.049–0.085 mHa, and frozen evaluation reduces per-geometry cost by 986x (25.8x estimated end-to-end GPU-cost reduction on a 161-point N2 grid) at ~1 mHa MAE.
cQOT7zd2tr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three-seed orbital-alignment ablation cleanly demonstrates that consistent orbital identities and phases are critical for sharing second-quantized wavefunctions across geometries.
cQOT7zd2tr.main_concern: Reviewers note missing direct comparisons against eigenvector continuation, PESNet, and warm-start baselines, limited ML novelty beyond known quantum-chemistry alignment, and restriction to small 1D molecular scans.

wF3w7ENnMY.one_liner: Adapts a pretrained video world model with coupled kinematic supervision and sequence optimization for RGB-only egocentric motion reconstruction.
wF3w7ENnMY.problem: Reconstructing full-body human motion from egocentric RGB video alone requires inferring largely unseen limbs without ground-truth camera trajectories.
wF3w7ENnMY.method: HumanWM adapts a pretrained video world model's action interface to jointly model egocentric video and structured human actions under Coupled Kinematic Supervision (constraining spatial structure and acceleration), followed by full-sequence inference optimization with rotational and root-dynamics regularization.
wF3w7ENnMY.key_idea: Repurposes a pretrained video world model's action modality to jointly generate egocentric video and human kinematics with coupled spatial-acceleration supervision and sequence-level regularization.
wF3w7ENnMY.evidence: Supported by experiments on 3,000 sequences from 57 Nymeria test recordings comparing RGB-only and task-text configurations against baselines including ReViV.
wF3w7ENnMY.claimed_gains: Compared with RGB-only ReViV, RGB-only HumanWM reduces GA-MPJPE by 38.2% and PA-MPJPE by 44.9%; adding task text yields 78.10 mm GA-MPJPE, 46.49 mm PA-MPJPE, and 0.216 m final root trajectory error.
wF3w7ENnMY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree adapting a pretrained video world model's action interface for RGB-only egocentric motion reconstruction is a clean framing with large error reductions over ReViV.
wF3w7ENnMY.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that all evaluation is confined to a single dataset (Nymeria), leaving cross-dataset generalization and the specific benefit of world-model pretraining over standard video encoders untested.

NfH0v1QPFQ.one_liner: Replaces manual trust hyperparameters in constrained RL with an automatic lower-confidence-bound step size to mitigate phantom cost overestimation.
NfH0v1QPFQ.problem: Cost critics in constrained RL can overestimate costs in underexplored states ('phantom costs'), while EM-style safety surrogates rely on brittle manually tuned step-size hyperparameters.
NfH0v1QPFQ.method: ILB-CRL formulates an off-policy EM-style incremental safety update whose trust coefficient alpha is computed automatically from a lower confidence bound on optimal safety improvement using a critic ensemble.
NfH0v1QPFQ.key_idea: Computes the constrained-RL safety-update trust coefficient automatically from a lower confidence bound on optimal safety improvement rather than a fixed hyperparameter.
NfH0v1QPFQ.evidence: Supported by a geometric convergence proof under stated assumptions and off-policy constrained RL experiments across multiple continuous-control tasks.
NfH0v1QPFQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well organized, clearly motivates self-reinforcing cost overestimation, and achieves competitive task returns within cost limits.
NfH0v1QPFQ.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments never directly test phantom-cost correction, compare off-policy ILB-CRL primarily against on-policy OmniSafe baselines with extra components (RETRACE, PopArt, budget state), and show weak ablation support for adaptive alpha.

k0I8pcHO1i.one_liner: Embeds agent populations via kernel mean embeddings and cylindrical kernel functionals for zero-shot population-size transfer in MARL.
k0I8pcHO1i.problem: First-moment mean-field RL discards distributional structure among agents, degrading multi-agent policies when deployment population size differs from training.
k0I8pcHO1i.method: SKARL represents empirical populations as kernel mean embeddings and individual values as cylindrical kernel functionals, deriving a Nystrom-projected RKHS Riesz gradient for scalable learning across variable population sizes.
k0I8pcHO1i.key_idea: Represents population states with kernel mean embeddings and agent values with cylindrical kernel functionals updated via a Nystrom-projected RKHS Riesz gradient.
k0I8pcHO1i.evidence: Supported by density and O(sqrt(|N-M|/(NM))) finite-sample sensitivity bounds plus variable-size transfer experiments on MPE, MAgent2, and PettingZoo.
k0I8pcHO1i.claimed_gains: In MAgent2 pursuit (trained at N=11, tested up to M=500), SKARL improves per-agent return by 15–17% over first-moment MFRL; in combined arms (N=120), it retains positive mean return from M=18 to M=450.
k0I8pcHO1i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the kernel mean-embedding representation is principled beyond first-moment mean-field summaries and shows strong large-scale zero-shot transfer on MAgent2.
k0I8pcHO1i.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing key baselines (M3ARL, DeepSets), unisolated component ablations (first-order correction and RKHS-preconditioned updates), and unclear decentralized execution with neighbor-action-dependent Q-functions.

enKDGOuzZ9.one_liner: Locates a jailbreak-resilient intermediate anchor layer via layer-wise probes to steer downstream layers and guide decoding.
enKDGOuzZ9.problem: Inference-time jailbreak defenses typically rely on external filters or auxiliary models while overlooking internal hidden layers that retain safety separability even under successful jailbreaks.
enKDGOuzZ9.method: SelfShield uses a layer-wise probe network to identify the intermediate anchor layer where safety discrimination peaks before degrading, adaptively injects steering vectors into subsequent layers, and leverages the anchor-layer token distribution during decoding.
enKDGOuzZ9.key_idea: Detect the safety-resilient intermediate anchor layer via layer-wise probes, steer downstream layers to prevent safety degradation, and guide generation with the anchor-layer token distribution.
enKDGOuzZ9.evidence: Evaluations test SelfShield across three LLM backbones and multiple jailbreak attacks while measuring both defense success rate and benign-request compliance.
enKDGOuzZ9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the model-intrinsic defense framing and clear evaluation of both jailbreak defense and benign-task utility across multiple models and attacks.
enKDGOuzZ9.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the anchor-layer selection lacks causal validation and calibration controls, the main defense metric conflates refusal with harmlessness, and closely related hidden-state safety literature is omitted.

wmAj59AjNE.one_liner: Selects nested binary interaction moment dictionaries via information geometry to recover product-Bernoulli mixtures by constrained moment matching.
wmAj59AjNE.problem: Unsupervised representation learning maps discrete data into latent coordinates that are hard to relate to observable statistical dependencies.
wmAj59AjNE.method: ODIN uses an information-geometric criterion to construct a nested hierarchy of binary interaction atoms, lifts discrete data into this explicit moment space, and recovers product-Bernoulli mixture parameters via constrained moment matching with a Jacobian full-rank local identifiability certificate.
wmAj59AjNE.key_idea: Select a nested hierarchy of binary co-activation moments via information geometry and estimate product-Bernoulli mixtures by constrained moment matching with Jacobian-rank identifiability checks.
wmAj59AjNE.evidence: Theoretical identifiability analysis is paired with synthetic mixture parameter recovery experiments and real-world discrete clustering benchmarks.
wmAj59AjNE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear separation between dictionary selection and local identifiability, transparent reporting of limitations, and explicit co-activation coordinates.
wmAj59AjNE.main_concern: Reviewers argue that component interpretability comes from the fitted Bernoulli mixture (which standard EM also yields) rather than ODIN, and note insufficient positioning against classical CP tensor decomposition identifiability results and random dictionaries.

l06ZB2czBv.one_liner: Adapts weight-tied recursive refinement to multivariate time-series classification using a convolutional tokenizer, single-state loop, and pooled readout.
l06ZB2czBv.problem: Adapting weight-tied recursive neural architectures to many-to-one multivariate time-series classification requires suitable temporal tokenization and latent-state organization.
l06ZB2czBv.method: The Recursive Time-Series Model (RTSM) pairs a learned convolutional temporal tokenizer (with gated depthwise and dense dilated Conv1D) with single-state weight-tied recursive refinement and a pooled sequence classification readout.
l06ZB2czBv.key_idea: Encode multivariate time series with a convolutional temporal tokenizer, refine a single shared latent state with weight-tied recursion, and pool for classification.
l06ZB2czBv.evidence: Evaluations span all 30 UEA multivariate time-series datasets over three seeds against deep-learning baselines, alongside tokenizer, state-organization, and single-pass ablations.
l06ZB2czBv.claimed_gains: Across all 30 UEA datasets and three seeds, RTSM achieves 72.62% mean accuracy, while a separately trained single-pass variant reaches 72.47% versus 68.27% for tokenizer-only classification.
l06ZB2czBv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean adaptation of TRM-style architectures to time-series classification, the convolutional tokenizer design, and validation-based reevaluation across all 30 UEA datasets.
l06ZB2czBv.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that the paper fails to show that recursion itself drives the gains—single-pass models nearly match full RTSM (72.47% vs. 72.62%) and most improvement comes from the tokenizer—while code and split details are missing.

BQ3b4yblxt.one_liner: Replaces LiRA's shadow-model ensemble with mid-training checkpoints from a single trajectory for per-sample membership inference.
BQ3b4yblxt.problem: Population-based membership inference attacks can yield inverted signals on vulnerable memorized samples, while per-sample attacks like LiRA require training dozens to hundreds of shadow models.
BQ3b4yblxt.method: The authors introduce a vulnerability-stratified evaluation protocol and propose Ghost-LiRA, which treats intermediate checkpoints from the target model's training trajectory as OUT-model proxies to build a temporal ensemble for per-sample membership scoring.
BQ3b4yblxt.key_idea: Substitute LiRA's spatial shadow-model ensemble with a temporal ensemble of mid-training target-model checkpoints that approximate exclusion of late-memorized vulnerable samples.
BQ3b4yblxt.evidence: Experiments evaluate Ghost-LiRA under vulnerability-stratified protocols across multiple datasets and model architectures.
BQ3b4yblxt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing inverted signals on vulnerable samples via vulnerability-stratified evaluation is meaningful and that leveraging late-stage memorization for cheap per-sample MIA is compelling.
BQ3b4yblxt.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the strong, less practical threat-model assumption that intermediate target-model checkpoints are available to the attacker, question whether correlated checkpoints trained on the sample are valid OUT proxies, and note overlap with TrajectoryMIA and SeqMIA.

VK1feRpb0M.one_liner: Probes cache-to-cache LLM communication with zeroed caches and logit decomposition, showing gains stem from question-independent output calibration.
VK1feRpb0M.problem: Cache-to-cache (C2C) communication is credited with transferring question-specific semantics via KV caches between heterogeneous LLMs, but its actual mechanism has not been causally verified.
VK1feRpb0M.method: Using released C2C weights and protocols, the authors run four controlled probes: sender-only answer tests, replacing sender KV caches with zeros, decomposing induced logit shifts into constant versus question-dependent terms, and scaling/centering receiver output distributions.
VK1feRpb0M.key_idea: Zero out the sender KV cache and decompose receiver logit shifts into question-independent and question-dependent components to test whether C2C performs semantic transfer or output calibration.
VK1feRpb0M.evidence: Controlled experiments evaluate released C2C checkpoints across receiver scales and task-trained fusers.
VK1feRpb0M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the zero-cache and logit-shift decomposition probes provide strong mechanistic evidence that output-bias calibration explains the released C2C checkpoint gains.
VK1feRpb0M.main_concern: Reviewers note that the main bias-correction finding is concentrated on a single degenerate 0.6B receiver, limiting generality across larger receivers, and cite partial overlap with prior causal audits of relayed KV caches.

4DnF1faD6W.one_liner: Amortizes sampling-based MPC by learning a cost-conditioned population-attention flow that iteratively transports candidate action sequences toward lower cost.
4DnF1faD6W.problem: Sampling-based trajectory optimizers use hand-crafted updates that ignore cross-instance structure, while direct generative policies do not iteratively optimize actions through a predictive model.
4DnF1faD6W.method: FlowOpt Policy casts MPC as a learned transport step grounded in Wasserstein gradient flow, using self-supervised flow matching on higher-budget optimizer improvements to train a population-attention flow that iteratively shifts candidate action ensembles conditioned on rollout costs.
4DnF1faD6W.key_idea: Iteratively transport a population of candidate action sequences toward lower cost using a cost-conditioned population-attention flow trained via self-supervised flow matching.
4DnF1faD6W.evidence: Supported by a Wasserstein gradient-flow derivation showing MPPI/CEM as special cases, and experiments on CarNav, HalfCheetah, Walker, Push-T, Cheetah-WM, and Humanoid-WM.
4DnF1faD6W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing online action optimization as cost-conditioned ensemble transport unifying MPPI/CEM is conceptually clear and backed by comprehensive task comparisons.
4DnF1faD6W.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons against existing learned feedback-conditioned MPC optimizers (e.g., DMPO), limited novelty of transport-based control, stale costs held fixed across Euler steps, and incomplete component ablations.

JadfZVJabx.one_liner: Optimizes non-truthful neural auctions as a multi-follower Stackelberg game using a fully first-order bilevel hypergradient algorithm.
JadfZVJabx.problem: Learning revenue-maximizing non-truthful auctions is difficult because strategic bidders' equilibrium strategies co-evolve with the auction mechanism.
JadfZVJabx.method: The authors formulate non-truthful auction design as a multi-follower Stackelberg game and develop a fully first-order bilevel algorithm using an auxiliary game to approximate hypergradients without second-order Jacobians.
JadfZVJabx.key_idea: Solve multi-follower Stackelberg non-truthful auction design via a fully first-order auxiliary-game hypergradient estimator with non-asymptotic convergence guarantees.
JadfZVJabx.evidence: Supported by convergence proofs under smoothness and strong monotonicity plus experiments on symmetric/asymmetric single-item and multi-item auctions.
JadfZVJabx.claimed_gains: Reaches an O(epsilon)-stationary point in tilde-O(epsilon^-2) first-order oracle calls while converging faster and scaling better with bidder count than second- and zeroth-order baselines.
JadfZVJabx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that applying fully first-order multi-follower bilevel optimization to non-truthful neural auction design is a natural, theoretically grounded direction.
JadfZVJabx.main_concern: Reviewers note that single-item experiments already have known Myerson optima while multi-item results trail GemNet, that equilibrium-tracking claims and strong-monotonicity assumptions exceed proof/implementation conditions, and that first-order motivation over second-order methods is underexplained.

0o3Yu6bv9u.one_liner: Cryptographically binds palimpsestic memorization fingerprints to public developer commitments to enable verifiable, contestable open-weight model ownership proofs.
0o3Yu6bv9u.problem: Existing model fingerprinting methods detect embedded signals but do not let a developer publicly prove ownership or contest omitted lineage after third-party fine-tuning.
0o3Yu6bv9u.method: The authors introduce a cryptographic framework binding model fingerprints to developer identity and public lineage commitments, instantiate it with palimpsestic memorization in a Python library, and evaluate robustness against linear-programming adversarial fine-tuning.
0o3Yu6bv9u.key_idea: Cryptographically commit palimpsestic memorization fingerprints to a developer's public lineage chronology to enable third-party verifiable ownership and lineage challenges.
0o3Yu6bv9u.evidence: Evaluated under LP-based adversarial fine-tuning across six open-weight models from three families (OLMo, Pythia, and CrystalCoder).
0o3Yu6bv9u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that publicly verifiable contestable ownership proofs combining chronological commitments with palimpsestic memorization address an important open-weight attribution problem.
0o3Yu6bv9u.main_concern: Reviewers question the first-order linearized attack model (which ignores utility preservation and nonlinear adaptive fine-tuning), unspecified reference-model sensitivity, and missing theoretical collision/forgery guarantees for palimpsestic fingerprints.

XDkU3dheTL.one_liner: Selects parent molecules for oracle evaluation by combining the mean and dispersion of surrogate-predicted rewards across sampled offspring.
XDkU3dheTL.problem: Parent-conditioned molecular search often ranks parents by their own observed rewards, which may not reflect their capacity to generate multiple high-reward offspring under tight oracle budgets.
XDkU3dheTL.method: Generator Disagreement Acquisition (GDA) samples offspring from each candidate parent, computes the mean and dispersion (generator disagreement) of their surrogate-predicted rewards to prioritize parents for oracle evaluation, and updates both the surrogate and parent pool in a closed loop.
XDkU3dheTL.key_idea: Score parent molecules by the mean plus dispersion of surrogate-predicted rewards across their sampled offspring rather than parent reward or predictor ensemble uncertainty.
XDkU3dheTL.evidence: Evaluated with random-forest ensembles across six tasks from DOCKSTRING and GEAM (512 initial labeled molecules, 800 oracle queries, five seeds) and ablations.
XDkU3dheTL.claimed_gains: With random-forest ensembles, GDA reaches 100 top-1% hits in all five seeds across all six tasks with lower mean oracle burden than each tested external baseline reaching that count.
XDkU3dheTL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating parents via predicted offspring reward distributions is clearly motivated and well suited to multi-candidate molecular discovery.
XDkU3dheTL.main_concern: Reviewers note missing simple baselines (predicted offspring max or top-k mean), inconsistent benefits of the dispersion term over c=0 ablations, confounded memory updates, limited recent external baselines, and overlap with plant-breeding offspring-variance methods.

e9N2thoTOd.one_liner: Replaces First-Explore's bespoke transformer training with PPO, GRU backbones, and adaptive exploration stopping for sample-efficient meta-RL.
e9N2thoTOd.problem: First-Explore handles high-cost exploration via partitioned explore/exploit modes, but relies on a bespoke, sample-inefficient training procedure and fixed exploration horizon.
e9N2thoTOd.method: First-Explore+ (FE+) replaces First-Explore's custom procedure with standard PPO over a GRU policy, adds exploit-context injection and an auxiliary return critic, and introduces an adaptive criterion to switch from exploration to exploitation without validation tuning.
e9N2thoTOd.key_idea: Train decoupled explore/exploit in-context meta-RL policies with standard PPO, GRU backbones, exploit-context injection, and an adaptive mode-switching criterion.
e9N2thoTOd.evidence: Evaluated across 10 seeds on deceptive meta-RL benchmarks including Deceptive XLand-MiniGrid against First-Explore, RL^2, and E-RL^2.
e9N2thoTOd.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds First-Explore using orders of magnitude fewer training samples and achieves high scores on Deceptive XLand-MiniGrid where RL^2 and E-RL^2 fail.
e9N2thoTOd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that FE+ simplifies First-Explore, eliminates post-hoc validation tuning of the exploration episode count, and demonstrates adaptive mode switching.
e9N2thoTOd.main_concern: Reviewers find novelty too incremental over First-Explore, note poor self-contained presentation, and criticize the narrow evaluation on simple low-dimensional environments against outdated baselines.

77cznAkMrh.one_liner: Selectively recomputes query-relevant video KV caches at query time so streaming video-LLMs can use shorter idle-time prefill windows.
77cznAkMrh.problem: Streaming video-LLMs prefill frames with restricted context windows before queries arrive, causing context mismatch with eventual queries while still incurring high idle prefill cost.
77cznAkMrh.method: FrameBlend is a training-free plug-and-play module that re-prefills selected video tokens with query-relevant context at query time and replaces their cached KVs, allowing shorter idle-time attention windows without retraining.
77cznAkMrh.key_idea: Re-prefill selected query-relevant video tokens at query time and replace their cached KVs, enabling shorter idle-time prefill attention windows.
77cznAkMrh.evidence: Evaluated across three SVU frameworks (ReKV, LiveVLM, HERMES) and five streaming and offline benchmarks (including OVO-Bench, RVS-Ego, RVS-Movie, MLVU) on Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
77cznAkMrh.claimed_gains: Achieves accuracy gains of up to 3.9 percentage points across five benchmarks and reduces per-frame prefill FLOPs by over 20% and total processing time by 14–59% on RVS-Ego for retrieval-based frameworks.
77cznAkMrh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that FrameBlend is a simple, training-free plug-and-play fix for prefill-query context mismatch that lets shorter idle windows outperform defaults.
77cznAkMrh.main_concern: Reviewers note that prefill window sizes are tuned per framework and benchmark without a described validation split (risking test-set tuning), that many gains are small without uncertainty estimates, and that query-time recomputation increases TTFT without solving long-term KV growth.

lVZXO1TPN8.one_liner: Automates ML data engineering for fixed algorithms using a tree-structured search over data branches, shared external data pool, and cumulative memory.
lVZXO1TPN8.problem: Data engineering—discovering external datasets, cleaning, selecting, and transforming data—remains manual and ad hoc despite standardized model architectures and training recipes.
lVZXO1TPN8.method: DataMaster optimizes only the data side for a fixed learning algorithm using three components: a DataTree organizing branching data-engineering refinements, a shared Data Pool for reusing discovered external sources, and a Global Memory storing node outcomes, artifacts, and reusable findings.
lVZXO1TPN8.key_idea: Combine tree-structured data-branch refinement, a shared discovered-dataset pool, and cumulative global memory to separate cheap data discovery from expensive training validation.
lVZXO1TPN8.evidence: Evaluated on classical ML tasks (including MLE-Bench Lite) and LLM post-training (including GPQA) with component ablations and data-leakage audits.
lVZXO1TPN8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that autonomous data-side optimization is a practical problem and that separating cheap shareable discovery from expensive downstream scoring is a sensible design.
lVZXO1TPN8.main_concern: Reviewers point out that all headline numbers come from single runs with demonstrated >=10 pp variance exceeding reported margins, alongside limited novelty over tree-search memory agents and unclear UCB scheduling.

lgJdqZ4S40.one_liner: Trains a single weight-conditioned LLM policy via offline geometric-mean self-distillation for multi-objective alignment.
lgJdqZ4S40.problem: Existing multi-objective alignment methods require costly online training, multiple explicit reward models, or heuristic parameter merging with weak trade-off guarantees.
lgJdqZ4S40.method: SteerDPO derives the optimal policy for any preference weight as a normalized weighted geometric mean of single-objective optimal policies under KL-regularized linear scalarization. It uses this identity to train a single preference-conditioned policy from per-objective pairwise preference data via offline self-distillation without explicit reward models.
lgJdqZ4S40.key_idea: Distills a single weight-conditioned policy from normalized weighted geometric means of learned one-hot optimal policies using offline pairwise preference data.
lgJdqZ4S40.evidence: Evaluated on two- and three-objective synthetic bandits and LLM alignment experiments with Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen3-8B measuring reward quality, steering, and front geometry.
lgJdqZ4S40.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the first-principles closed-form derivation and the practical single-stage offline self-distillation framework that avoids explicit reward models.
lgJdqZ4S40.main_concern: Reviewers note missing baselines such as COS-DPO, overlap with prior geometric-mean policy-composition results, oracle-versus-proxy evaluation discrepancies, and no evaluation on unseen preference weights.

Q8E2NaWalI.one_liner: Identifies an Evidence Anchoring Boundary in MLLMs and routes visual counterfactual interventions selectively by question type.
Q8E2NaWalI.problem: Training-free visual interventions for hallucination mitigation lose leverage at deeper layers and can degrade correct answers depending on the question.
Q8E2NaWalI.method: The authors apply RMS-matched visual-residual edits across decoder layers to locate the Evidence Anchoring Boundary (EAB) where visual intervention effects drop sharply. They then compare counterfactual subtraction across presence, attribute, and relation questions and build calibrated selective routing that intervenes only when calibration supports it for the question type.
Q8E2NaWalI.key_idea: Measures RMS-matched layer-wise visual-residual edits to locate the Evidence Anchoring Boundary and routes counterfactual subtraction selectively by calibrated question type.
Q8E2NaWalI.evidence: Evaluated across six MLLM checkpoints from three model families with calibration and disjoint held-out evaluation queries across presence, attribute, and relation questions.
Q8E2NaWalI.claimed_gains: Held-out intervention effects before EAB are 13.78x–26.10x larger than after it, and calibrated selective routing improves full-set attribute accuracy by 1.56–1.81 points.
Q8E2NaWalI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the layer-wise EAB analysis with RMS-matched controls, held-out calibration validation, and question-type breakdown informative.
Q8E2NaWalI.main_concern: Reviewers point out underspecified details for extracting and removing visual residual contributions and question the robustness of the 10% EAB threshold calibrated on 48 queries.

QPcTrTzyue.one_liner: Distills step-aligned privileged teacher distributions from fixed demonstrations for rollout-free LLM reasoning post-training.
QPcTrTzyue.problem: On-policy post-training improves LLM reasoning but incurs heavy rollout generation costs, while standard supervised fine-tuning on fixed demonstrations gives weak continuation supervision.
QPcTrTzyue.method: Step-Aligned Privileged Distillation (SAPD) aligns each reasoning step in a fixed reference demonstration with targeted privileged context from the known solution progression. A teacher conditioned on this step-aligned context produces distributional supervision for the student without generating rollouts.
QPcTrTzyue.key_idea: Conditions a teacher on each reasoning step's local reference progression to provide step-aligned distributional supervision from fixed demonstrations without rollouts.
QPcTrTzyue.evidence: Evaluated on mathematical reasoning benchmarks including AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25, plus out-of-domain coding preservation and training-loop efficiency comparisons against SFT, label smoothing, GRPO, and OPSD.
QPcTrTzyue.claimed_gains: Achieves approximately 2x training-loop speedups over on-policy baselines while outperforming SFT and label smoothing on average and remaining competitive with on-policy RL and self-distillation.
QPcTrTzyue.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the simple, intuitive step-aligned supervision design, clear ablations against full-solution and misaligned guidance, and rollout-free efficiency.
QPcTrTzyue.main_concern: Reviewers question modest accuracy gains without multi-seed statistical validation, checkpoint selection on evaluation benchmarks, and mismatched training sequence lengths against OPSD.

9OfRnmHk5H.one_liner: ZeroCode constructs error-correcting parity-check matrices edge-by-edge from the all-zero matrix using action-masked PPO.
9OfRnmHk5H.problem: Error-correcting code applications impose diverse structural constraints on parity-check matrices that existing code-design methods cannot unify on demand.
9OfRnmHk5H.method: ZeroCode formulates parity-check matrix construction as sequential edge selection starting from an all-zero matrix, trained with discrete PPO and action masking to enforce constraints like max degree, 4-cycle-free graphs, and quasi-cyclic structure while producing a library of edge-count trade-offs in one rollout.
9OfRnmHk5H.key_idea: Builds parity-check matrices edge-by-edge from the all-zero matrix using discrete PPO with action masking to enforce structural code constraints.
9OfRnmHk5H.evidence: Evaluated on belief-propagation decoding BER across four short (n, n/2) block-code lengths against RL (DDPG), genetic, differentiable, and classical baselines with ablations.
9OfRnmHk5H.claimed_gains: Achieves approximately 1 dB gain over the prior RL-based construction method at a bit error rate of 10^-4 for the (32,16) code.
9OfRnmHk5H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the action-masked sequential edge construction from the all-zero matrix clean, flexible for enforcing structural constraints, and well-ablated.
9OfRnmHk5H.main_concern: Reviewers warn of potentially unfair search-budget comparisons against baselines, narrow evaluation scope (only four small (n, n/2) codes under BP decoding), and wasteful early BP reward evaluations on invalid matrices.

V8HsaKI8TZ.one_liner: ToDA pools frozen language models by letting each token attend across all its layer representations before a token graph aggregates them.
V8HsaKI8TZ.problem: Standard final-layer pooling methods for frozen language models fail on tasks requiring local composition and target-specific aggregation when global cues are removed.
V8HsaKI8TZ.method: The authors introduce a diagnostic suite of composition and target-specific aggregation tasks with balanced global cues, and propose Token-Depth Aggregation (ToDA), where each token attends over its own representations across all layers before a token graph combines the depth-fused tokens.
V8HsaKI8TZ.key_idea: Performs per-token self-attention across all frozen LM layers before applying a token graph to aggregate local compositional signals.
V8HsaKI8TZ.evidence: Evaluated across frozen encoder and decoder backbones on the proposed composition/aggregation suite plus standard GLUE, IMDB, and MTEB benchmarks.
V8HsaKI8TZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the carefully balanced diagnostic task suite (such as target-specific review aggregation) and the large, consistent improvements ToDA achieves on those tasks.
V8HsaKI8TZ.main_concern: Reviewers criticize unequal hyperparameter tuning budgets (32 configs for ToDA vs. 2 for most baselines on tuning-sensitive tasks), unacknowledged prior work on token-dependent layer weighting (SBERT-WK), and limited practical relevance of frozen-encoder classification.

PuPVjzFkZK.one_liner: FROST freezes a simulation-trained PDE forecaster and trains a conditional generative model over its real-measurement residuals for sim-to-real transfer.
PuPVjzFkZK.problem: Deterministic real-data fine-tuning of simulation-pretrained neural operators leaves structured forecast mismatches caused by unresolved physical dynamics and measurement noise.
PuPVjzFkZK.method: Frozen-Operator Stochastic Transport (FROST) keeps an upstream PDE forecaster frozen and learns the conditional distribution of its residuals from real measurements conditioned on observed history and the base forecast, correcting bias while modeling structured variability.
PuPVjzFkZK.key_idea: Freezes the upstream neural operator and learns a conditional stochastic residual transport model from real measurements to correct bias and capture variability.
PuPVjzFkZK.evidence: Evaluated across five RealPDEBench experimental systems (seen and held-out parameters) and six frozen backbones on cylinder and public foil datasets.
PuPVjzFkZK.claimed_gains: Reduces long-horizon ensemble-mean error by up to 61% and fair CRPS by up to 75% over fine-tuned FNO across five RealPDEBench systems.
PuPVjzFkZK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sim-to-real PDE adaptation is timely and praise the extensive real-world evaluation across five physical systems and multiple frozen backbones.
PuPVjzFkZK.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over existing generative residual correction for PDEs, weak probabilistic calibration evidence (K=4 ensembles, under-dispersion, worse CRPS than retrofitting on 3/5 systems), and weak support for simulation pretraining's value.

8mfSDUuN9P.one_liner: Slide&Prune jointly allocates singular components, attention heads, and FFN channels under a shared budget via two-stage global and sliding-window reconstruction.
8mfSDUuN9P.problem: Layer-wise top-k SVD truncation ignores cross-block error compounding across composed Transformer layers under aggressive LLM compression.
8mfSDUuN9P.method: Slide&Prune (S&P) runs a two-stage post-training pipeline (global allocation followed by sliding-window multi-block reconstruction) that jointly selects singular components, attention heads, and FFN channels under a shared parameter budget without updating pretrained weights or SVD factors.
8mfSDUuN9P.key_idea: Jointly selects SVD components, attention heads, and FFN channels under a single budget using global and sliding-window multi-block reconstruction with frozen weights.
8mfSDUuN9P.evidence: Evaluated across LLaMA, OPT, and Vicuna models (6.7B-30B) on WikiText-2 perplexity and comparisons against low-rank, structured pruning, and hybrid baselines.
8mfSDUuN9P.claimed_gains: On LLaMA-1-7B at a 0.4 compression ratio without weight updates, achieves 13.75 WikiText-2 perplexity versus 29.44 for the strongest evaluated baseline.
8mfSDUuN9P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-block joint allocation of low-rank components, heads, and channels well-motivated with strong perplexity gains over compared SVD baselines.
8mfSDUuN9P.main_concern: Reviewers cite overstated claims and omitted recent SVD/hybrid baselines (e.g., AA-SVD, MoDeGPT, LoRAP), heavy reliance on older LLaMA-1-7B for aggressive compression, missing ablations, and unmatched compute budgets.
